entries.name: Training for Senior Officer in Haryana State
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Training for Senior Officers in Haryana State
entries.purpose: The goal/objective of training is to develop a professional, impartial and efficient civil service that is responsive to the need of the citizens. In doing so, care will be taken to emphasize the development of proper ethics, commitment to work and empathy for the vulnerable sections such as differently abled, senior citizens, SCs, STs etc. The competency framework will be used to ensure that civil servants have the requisite knowledge, skills and attitude to effectively perform the functions they are entrusted with. The success of training will lie in actual improvement in the performance of civil servants. The objectives of the training can best be described in capacity building and enhancement of Human Capital through an integrated framework of knowledge, Skill and Attitude. Capacity Building in Government of Haryana shall strive to achieve the following objectives: i) Keeping up-to-date and enhancing professional knowledge and skills needed for better performance of individuals and organizations; ii) Promoting better understanding of professional requirements as well as sensitization towards the socio-economic and political environment in which government work is done; and iii) Bringing about right attitudinal orientation. The training programmes of various modules will be designed for senior officers like IAS/HCS and other senior officers in the other Government Departments/Boards & Corporations etc. The training will enhance the competence of the Officer which ultimately improve public service delivery that is the core object of the State Service. *****

entries.purpose: The “State-wide Antyodaya SARAL Helpline” has been operational in HARTRON since September, 2018 for service/scheme related queries and grievances for citizens of Haryana. There are approximate 1.25 lac calls received in a month (Approximate 5,000 to 5,200 calls per day). In order to achieve with vision of Saral to transform citizen service delivery in Haryana, initially 10 seats started “Antyodaya Saral Helpline” at Hartron Bhawan Panchkula, has been extended from 10 seats to 20 seats, 20 seats to 50 seats and 50 seats to 100 seats due to huge incoming calls volume as per directions received from PD, CMGGA / Digital Haryana Cell so that no call should be dropped/un- answered. Currently, State-wide “Antyodaya SARAL Helpline” is operational with 114 seats (which have 110 operators & 4 supervisor) six days a week in 2 shifts i.e. Monday to Saturday from 07:00 AM to 03:00 PM & from 1:00 PM to 09:00 PM from Hartron Bhawan, Panchkula.

entries.name: Organisation of Seminars/Exhbition, Workshop at National/International level
entries.purpose: Name of Scheme Organisation of Seminars/Exhibitions, Workshops at National /International level The vision of Digital India programme is to transform India into a digitally empowered society and knowledge economy. It is much more than going paperless, but it is about transforming the lives of people across societies through effective use of ever evolving robust technologies and methodologies. 2. It is also known that with the rapid technological innovations and large number of IT & electronic units entering in the field, the market is getting highly competitive. Thus, it is becoming difficult for the industry to market their products and services. It is particularly so for small-scale industry, which has meagre resources in terms of trained manpower and finances for interacting with the buyers and to exhibit products and services in the national/ international exhibitions. 3. In view of the above, it is proposed that Society under the above scheme, may assist the IT & electronic industry in the State in the form of; (i) Holding workshops/ seminars at the state level on e-Governance, cyber Security, Social & financial inclusion, Incubation & entrepreneurship, awareness on technology innovations, public private partnerships etc inviting stakeholders in the development of State. stakeholders in the state would be academics, technology providers, government, industry and the citizens (ii) Arranging buyer’s seller’s meet where the products of the local industry will be displayed. Seminars will be held so as to know their requirements and future trends. (iii) Participation in national/ International seminars and exhibitions by senior officials so as to know the emerging trends in the field of information technology and electronics. (iv) A massive promotion/ advertising campaigns would be done at district, block and village levels to connect to the grass root level. At least 12-15 seminars/workshops and training are to be organized across all district reading portal awareness programme and information on cyber security from time to time.

entries.name_in_the_narrative: Grant-in-Aid for the Integrated Development of Scheduled Castes of Mewat Area
entries.purpose: The State Government had constituted Mewat Development Board (MDB) in 1980 with the vision to ameliorate the conditions of poverty, unemployment, economic and social backwardness and to raise the standard of living of the people in the Mewat area consisting of six blocks of Nuh District viz Nuh, Tauru, Ferozepur Jhirka, Nagina and Punhana and one block of Palwal district namely Hath in to provide special funds for the development of these areas. Mewat Development Agency (MDA) is the executing Agency for the specific development programmes in this backward region. The Government provides Grant-in-Aid for on-going schemes/activities to create infrastructure and basic amenities in the field of education, drinking-water supply, water harvesting, agriculture, animal husbandry, women empowerment, sanitation, community development etc. In 2018, National Institution for Transforming India (NITI) Aayog started Aspirational District Programme to identify and support the most backward districts of India. Out of 108 districts selected by the NITI Aayog, Mewat scored lowest among all the indicators. Hence, Mewat was tagged as the most backward district of the country. Mewat Development Agency being the nodal agency for the development of Mewat district (now known as Nuh district) has very high responsibility to meet the expectation of the people of the region. Mewat Development Agency works in various sectors, either alone or with the support of line departments, for the upliftment of the region. The major components of development are as follows:- 1. Health 2. Education 3. Scholarship & Coaching 4. Skill Development Trainings 5. Animal Husbandry: 6. Rain Water Harvesting/Renewable Energy a)Rain Water Harvesting b)Renewable/Solar Energy 7. Information Education Communication Activities. *****

entries.name: Strengthening of Planning Machinery at State Level- Establishment Expenses
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Strengthening of Planning Machinery at State Level- Establishment Expenses
entries.purpose: In order to achieve optimum outcome in terms of balanced development, based on the recommendation of an Expert Group on Planning at grass root level, guidelines for District Planning were framed by erstwhile Planning Commission, Government of India in 2006. Through these guidelines, strengthening of existing institutions like the State Planning Board and State Planning Department were also suggested. Therefore, it is necessary to strengthen the Planning Unit at State level so that all functions/ activities could be carried out properly. In today’s modern technological era, the system of manual data processing and analysis has become obsolete and is also not suited to cope up with even the existing statistical system, so, an increasing demand was felt in the department for new computer based data processing technique since long time. The Department had prepared its IT plan as per State Government instructions and purchased Computer Hardware and Software. Keeping in view the nature and quantum of work of various sections of the department at Headquarter as well as its District level field offices, the department has identified 28 software applications, required for the full implementation of the department’s IT Plan. To engage Young Professionals in Finance & Planning Department, candidates possessing high academic credentials, professional achievement and leadership qualities are selected as Young Professionals. These qualified Young Professionals provide high quality professional inputs in the field of Economics, Finance, Education, Health, Agriculture, Urban Development and other major sectors. The estimates of State Domestic Product and related aggregates are considered to be the most important economic indicators to measure the economic development of the State. This department compiles estimates of Gross State Domestic Product (GSDP) & related aggregates as per the technical guidance & methodology provided by National Statistical Office (NSO), Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI), Govt. of India. A Committee on Sub-National Accounts was constituted by Govt. of India to review the concepts, definitions, classifications, data conventions, data sources and data requirement for preparation of State Domestic Product (SDP) and District Domestic Product (DDP) and to lay down revised guidelines. The committee submitted its final report in March, 2020, recommending several actions to be taken by the NSO and State Governments. The recommendations of the committee did not only consist suggestions regarding improvement in the extent GSDP methodology and data sources but also regarding compilation of Sub-State aggregates and compilation of expenditure side aggregates by the State, as per defined release and revision calendar. The committee divided its recommendations broadly in following eight categories:- 1. General; 2. GSDP at Current Prices; 3. GSDP at Constant Prices; 4. New Surveys to be mandatorily undertaken by State DESs’; 5. Frequency and Revisions of GSDP Estimates; 6. Expenditure Estimates; 7. District Domestic Product; 8. Strengthening and Training of Manpower at State DESs’ and National Account Division (NAD) for GSDP Estimation. Under this scheme, the funds shall be provided to the Institutes/ Universities to carry out research work for the Department of Economic and Statistical Affairs, Haryana to implement the recommendations of Sub-National Accounts (SNA) committee for improvising GSD Estimation and other areas of research, in the state.

entries.name: Modernisation and Strengthening of State Statistical System
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Modernization and Strengthening of State Statistical System
entries.purpose: The Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MOSPI), Government of India had initiated the Indian Statistical Strengthening Project (ISSP), with an objective of achieving the recommendations of the National Statistical Commission (NSC), Government of India. The mission of the Indian Statistical System shall be to provide the decentralized structure of the system, reliable, timely & credible socio economic statistics, to assist decision making within & outside the Government, to stimulate research and promote informal debate relating conditions affecting people’s life. The ISSP project is being implemented by Government of India (GoI) in two tiers. Tier-I comprises assessments and recommendations and Tier-II comprises implementation. In Tier-I, MoSPI conducted a study to identify the specific requirements for State Statistical Bureaus (SSBs)/State Directorates of Economics and Statistics (DESs). The objective of this study was to document the status of data collection, processing & the standards followed in each State, to assess the infrastructure & human resource available and make recommendations for improving statistical capacity in each State. Some of the recommendations are given as under:- 1. Directorate of Economic and Statistics (DES) should be made a separate department in each State and be declared as Nodal Agency for providing all information related to Statistics. 2. In most of the States, there is a system for collection of village level statistics. Therefore, this system should also be created in the remaining States and DES should also be involved in the process of generating local area development statistics. 3. Additional manpower needed to be provided for statistical activities especially at the primary local level. 4. ISSP is crucial for the development of State Statistical System and so it should be implemented as early as possible. 5. Most of the States have Common Statistical Cadre at least in respect of key departments. Having a common cadre is essential to generate quality statistics and to improve Statistical coordination. So, all States should work for common statistical cadre by covering Statistical Units/Cells functioning in various other departments of State Government. Keeping in view the above mentioned recommendations by Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI) Government of India, there is also an urgent need to strengthen the State Statistical System of Haryana State, so that an effective system could be developed at both levels for getting reliable and timely desired results. Accordingly, the department has prepared its IT and monitoring plan and for that purpose, there is a proposal to hire vehicles for field officers. Other objective of the scheme is to organize training of the officers/officials of DESA, Haryana and various other organizations by the departmental officers who had received training at Haryana Institute of Public Administration, Gurugram, Central Statistical Organisation, Government of India and other institutes for enhancing their knowledge and technical skills. The Department of Economic & Statistical Affairs, Haryana is the nodal department for the formulation and monitoring of Welfare and Development schemes in Budget Estimates. In this context, various preliminary meetings are being held with officers/officials of all the concerned departments at Headquarter level to discuss Revised Estimates and Budget Estimates demand of their departments. Review meetings are also being held regularly during the year to monitor the expenditure incurred under Welfare and Development schemes.

entries.name: Construction of Vitt Bhawan
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Construction of Vitt Bhawan
entries.purpose: The Department has been allotted a plot in Sector-5B, MDC, Panchkula for construction of “Vitt Bhawan Haryana” through HSVP, Panchkula. In the proposed Vitt Bhawan building, the office of Small Savings Department, Local Audit and Treasury & Accounts, Haryana, will be housed. Under the scheme, the provision of funds has been made for construction of “Vitt Bhawan Haryana” in a phased manner.

entries.name: Treasury and Accounts Administration
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Treasury and Accounts Administration
entries.purpose: This scheme is equipped with budgetary provision for purchase of land and carrying out other major works.

entries.name: Scheme for Creation/Purchase of Capital assets for Directorate of State Audit
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Scheme for Creation/Purchase of Capital assets for Directorate of State Audit
entries.purpose: Under this scheme Directorate of State Audit Haryana requires funds for purchase of Capital assets for the following purposes: (i) For purchasing of 2 Cars and their maintenance. (ii) The Department is newly established. Furniture and Fixture are required to be purchased to run the office.

entries.name: Share Capital to Haryana State Financial Services Limited
entries.purpose: Name of the Scheme- Share Capital to Haryana State Financial Services Limited Under this scheme, the provision of funds have been made for providing share capital to Haryana State Financial Services Limited. *****

entries.name: Swarna Jayanti Haryana Institute for Fiscal Managment
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Swaran Jayanti Haryana Institute for Fiscal Management
entries.purpose: Swarna Jayanti Haryana Institute for Fiscal Management has constructed a building at IP-9, Sector-3, Panchkula for setting up its office. The mission of SJHIFM would be to position itself as the first point of reference for consultancy and handholding by the Government to provide structured training and research programmes for Govt. officers/officials in the areas of public finance policy, financial management and financial administration with specific focus on taxation, budgeting, financial planning, audit and account management procedures and policy issues. This would not only enhance the research repertoire of the candidates but also enable SJHIFM to borrow from the learning of collaborative research and incorporate the same in their training calendar. The Class-rooms will be facilitated with audio-visual equipment and other electronic aids to facilitate effective teaching/training methods. Under the scheme, a token provision of funds have been kept for the Financial year 2026-27. *****

entries.name: Strengthening of District Plan
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Strengthening of District Plan
entries.purpose: District Plan Scheme was introduced in Haryana State during the year 2008-09. Funds are allocated under this scheme to the districts on the basis of their population. The Government of Haryana constituted District Development and Monitoring Committees (DDMC) in all districts from the year 2012-13 with a view to ensure proper and timely utilization of District Plan funds in public interest and avoiding non-utilization of funds. The Committee in each district is being chaired by the Minister heading the District Public Relations and Grievances Committee. The Deputy Commissioner of a district is the Vice-Chairman of the committee and he also chairs the meeting of DDMC in the absence of Chairman. The DDMC is empowered to approve various development works as per local needs. These funds are released to different executing agencies in Rural and Urban areas by the Additional Deputy Commissioners-cum-Chief Planning & Development Officers for various development works. Further, for better & effective implementation of the scheme & execution of the development works and monitoring of development works, there is a proposal to purchase vehicles for Head Quarter, during the year.

entries.name: Welfare of Scheduled Castes under District Plan Scheme
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Welfare of Scheduled Castes under District Plan Scheme
entries.purpose: Under this scheme, the funds are being sanctioned for execution of development works approved by respective District Development and Monitoring Committees as per scheme guidelines on the basis of local needs. These funds can be utilized to meet the gap of resources of different departments at district level. 40% of the total funds of District Plan Schemes are to be spent on the local needs of the area to provide direct benefits to the Scheduled Castes population. *****

entries.name: Scheme for providing Loan to Haryana State Agricultural Marketing Board (HSAMB) Panchkula for the Establishment of Apple Fruit and Vegetable Market at Pinjore
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Scheme for providing loan to Haryana State Agricultural Marketing Board (HSAMB) Panchkula for the Establishment of Apple Fruit and Vegetable Market at Pinjore
entries.purpose: This scheme introduced in the financial year 2021-22 for establishment of new Apple, Fruits & Vegetables Market at Pinjore. The major objective of this scheme is to create infrastructure facilities such as shops, offices, Kisan Rest House, Trade & Training Centre Platforms for loading/unloading/assembling and auctioning of the produce, parking sheds, internal roads, garbage disposal arrangements also including drinking water, sanitation arrangements, weighing and mechanical handling equipment etc. In addition to the above, the provisions of plots for ancillary facilities such as Controlled Atmosphere Cold Storage (CA chambers), Ripening Chambers, Pre-Cooling Chambers, and processing Units for fruits and vegetables, Packaging Station, Petrol-cum-CNG Station has been kept. These plots will be allotted to the most eligible entrepreneurs through an open auction to build, own and operate these facilities.

entries.name: Scheme for Providing Loan to HIHMC Panchkula for Establishment of India International Horticulture Market, Ganaur, Sonepat
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Scheme for providing loan to Haryana International Horticultural Marketing Corporation (HIHMC) Panchkula for Establishment of India International Horticulture Market Gannaur, Sonepat
entries.purpose: The project for Development of India International Horticulture Market, Ganaur, Sonepat, Haryana has been introduced in the year 2020-21 for the prosperity and welfare of the farmers. The Haryana International Horticulture Marketing Corporation Ltd. is the sponsoring agency of this project. This scheme mainly focus on the loan to HIHMC Panchkula for the establishment of India International Horticulture Market Gannaur, Sonepat. i) To establish a market of international standards for handling fruits, vegetables, and other perishables, along with developing associated infrastructure and related facilities, initially at Ganaur or any other location in Haryana as decided by the State from time to time. ii) To design, plan, build, construct, operate, manage, develop, finance, and maintain infrastructure related to agriculture, horticulture, dairy, poultry, livestock, and dry fruits, including processing, exports, and other allied commercial activities related to produce market projects across India and abroad. iii) To appoint transaction advisors and consultants for preparing feasibility studies, surveys, detailed project reports, and conducting tests to determine the desirability, viability, and feasibility of establishing markets and allied projects through user charges, revenue sharing, collaboration, participation, consortiums, custom hiring, etc., in any part of India or abroad. The market is being developed on 554 acres of land and is envisioned as one of the most modern and largest markets in the country. It is planned to handle produce arrivals from South to West India while providing upstream services across North, South, East, and West regions, with an estimated arrival capacity of approximately 20 lakh MT annually. The market will integrate all essential market and non-market services, including supporting facilities. It will be developed as a Green Hub, featuring:

entries.name: Scheme for loan to Haryana Agro Industries Corporation
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Scheme for Loan to Haryana Agro-Industries Corporation.
entries.purpose: This scheme was launched on 2nd August, 2021 for opening of consumer goods retail outlets under “Har-Hith” Retail Expansion Project. In this project, 2000 retail stores/outlets (1500 stores in rural areas and 500 stores in urban areas) will be set-up across all the districts of Haryana which will help in boosting the spirit of entrepreneurship and generating employment across the State of Haryana and will cater the daily (Kirana) needs of the consumers. All stores will be allotted to the candidates having domicile of the village/ward in the State of Haryana. The operations of the retail outlet will be the responsibility of the allottee. IT and logistics will be handled by private vendors to ensure best deliverance. Warehousing and logistics will work through master warehouses and DCs across the State of Haryana to ensure smooth delivery of products at Central Warehouses. The integrated IT and technology system will also enable for complete visibility of end-to-end retail operations.

entries.name: Loan for Warehousing and Cold Storage
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Loan for Warehousing and Cold Storage
entries.purpose: Haryana State Warehousing Corporation (HSWC) came into existence on 1/11/1967. It was carved out from the erstwhile Punjab Warehousing Corporation. It is a statutory body created under an Act of Parliament with the twin objectives of providing scientific storage facilities for a wide range of agricultural produce and notified commodities to the farmers, Govt. agencies, Public Enterprises, traders, etc. and to make available credit against goods deposited in the warehouses. At the time of its inception, HSWC had only 16 godowns of 7000 MTs total capacity and has grown manifold with the present number of warehouses rising to 115 and storage capacity to 18.80 lakhs Metric Tons (as on 28.02.2023) under this scheme., NABARD will be providing the loan to Haryana Warehousing Corporation for the construction of godowns in rural areas of the State. *****

entries.name: Scheme for State Government loans to Haryana State Cooperative Agriculture & Rural Development Bank for Farmers
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Scheme for State Government Loans to Haryana State Cooperative Agriculture & Rural Development Bank for Farmers (HSCARDB)
entries.purpose: HSCARDB is the main source of investment credit to farmers in the state. The bank depends on refinancing from NABARD to carry out its loaning operations. The bank is not in a position to advance loans from its own resources to sustain the loaning to its prospective customers. The benefit of the scheme the HSCARDB will sustain for implementing its lending programme for the farmers.

entries.name: Loan to Hosuing Cooperative for SC Memebers
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Loan to Housing Cooperatives for SC members
entries.purpose: The HOUSEFED is an apex cooperative housing federation in the State which is playing a good role in providing finance to the group housing cooperative societies. In order to uplift of Scheduled Castes, Backward Classes and other Economically Weaker Section of the society living in the towns/cities, the members of Housing Cooperatives are granted loan from Government through Housing Federation. The Government will sanction loans to Housing federation for further providing loans up to Rs. 12,50,000/- depending on the size of dwelling unit to be constructed for extensive outreach of the scheme for maximum benefit of the urban poor for each individual member and remaining part of 25% of the loan sanctioned will be borne by the borrower member from his own resources. The loan shall be advanced for construction of flats/ houses to the category of Urban Poor Scheduled Castes, Backward Classes and other Economically Weaker Section who are the members of Cooperative Group Housing Societies in Urban Areas and land has been allotted by Haryana Shehri Vikas Pradhikaran/ Haryana State Infrastructure & Industrial Development Corporation any authorized Agency or the members of Cooperative House Building Societies in Urban Areas colony, that should be duly approved by Town Country Planning / Municipal Committees/ Govt. Agency. The rate of interest on this loan will be @ 4 % p.a. on subsidized rate. The benefit of the scheme will be that about 100 members of Cooperative Housing Societies in Haryana State will have their own house as well as Scheduled Castes members Cooperative Housing Societies.

entries.name: Loan to scheduled castes labour & construction societies
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Loan to Scheduled Caste Labour & Construction Societies
entries.purpose: The Primary Cooperative Labour & Construction Societies will be able to raise financial facilities from bank and invest the loan amount in execution of works. These societies would be able to enhance their work securing capacity as well as its timely execution by ensuring continuous job/work to its members for raising their socio- economic status. The State Government will provide financial assistance in the shape of share capital (Rs. 80,000) working capital loan (Rs. 80,000) and managerial subsidy (Rs. 40,000) as per recommendation of Assistant Registrar, Cooperative Societies concerned. The assistance shall be given to those Labour & Construction Societies that has been registered for more than three years and executed work to the tune of Rs. 10.00 lakh or more.This scheme will help the Primary Labour & Construction Societies to enhance their business activities as well as Scheduled Caste Cooperative Labour & Construction Societies.

entries.name: Loans to Haryana State Agricultural Marketing Board (HSAMB)
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Loans to Haryana State Agricultural Marketing Board (HSAMB)
entries.purpose: The main objective of the scheme is to execute the development works under Hon’ble Chief Minister announcements related to construction and special repair of 246 Rural and 183 Link Roads and Mechanization of Mandies by transferring NABARD Loan to Haryana State Agricultural Marketing Board (HSAMB).

entries.name: Loans to village Panchayat for Revenue Earnings
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Loans to Village Panchayat for Revenue Earning schemes
entries.purpose: The interest free loan recoverable in 30 yearly instalments is provided to the Gram Panchayats/Panchayat Samiti in the State with a view to augment their financial position. The loan is granted for installation of tube-wells, pumping sets on shamlat land, construction of shops at bus stand, construction of staff quarters etc. The financial assistance is released on the basis of resolution by the respective Gram Panchayat/Panchayat Samiti based on estimates prepared by the competent authority and on the recommendations of the respective DDPO/BDPO. The objective of the scheme is enhancing the income of Gram Panchayats by providing them interest free loans. The scheme aims to strengthen the financial position of Gram Panchayats, enabling them to undertake income-generating activities and become self-sustaining units.

entries.name: Interest Free Loan in lieu of deferred sales Tax /Vat
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Interest Free Loan in lieu of deferred Sales Tax/VAT
entries.purpose: The State Government had introduced a scheme under the Industrial Policy-2005 and Industrial Policy-2011 namely “Interest Free Loan in lieu of deferred Sales Tax/VAT” to the new Industrial units. The objective of the scheme is to encourage entrepreneurs to set up their industrial units in the backward areas of the State. The incentives to be provided under the scheme are as under:- (b) Mega Project with investment of ` 100.00 crore and above or any project employing more than 500 persons irrespective of investment to be set up in the backward areas would be eligible for financial assistance to be quantified @ 50% of the tax paid on the sale of goods produced by such industrial units, under the Haryana Value Added Tax Act 2003 for a period of 5-7 years from the date of start of commercial production, as Interest Free Loan (IFL) repayable after a period of five years from the date of disbursement of Interest Free Loan. (b) New MSME units in the backward areas would be eligible for financial assistance in the shape of Interest Free Loan to be quantified @50% of the Haryana Value Added Tax Act, 2003 for a period of 5 years from the date of start of commercial production and repayable after a period of five years. Since the purpose and nature of both the above mentioned schemes are same, therefore, both the above said schemes have been merged and renamed as “Grant of Interest Free Loan in lieu of Sales Tax/VAT”.

entries.name: Setting up of power cogeneration and ethanol Plant in Cooperative Sugar Mills.
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Setting up of Power Cogeneration and Ethanol Plant in Cooperative Sugar Mills
entries.purpose: This scheme has been formulated for expansion and modernization of Cooperative Sugar Mills by adopting modern technologies to derive the benefits of scale of economy and generating environment friendly clean energy from bagasse by setting up Cogeneration plants and production of ethanol from molasses for blending in petrol. This will help the Mills in generating extra revenue and minimize the losses of Sugar Mills. Setting up of power cogeneration plants in Sugar Mills will help in generating extra income from power export to the State Grid. Similarly, Mills will earn extra revenue from sale of Ethanol. This will help the Mills to improve their financial help to some extent.

entries.name: Loans to all Co-operative Sugar Mills
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Loans to all Co-operative Sugar Mills
entries.purpose: The main object of the scheme is to enable the Cooperative Sugar mills to make payment of cane arrears to the cane growers. The State Govt. provides highest State Advised Price (SAP) of sugarcane Rs.415/- for Early and Rs. 408/- for Mid and Late variety for the crushing season 2025-26 amongst all of the States, against the Fair & Remunerative Price (F&RP). The Government intends to improve the productivity of sugarcane and sugar recovery and make availability of sugar to the consumer at reasonable price. The main benefit of the scheme is that the sugar mills of Haryana can make payment of cane price to the farmers.

entries.name: Scheme on National Project Management of Soil Health & Fertility
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Scheme on National Project Management of Soil Health & Fertility
entries.purpose: The objective of the scheme is to provide chemicals, glass-wares and equipment for strengthening of Soil Testing Laboratories as per their requirement, sample analysis, providing training to students of Government Schools/Colleges. Long term objective of the scheme is implementation of ‘HarKhet-SwasthKhet’ campaign in which each and every acre of cultivable land of the State will be sampled and tested. There are 52 departmental Static and 54 Mini- Soil Testing Laboratories functional at the Divisional, sub-divisional and district levels.

entries.name: Scheme for Quality Control on Agriculture Inputs
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Scheme for Quality Control on Agriculture Inputs
entries.purpose: The objectives of the scheme are to check malpractices/adulteration in fertilizers, pesticides, seeds as well as to ensure good quality agricultural inputs to the farmers by testing pesticides, fertilizers and seeds samples on the basis of provisions of Insecticides Act, 1968, Insecticides Rules, 1971 and Fertilizers (Control) Order, 1985 and Essential Commodities Act, 1955, Seed Act, 1966 and Seed (Control) Order, 1983 and to create a buffer stock of DAP and Urea fertilizers with the institutional agencies like Haryana State Co-operative Supply and Marketing Federation Limited (HAFED), Haryana Agro Industries

entries.name: Reimbursement of Market fee Plus GST under Price Support System to HAFED
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Reimbursement of Market Fee Plus GST under Price Support System to HAFED.
entries.purpose: The main objective of the scheme is procurement in order to ensure a remunerative and stable price environment to the farmers of the State for increasing agriculture production and productivity. The market prices for agricultural produce many times have a propensity to be unstable and volatile which may result in undue losses to the farmers and discourage them for adoption of the modern technology and required inputs. The Government of India declare the Minimum Support Price (MSP) for notified agricultural commodities every year well before the sowing season of both crops so that the farmers may take a considered view whether the said particular crop will be a profitable venture for them or not. The MSP of Oilseeds and Pulses have a propensity to be unstable and volatile which may result in undue losses to the farmers and discourage them for adoption of the modern technology and required inputs. Consequently, State Government has decided to procure the oilseed & pulses at MSP under Price Support Scheme of Government of India through State Nodal Agency Haryana State Co-operative Supply and Marketing Federation Limited (HAFED). A State Scheme for reimbursement of Market Fee Plus Goods and Service Tax (GST) under Price Support Scheme to HAFED is functional in the State.

entries.name: Scheme for Promotion of Cotton Cultivation in Haryana State.
entries.purpose: Name of Scheme: Scheme for Promotion of Cotton Cultivation in Haryana State. The main objective of the scheme is to increase area, production and productivity of cotton crop with water conservation and improving the economic conditions of the farmers in the state. Cotton is one of the important commercial cash crops of the state, which is generally grown in south-western part of the state. The Scheme will be implemented in all the cotton growing districts of the State namely Hisar, Sirsa, Fatehabad, Jind, Rohtak, Jhajjar, Bhiwani, Charkhi-Dadri, Rewari, Mohindergarh/Narnaul, Sonipat, Panipat, Palwal, Faridabad, Mewat, Gurugram and Kaithal for carrying out the various types of developmental activities in the cotton crop. Under the Scheme Assistance on Desi Cotton, Integrated Method of Pest Management (IPM) and Promotion of Micro nutrients (INM), Judicious Quantification of Nutrients and Soil Health, Evaluation of Bt. Cotton Hybrid, Training of Farmers, Farm Field School, Kapas Diwas, Kisan Mela, Water Tank with Micro Irrigation System (Drip/Sprinkler Set), Training of Extension Officers, Production of Cotton Hybrid Seed, Exposure visits, Workshops, Seminars, Distribution of Literature, Awareness Campaign etc is provided.

entries.name: Scheme for Technology Mission on Sugarcane
entries.purpose: Name of Scheme Scheme for Technology Mission on Sugarcane The Technology Mission on Sugarcane is an existing State Plan scheme. The scheme is implemented in the assigned areas of the Sugar Mills of the State and to

entries.name: Scheme for Promotion of crops diversification and water Conservation
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Scheme for Promotion of Crops Diversification and Water Conservation
entries.purpose: The following programme/scheme is covered under promotion of Crops Diversification and Water Conservation:- (i) Mera Pani Meri Viraasat During Kharif 2020, Govt. of Haryana had launched a unique initiative “Mera Pani Meri Virasat” to diversify the Paddy Crop (water guzzling crop) into alternative less water consuming crops like Maize, Cotton, Bajra, Pulses, Vegetables and Fruits. Under the “MPMV”, assistance @7000/acre is being provided to the farmers who have replaced their paddy crop with alternate crops. The Scheme was further strengthened in Kharif 2021 with additional alternate crops like Kharif Oilseeds (Til, Castor, Groundnut), Kharif Onion, Kharif Pulses (Moth, Urd, Guar, Soyabean), fodder crops. In Kharif 2021 another initiative was inclusion of fallow land in this scheme. Farmers who kept their land fallow in place of paddy for improvement of soil health were also allowed for incentive in Kharif 2021(Khet Khali Phir Bhi Khushhali). During Kharif, 2021 Bajra crop was dropped from the ambit of alternate crops. Due to concerted efforts of the State Government, an approximate 25,600 hectare land 20,752 hectare area was diversified from paddy to other alternate crops and the State Government has provided incentives of Rs. 45 crores and Rs. 36 crores during 2020 & 2021, respectively. The Scheme was further strengthened in Kharif 2022 by inclusion of Agro-Forestry (Poplar and Eucalyptus) in the ambit of alternate crops. During Kharif, 2022 an area of 37956 hectare was registered against the targets of 40000 hectare and an area of 23560 hectare has been verified. During the Kharif 2022 the State Government has provided incentives of Rs. 41.23 crore. During Kharif, 2023 an area of 28370 hectare has been registered against the targets of 48000 hectare and an area of 14345 hactare has been verified. The Scheme has been further continued in Kharif 2024, with a target of 80000 hactare diversification of paddy into other alternative crops. During this current year through online registration an area of 26260 hectare is registered.

entries.name: Scheme for the Strengthening of Haryana Kisan Kalyan Pradhikaran
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Scheme for the Strengthening of Haryana Kisan Kalyan Pradhikaran
entries.purpose: The State Government constituted Haryana Kisan Kalyan Pradhikaran on 10th April, 2018 to formulate and undertake humanistic and holistic welfare based approach to address the difficulties faced by the farmers of the State and to provide relief to

entries.name: Scheme for Promotion of sustaninable Agriculture Strategic initiatives and Kisan Kalyan Kosh
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Scheme for Promotion of Sustainable Agriculture Strategic Initiatives and Kisan Kalyan Kosh
entries.purpose: The objective of the scheme is to promote sustainable agriculture by extension through mass media in an integrated manner, subsidy component, awards to the outstanding farmers, villages and districts and other charges. There are two Centrally Sponsored Schemes Rashtriya Krishi Vikas Yojana (RKVY) and National Food Security Mission (NFSM), where subsidy is provided on the distribution of certified seed of the crops covered under the respective schemes. Subsidy is provided only on the certified seeds being sold to the farmers through sale outlets of Government/ Institutional agencies like Haryana Seeds Development Corporation (HSDC), Haryana Land Reclamation and Development Corporation (HLRDC), Haryana Agro Industries Corporation Ltd. (HAIC), Haryana State Co-operative Supply and Marketing Federation Limited (HAFED), Chaudhary Charan Singh Haryana Agriculture University (CCSHAU), National Seeds Corporation Ltd. (NSC), Haryana State Cooperative Apex Bank Ltd. (HARCO) Bank, Indian Farmers Fertilizer Cooperative Ltd. (IFFCO)/ Indian Farm Forestry Development Cooperative Limited (IFFDC), Cooperative Limited (KRIBHCO) and National Fertilizer Ltd (NFL). The subsidy is equally admissible to each category of farmers. The subsidy will also be available in those districts which are covered under National Food Security Mission (NFSM) also. In order to strengthen the extension services by using print and electronic media and information technological support following steps are taken: a) To publish necessary material in print or electronic form. b) Regular issue of printed or electronic material, such as book or magazine (offered for distribution of Newspapers, Magazine, Pamphlets, Folders etc.) and prepare the material for electronic media (radio jingles, documentary films & TV programme etc.) will also be used for dissemination of the latest information and knowledge on a wide spectrum of topics to the farming community. Discussion on field problems and finalization of the package of practices in Agriculture Officer’s Workshop/Seminars before sowing of Kharif & Rabi crops, Agriculture Day/ Kisan Gosthies/Exhibitions, Awareness Camps and State/Districts level Kisan Melas are organized to create awareness among the farmers regarding the improved agronomic practices of Rabi and Kharif crops. The following Awards are taken in the Scheme for the outstanding Farmers of the Haryana (Districts and Villages level):- • Award to the Farmer having highest productivity • Award for outstanding /innovative Farmers. • Award to the outstanding Districts • Award to the outstanding Villages

entries.name: Scheme for strengthening of Agriculture Extension infrastructure.
entries.purpose: Name of Scheme Scheme for Strengthening of Agriculture Extension Infrastructure The objective of the scheme is to increase the knowledge system, improve the quality of data collection, technical competency of the farmers at village level and to provide a communication link between the extension staff of the Department & farming community. The scheme is not only to ensure maintenance but also to improve and pursue the mandates of training and visit programs of Agriculture Extension.

entries.name: Haryana Fasal Suraksha Yojana
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Haryana Fasal Suraksha Yojana
entries.purpose: During Kharif 2023, the Agriculture Insurance Company of India Ltd. had refused to implement the scheme 'Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana' in cluster-II. Due to this peculiar situation and in the interest of the farmers, the State Government has launched a new scheme named as 'Haryana Fasal Suraksha Yojana' in Cluster Il having seven districts Ambala, Hisar, Jind, Mahendergarh, Karnal, Sonipat and Gurugram for cotton crop loss compensation for the season Kharif 2023 in the State. The farmers have been charged enrolment fee of Rs. 1500/- per acre to register their Cotton crop under the scheme through online mode. Under the scheme, 17,806 farmers have been registered with registered area 61417.806 (in Acre) and collection amount of Rs. 9,21,26,685.50/-. A total of 15,317 farmers have been benefited with financial amount of Rs 65,08,18,007.11, out of which Rs. 63,49,36,732.60 has been disbursed to the farmers and the remaining amount of NEFT rejected cases is in the process of disbursement. In addition to this, during Kharif 2024, the State Govt. has decided to disburse an amount of Rs. 2000.00 per acre to farmers for adverse weather conditions for Agricultural and Horticultural Crops. For this decision, an approximate amount of Rs. 800.00 Crore has already been disbursed to farmers. Hence, the Haryana Fasal Suraksha Yojana is now being used for the purpose to disburse the bonus to the farmers.

entries.name: Pradhan mantri Fasal Bima Yojana
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Pradhan Mantri Fasal BimaYojana
entries.purpose: Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana is a flagship scheme of the State and Central Government implemented on a subsidy-sharing basis in a 50:50 ratio. This path-breaking initiative aims to ensure the welfare of farmers. Under the scheme, farmers are required to pay a uniform premium of only 2% of the sum insured for all Kharif crops, 1.5% for Rabi crops, and 5% for cotton crops. The remaining premium will be equally borne by the State and Central Government. The scheme aims to keep the premium burden on farmers significantly low while ensuring comprehensive risk coverage. The use of technology is a key feature of the scheme. Smart phones will be utilized to capture and upload data from Crop Cutting Experiments (CCE), which will help reduce delays in claim settlements. Additionally, remote sensing technology will be employed to minimize the number of Crop Cutting Experiments (CCEs) required. The scheme provides coverage for the following stages of crops and associated risks leading to crop loss: 1. Localized Risks: Losses or damage resulting from identified localized risks, such as hailstorms and inundation (except paddy), affecting isolated farms within the notified area.

entries.name: Crop residue management under Clean Air Project for sustainable Development - SPV ARJUN
entries.purpose: Name Code of the Scheme Crop Residue Management under Clean Air Project for Sustainable Development-SPV ARJUN The objective of the scheme is to provide a critical component of the Haryana Clean Air Project for Sustainable Development (HCAPSD), to meet the expenditure for crop residue management interventions during Financial Year 2026-27, including seasonal readiness for Crop Residue Burning Control, cluster facilitation, field monitoring, logistics planning, and sample surveys.

entries.name: Scheme for management of crop residue
entries.purpose: Name Code of the Scheme Scheme for Management of Crop Residue The objectives of the scheme are:- 1. Providing incentive @ Rs. 1000/- per acre In-Situ & ex-situ as operation charges for management of Crop Residue in compliance of the Orders of Hon’ble Supreme Court. 2. Protecting environment from air pollution and preventing loss of nutrients and soil micro-organisms caused by burning of crop residue. 3. Promoting Farm Machinery Banks for custom hiring of crop residue management machinery to offset the adverse economies of scale arising due to small landholding and high cost of individual ownership. 4. Creating infrastructure and capacity building for monitoring and effective implementation to achieve the target of zero crop burning. 5. Providing incentive to the farmers on In-Situ & Ex-situ to encourage them for zero burning of the crop residue. 6. Dissemination of area specific/crop specific technology.

entries.name: Scheme for Agriculture Engineering Service
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Scheme for Agriculture Engineering Service
entries.purpose: The objectives of the scheme are:- 1. To provide fuel for cooking purposes and organic manure to rural household through the construction of family biogas plants. 2. To mitigate drudgery of rural women, reduce pressure on forest and accentuate social benefit. 3. To improve sanitation in villages by linking sanitary toilet with biogas plant. 4. To strengthen of tube-well machinery & equipment for augmentation of under-ground water resources for irrigation purposes. 5. To help the farmers of State in the installation of tube well at their field by providing operators, machinery and casing pipe. It will contribute as large extent to help the farmers in improving their economy and agriculture production in the state. 6. To increase the production and productivity and give employment to farmers by providing of Agriculture implements on custom hiring. 7. To maintain the agriculture implements/machinery purchased under centrally sponsored schemes for demonstration purposes.

entries.name: The Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA) Project for Promoting Sustainable Horticulture in Haryana Strengthening of Horticulture Extension System and Producer Groups
On-Farm & Marketing Support to Horticulture Farmers
entries.name_in_the_narrative: On-Farm & Marketing Support to Horticulture Farmers
entries.purpose: The purpose of this scheme is to collectivize farmers, especially small producers at various levels across the State, to foster technology penetration, improve productivity, enable improved access to inputs, services and increase farmers income, thereby strengthening their sustainable agriculture-based livelihoods at the same time. Organized retailing in Fresh Fruits and Vegetables (FFV) is bringing about dramatic changes in horticulture marketing in India and that requires dedicated supply chain than the traditional approach of marketing of fresh produce. This Scheme requires development of backward and forward integration by creating on farm infrastructure required for organized marketing of fruits and vegetables. The main objectives of this Scheme are as under:- a) To develop farmer socio economic security model in the villages – farm sustainability. b) To achieve nutritional security and deliver safe food to the consumers. c) Transparent Institutional Delivery Mechanism d) Comprehensive and state of the art research and cold-chain design, including energy transition e) Successful business model and incubating the start-ups and a centre to facilitate the development of cold-chain, f) Demonstration of the best available technology, conduct and facilitate high-quality research and development. g) Enhance capacity and raise awareness of stakeholders including Farmer Producer Organizations (FPOs). Major programmes/components covered under this scheme are as under:- Integrated Packhouse/Collection centre development in different clusters including grading /packing machines, cold rooms, refer vans, primary processing centres, solar power, waste management unit, etc.

entries.name: Scheme for promotion of Advanced National and International Technologies in Horticulture Sector
Scheme for Horticulture Crops Insurance in Haryana renamed as Mukhyamantri Bagwani Bima Yojana (MBBY)
entries.purpose: Name of Scheme Scheme for Horticulture Crop Insurance in Haryana renamed as Mukhya Mantri Bagwani Bima Yojana (MBBY) Govt. has launched horticulture crop insurance scheme as Mukhya Mantri Bagwani Bima Yojana (MBBY) for the farmers growing horticulture crops to mitigate their risk against loss due to adverse weather & natural calamities, like hailstorm, temperature- High Temperature/Heat wave & frost, water perils, wind velocity and fire. A total of 46 vegetable, fruit & spice crops will be covered under the scheme. Farmers need to give only @ 2.5% i.e. Rs. 750/- and Rs. 1000/- against sum assured of Rs. 30,000/- for vegetables/spices and Rs. 40,000 for fruit crops per acre, respectively. The claim compensation will be based on survey and extent of loss in four categories of 25, 50, 75 & 100. Farmers are to adopt this scheme while registering their crop and area on Meri Fasal Mera Byora (MFMB) portal. A seed capital of Rs. 10.0 crores will be kept by State Govt. State and District Level Committees under PMFBY shall monitor, review, and resolve the disputes at State Level as well as District Level. The objectives of the scheme is as under: I. Encourage farmers to raise horticulture crops to increase their income level. II. Ensure the financial sustainability of farmers suffering from crop losses due to adverse weather & natural calamities. III. Encourage farmers to use innovative & modern agricultural practices. IV. Encourage farmers to diversify from wheat & paddy to horticulture crops.

entries.name: Scheme for Integrated Horticulture Development in Haryana State
National Horticulture Mission (NHM)
entries.name_in_the_narrative: National Horticulture Mission (NHM)
entries.purpose: National Horticulture Mission has a vital role for the holistic growth of the horticulture sector covering fruits, vegetables, root & tuber crops, mushroom, spices, flowers, aromatic plants, coconut, cashew, cocoa and bamboo. To make horticulture a profitable diversified farm activity in increasing income of the farmers by achieving potential productivity through sustained and advance technologies. The benefit has been given to all categories of farmers, one time through DBT. To avail the benefits of the scheme it is mandatory that the beneficiary should be landowner or taken land on lease. Under this scheme, funds in excess of the prescribed proportions as "Top-up" as extra State share in the Centrally Sponsored Scheme (60:40) The objectives of the Scheme are as under:- • To generate employment opportunities for skilled and unskilled manpower. • To meet out domestic demand of fresh fruits & vegetables. • To promote public-private-farmer-partnership in horticulture activities.

Scheme for providing implements/machinery on subsidy to the group of farmers and SC farmers
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Scheme for providing implements/machinery on subsidy to the group of farmers and SC farmers
entries.purpose: The main objectives of the scheme are as under:- 1. Employment generation of Scheduled Caste Farmers. 2. Making farming a profitable business and improving financial health of SC Farmers. 3. To increase the farm power availability in the Haryana. 4. Reduction of drudgery of labour in farm operations. 5. Scheme for Integrated Watershed Development and Mangement project in the State
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Scheme for Integrated Watershed Development and Management Project in the State
entries.purpose: The aims of the scheme are as under: a) Conservation, development & sustainable management of natural resources including their use. b) Enhancement of agriculture productivity and production in a sustainable manner. c) Reduction in regional disparity between irrigated & rain fed areas. d) Creation of sustainable employment opportunities for the community. e) Control of soil erosion and restoring productivity in degraded lands.

entries.name: Scheme for Pilot Project for the reclamation of saline soil and Waterlogged land in the state.-Normal Plan
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Scheme for Pilot Project for the Reclamation of Saline Soil and Waterlogged Land in the State-Normal Plan
entries.purpose: The objective of the scheme preservation of the agricultural production capacity of agriculture land in the water logged and saline soils of Haryana which is in danger of becoming unproductive and also improvement of the agricultural production of land that has already become unproductive because of water logging/ salinity. The scheme will benefit large chunk of farming community with increased per unit productivity. Socio- economic conditions of the poor farmers will also improve. entries.name: Scheme for Strengthening of Human Resources and Infrastructure-Establishment Expenses
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Scheme for Strengthening of Human Resources and Infrastructure–Establishment Expenses.
entries.purpose: It is a continued staff scheme, provision of salary to the staff posted in offices of Deputy Directors in Sonipat, Palwal, Nuh and Charkhi Dadri as well as in 26 Sub Divisions.

entries.name: Scheme for providing Financial Assistance to the Societies for Prevention of Cruelty.
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Scheme for providing Financial Assistance to the Societies for Prevention of Cruelty
entries.purpose: Under this scheme, department is providing grant-in-aid to the societies setup for prevention of cruelty to animals. The Government of Haryana has declared 22 Veterinary Institutions/Government Veterinary Hospitals as infirmaries under the provisions of the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act, 1960, Such institutions are basically set up to provide shelter and other basic facilities to the Infirm & helpless animals. In order to make these Infirmaries functional, apart from the infrastructure to be provided, additional manpower needs to be deployed at these Institutions. It is also proposed that the management of these Infirmaries will be under overall control of the concerned Society for the prevention of cruelty as under consideration of Deputy Commissioner of District concerned. To provide the services of Societies for Prevention of Cruelty at gross- root level in the State all the veterinary Hospital/DDL and polyclinics are made child units of Society for Prevention of Cruelty to Animal (SPCA) as Pashu Sawasthay Kalyan Samitti (PSKS).

entries.name: Opening /Up-gradation and strenghtening of vety.Institutions
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Opening/Up-gradation and Strengthening of Veterinary Institutions
entries.purpose: This scheme comprises provision of salary/wages for staff sanctioned to run of 382 Government Veterinary Hospitals and 479 Government Veterinary Dispensaries that have been opened/upgraded, 21 mobile vans and 2 Disease diagnostic labs functioning in the State since 2005-06 as well as staff of the 8 Veterinary Poly Clinics and 2 Bio Safety Level-II Lab at Sonipat and Raipur Rani at Panchkula setup to provide specialized Veterinary Services to livestock of the State. Apart from this, provision has also been made for the supply of equipment, chemicals glass wares as well as to provide general veterinary care by way of supply of general veterinary medicines and drugs for the ailing livestock free of cost through the Government Veterinary Hospitals and Veterinary Dispensaries.

entries.name: Scheme for Conservation and Development of Indigenous cattle and Murrah development
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Scheme for the Conservation and Development of Indigenous Cattle and Murrah Development
entries.purpose: The objective of the scheme is conservation and development of the indigenous Cows and Murrah Buffaloes. It is essential to promote conservation and development of indigenous breeds. Livestock Sector has an important role in the integrated farming system particularly for the small as well as land less farmers in the State. For further growth of national economy, there is a need of policy support including emphasis on

entries.name: Scheme for the Establishment of Gou Seva Ayog
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Scheme for the Establishment of Gau Seva Ayog.
entries.purpose: The Govt. has constituted a Gau Seva Aayog for the preservation and welfare of cattle in the State. Grant-in-aid to Haryana Gau Sewa Ayog for the creation of infrastructure in the existing Gaushalas and newly created Nandishalas is being provided under the scheme. Other than this some amount is spent on Salary, POL, Rent, TA, Electricity Bill, Maintenance of Vehicles and for creation of Capital Assets for the Gaushalas who will rehabilitate Stray Cattle in addition to their holding capacity of cattle.

entries.name: Scheme for Establishment ofHi-tech Dairy units
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Scheme for Establishment of Hi-tech Dairy Units.
entries.purpose: This is a continued programme being implemented in the State with the following objectives:- (i) To provide self employment to unemployed rural/urban youths. (ii) To enhance the production of milk to cope up with the increasing demand of consumers in general and milk plants of the state in particular. (iii) Help to provide additional income to the families and the young new entrepreneurs. (iv) Creation of pool of quality germ plasma of Murrah Buffaloes.

entries.name: Scheme for Setting up of Pet Clinic
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Scheme for Setting up of Pet Clinic.
entries.purpose: It is a continued scheme under which an ultra modern pet Hospital-cum-Training Centre has been set up at Panchkula for diagnostic and treatment of the pet animals kept by the residents of the Panchkula area in particular and of the State in general. This institute also functions as a referral clinic where the facilities of diagnosis, follow-up during the course of the disease, evaluation of therapy and pronouncing a dependable prognosis is available. The indoor and out-door pets department have started functioning roundthe clock for the facility of the pet lovers by qualified veterinary and para vet staff. Grant-in-aid has also been provided to the Pet Animal Health Society, Haryana, Panchkula for the strengthening of canine dentistry and construction of new infrastructure.

entries.name: Scheme for Establishment of Backyard poultry unit
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Scheme for Establishment of Backyard Poultry Unit
entries.purpose: It is a continued state scheme under this scheme low input technology birds of Chabbrro breed will be supplied to the beneficiary families. There is a target to setup 1500 backyard poultry units in the State preferably in Mewat and Shivalik area and each family will be provided 50 chicks 8-10 days old free of cost to the beneficiaries with drinker and feeder. The Department has its own Poultry Hatchery at Hisar which will be further strengthened to produce quality chicks of low input technology that are highly suitable for backyard poultry farming in the State. This scheme will strengthen the infrastructure of Government Poultry Hatchery, Hisar for the purchase of Hatcher, Setter and other related items etc. Chicks would be reared at Govt. Hatchery, Hisar and thereafter will be supplied free of cost at the doorstep of the beneficiaries in the State along with drinkers and feeders as list of beneficiaries.

entries.name: Bhed/Bakri (Sheep/Goat) Palak Utthan Yojana
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Bhed/Bakri (Sheep/Goat) Palak Utthan Yojana
entries.purpose: This scheme has been started with an objective of providing self-employment opportunities to the unemployed persons in the State by establishing Sheep/Goat units of 10 Female +1 Male for SC/BPL/Widow and Landless General, BC and Other Category families free of cost. Further assistance would also be provided for insurance of the livestock. In addition to this assistance for purchasing of wool from established unit would be done by the department. All the animals of established unit will be provided deworming, vaccination and treatment free of cost by concerned Veterinary Institution (Animal Husbandry & Dairying Department).

entries.name: Scheme for Establishment of Goat and Sheep Unit
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Scheme for Establishment of Goat & Sheep Unit
entries.purpose: The scheme is designed to provide self-employment opportunities to the unemployed persons in the State by establishing Sheep / Goat units of (15 female + 1 male) and piggery units of (10 female + 1 male). There is a target to set up 200 such units during the year 2026-27. Under the scheme financial assistance to the tune of 25% of the unit cost will be provided by the Govt. whereas the remaining part will be the contribution of the beneficiaries either as loan from the financial institutions. The beneficiary would be provided the veterinary assistance facilities (treatment, vaccination and consultancy) by concerned area veterinary hospital. If any Livestock Insurance Scheme is in operation then the insurance of animals purchased for establishment of Unit is to be covered under that Scheme wherever permissible. However, if no Livestock Insurance Scheme is in operation then the beneficiary would have to arrange for the insurance of the animals. This subsidy would be provided in the bank account/ loan account of the beneficiary.

entries.name: Scheme for Employment opportunities to Scheduled Castes by establishing Livestock units for Scheduled castes
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Scheme for Employment opportunities to Scheduled Castes by Establishing Livestock Units for Scheduled Castes.
entries.purpose: The objective of the scheme is to provide employment opportunities to the Scheduled Castes by establishing 2 or 3 milch animals and Piggery Unit of (10 female + 1 male) will be established during the year 2026-27. The Government will provide subsidy to the tune of 50% of the unit cost on the establishment of these livestock units.Where as the remaining part will be loan from the bank/ financial institutions. This subsidy would be provided in the bank account/ loan account of the beneficiary. There is a target to setup 1500 dairy units and 100 piggery units during the year 2026-27. In addition to this, Sheep and Goat unit comprising 15 female+ 1 male is target to set up 800 units will be established. The Government will provide subsidy to the tune of 90% of the unit cost on the establishment of Sheep/Goat. Whereas the remaining part will be the loan from the bank/financial institutions.The subsidy will be provided three months after the purchase / tagging of Milch animals or disbursement of Loan by bank, whichever is later and subject to verification of unit by concerned veterinary surgeon. 2 Milch Animals Scheme is also applicable to the poorest of the poor family as identified under Mukhya Mantri Antodaya Parivaar Uthan Yojana-MMAPUY. The maximum applications have been received by the Animal Husbandry Department under this Flagship Scheme of Government for which subsidy liability will also be in 2026-27 .

entries.name: Scheme for Special Livestock Insurance for schedule castes
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Scheme for Special Livestock Insurance for Scheduled Castes.
entries.purpose: This scheme has been formulated as a SCSP scheme for the benefit and welfare of the scheduled caste families engaged in the rearing of livestock. The Government of India provides assistance to the tune of 40 % against the premium amount of Livestock Insurance of Scheduled Caste Families. The rest amount is paid under this scheme to make the Livestock Insurance of SC families totally free of cost.

entries.name: Scheme for the Ornamental Fisheries
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Scheme for the Ornamental Fisheries.
entries.purpose: The objective of this scheme is to bring revolution in the field of Ornamental Fisheries. After the establishment of Ornamental Fish Hatchery, there will be a boom in production of ornamental fishes in the State and will bring employment opportunities to the unemployed youth. It is envisaged to create a class of trained men power in the field of Ornamental Fish breeding and rearing by providing in house training to the educated youth at Government Fish Seed Farm Saidpura, Karnal (Rearing unit Ornamental Fish Hatchery), training sub centre at Jyotisar (Kurukshetra) and Aquaculture Research and Training Institute (ARTI), Hisar. For awareness and publicity of ornamental fisheries, awareness camps, workshops and seminars would be conducted district wise. The training will be imparted for 5 days.The main objective/aim of the scheme is to bring revolution in the field of Ornamental Fisheries. Provision of funds has been made to incur an expenditure on Ornamental Aquariums for awareness and publicity for the General Public and also a provision for installation of Aquariums and their maintenance .

entries.name: Scheme for welfare of Schedule caste families under Fisheries Sector-N.A
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Scheme for Welfare of Scheduled Caste Families under Fisheries Sector
entries.purpose: Aim of this scheme is to provide technical and financial assistance to the persons belonging to Schedule Caste families engaged in fisheries sector. Subsidy will be provided under various components such as renovation of ponds (both panchayati and own land ponds) Ist year lease money, 2nd year onward and lease money, purchase of fishing nets, subsidy to purchase Rehri along with (store, gas chulla, utensil etc.) for the fish/ fish product sale, inputs and subsidy on annual auction of notified water etc.

entries.name: Buildings
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Buildings
entries.purpose: The Forest Department has grown into one of the largest Department of the State. Its assets include a large number of buildings, in the field as well as at headquarter in the form of offices, residences and rest houses. These require annual maintenance and repairs. A large number of employees in the Department are still without Government accommodation. Thus, there is a need to construct new buildings and maintain the existing building /rest houses. The aims of the scheme are as under:- 1. Construction and maintenance of office institutes and residential buildings for staff and officers. 2. Construction and maintenance of Forest Rest Houses.

entries.name: Revitalization of institutions in Aravali Hills.
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Revitalization of Institutions in Aravalli Hills
entries.purpose: European Union sponsored project for rehabilitation of Aravalli Hills was executed by the Department during 1991-2000. Village Institutions were created and plantations were done in almost 350 villages in six districts wherein the Aravallis are located. After closure of the project, these institutions have become defunct and in several villages, the plantation areas have become degraded. This scheme is being implemented to maintain green cover in the Aravalli Hills which are one of the oldest mountain systems in the world. Some enrichment planting will be done in areas where degradation has taken place. Areas will be closed so that natural root stock gets regenerated. Protection trenches / stone wire / create wire structures will be constructed and village ponds will be rehabilitated besides other soil and moisture conservation works. The state plan scheme namely “Revitalization of Institution in Aravalli Hills” is being proposed to be named as “Revitalization of Aravalli Hills” to better reflect the objective of the scheme. Aims and objectives of the Scheme: - (i) To maintain and protect the green cover created under “Aravalli Afforestation Project” with the help of Village Forest Committees and other stakeholders. (ii) To afforest the barren hills by enrichment plantation with trench-cum–pit method and by carrying out various moisture conservation works. (iii) To close the barren hills by construction of stone wall fencing so that natural root stock available in the area gets regenerated. (iv) To conserve soil and water by construction of water harvesting structures/stone wire / create wire structures in the foothills of Aravalli. (v) To construct protection trenches in foothills of Aravalli to obstruct possible illegal mining activities and also to engage protection watches in these areas. (vi) To rehabilitate / construct ponds in the villages of the Aravalli regions for ground water recharge.
