entries.name_in_the_narrative: Herbal Nature Park

entries.name: Development of Agro Forestry Clonal and Non Clonal
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Development of Agro Forestry Clonal and Non-Clonal
entries.purpose: Agro-Forestry is a dynamic land management system that combines agriculture with forestry, horticulture, medicinal plants and animal husbandry on the same piece of land. It utilizes production potential of land in two to three tiers with suitable crop-tree combinations. The demand of agro-forestry products and services in the country is increasing with rapid economic growth, industrialization and increase in population. Integrated cultivation of agriculture and tree crops is being adopted as a strategy to save natural forests and to ensure sustained supply of raw-material to Wood-Based Industries. The aims of the scheme are as under: i) To increase the tree cover outside forests in consonance with the State and National Forest Policies. ii) To encourage practice of agro-forestry on farmlands for crop diversification and increase in the productivity of farmlands. iii) To raise woodlots on Panchayat lands, Institutional lands, Roadsides, Community lands and Private farm lands as well as Forest Lands. iv) To raise seedlings in nurseries for sale/distribution to public. v) To raise fruit orchards on common lands and Panchayat lands. vi) To implement Shiv Dham/Bani rejuvenation/Amrit Van plantation. Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam campaign and Van Mitra scheme. vii) To implement Paudhagiri scheme by providing quality seedlings to students studying in class 6th to 12th . viii) To do plantation around village ponds. ix) To provide pension under Haryana Pran Vayu Devta Pension Scheme to custodian of Pran Vayu Devta trees of 75 years of age or more and having high ecological significance. x) To carry out research activities; collections of forests seed and raising and procurement of quality seedling.

entries.name: Afforestation Waste land and Agro Forestry Project
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Afforestation Waste Land and Agro Forestry Project
entries.purpose: Afforestation of Wastelands and Agro-Forestry Project was launched in the State in the year 1991-92 to continue as Social Forestry Project. This project covered wastelands including alkali lands ,sand dunes, other Panchayat land and agriculture fields which are generally not covered under traditional forestry programme. The Project plays a vital role in harmonizing the regional imbalance of climate and environment in the State and neighboring areas. The project also promoted social, economic and developmental activities. To meet with the expenses on salary as per approved cadre of the establishment of the Department under the scheme, the whole salary portion of Strip plantation on Government & development of Agro-Forestry Clonal & Non-clonal Scheme merged in this scheme.

entries.name: Green Belts in urban Areas
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Green Belts in Urban Areas
entries.purpose: The urban areas are adversely affected from vehicular and industrial pollution. The population in the urban areas, therefore, suffers from respiratory and water borne diseases. Urban Island Heat effect also increases air temperature. The amelioration of urban environment effectively checks the air pollution bringing respite to the residents. Objectives of the scheme are to take up tree plantation activity in urban area along roads, in parks and in other areas available in various localities for increasing Tree Cover. To increase the green cover in urban areas for improvement in the environment, ameliorate the urban island heat impact and to check air pollution.

entries.name: Wild life Protection in Multiple use Area
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Wild life Protection in Multiple Use Area
entries.purpose: This scheme is for protection of wildlife and extension activities. It is proposed to encompass all these into one scheme and expand the activities for improvement of habitat for wildlife, especially for birds outside protected areas and for promotion of facilities for eco-tourism. Additional check posts and regulatory chain gate at entry points will be established for apprehending poachers and illegal trade in wildlife produce. A very effective means of protection of wildlife is through education of the common masses, farmers, teachers and students. Holding nature education camps, preparing the educational material and such other activities are included in this scheme. It is also proposed to strengthen the information on the wildlife resources in the State. For this, census of wildlife in the protected areas needs to be carried out. In- service training of the forestry staff in the wildlife and in-service training for up-grading the skills of the wildlife staff for better management of resources in the State has been proposed and incorporated. In recent years unusual mortality of peacocks, partridges and quails has been reported. Excessive use of pesticides/insecticides in agriculture may be harming the birds. The survival of these birds is important for agriculture because they protect the crops from insect pests. There are several important bird areas outside National Parks and Sanctuaries that will be developed. Activities to encourage publicity, extension and eco-tourism will be undertaken. Rewards/Incentives will be given to informer of wildlife offence under the scheme. In addition, Haryana Forest and Wildlife Department has started a scheme for the adoption of animals and birds in zoos and deer parks of the state to generate love for animals and birds. This noble scheme which is the brain child of Hon’ble Minister of Finance, Irrigation and Forest & Environment, started in Haryana with effect from 07.11.2011. The Aravalli Zoo-cum-Safari Park at Gurugram and Nuh shall be established under the scheme, announced in the Budget for the financial year 2025–26. Eco-friendly water body/wetland in Seonsar Reserve Forest, Survey Demarcation through installation of boundary pillars of Eco Sensitive Zones, National Parks/Wildlife sanctuaries also maintained and repair of old buildings through this scheme. Through the implementation of this scheme, the wildlife in the State will be better conserved and protected and any adverse effect on human and live stock population and agriculture due to decline in wildlife will be checked.

entries.name: Extension of Zoo and Deer Park
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Extension of Zoo & Deer Parks.
entries.purpose: The Zoos in the country have to follow the guidelines issued by the Central Zoo Authority (CZA) of Ministry of Environment, Forest & Climate Change (MOEF&CC) (GOI) and these have to be approved by it. In the absence of adequate resources for the management of Zoos, three Zoos were closed in the State and only three Zoos at Pipli, Bhiwani and Rohtak were given provisional approval by CZA. This has given specific requirement of space and facilities for each species of wild animal kept in the Zoo. The layout plan for Pipli and Rohtak Zoos has been prepared and resubmitted for approval to CZA. Although some cages at Pipli and Rohtak Zoos fit into these specifications, there are other enclosures that need to be renovated and enlarged. CZA provides adequate funds for such works, although the basic responsibility of maintaining the Zoos lies with the State Government. More cages are required to be constructed as per CZA guidelines. As indicated above, following Centres will be developed /maintained under the scheme. 1. Mini Zoo, Pipli. 2. Mini Zoo, Rohtak. 3. Mini Zoo, Bhiwani. 4. Deer Park, Hisar. 5. Peacock and Chinkara Breeding Centre Jhabua, Rewari. 6. Crocodile Breeding Centre, Bhoursaidan The school children and people in general get information about wildlife. It also creates awareness among people regarding wildlife conservation. They can also observe wildlife from close distance.

entries.name: Environmental Training Education and Awareness Programme
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Environmental Training Education and Awareness Programme
entries.purpose: The objective of this scheme is to promote awareness and education about environmental pollution/hazards through short films, pamphlets, distribution of environmental literature, posters, hoardings, blow-ups, conducting seminars/workshops and conference, holding exhibitions, imparting training and advertising in leading newspapers, radio and television. It is a very important project to create awareness at the grass root level in general public. Schools/Colleges are best place for creating awareness among the young generation. Regular seminars/workshops /quiz competitions for different age groups are organized in the state schools/colleges for creating awareness among the young generations. Training is also imparted to Eco Club Incharges of the Eco Club Schools and Colleges established in the state of Haryana. The funds will be disbursed to Education Department on account of organizing the Awareness Programmes among school/college students.

entries.name: Setting up of Environment Training Institute at Gurugram
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Setting up of Environment Training Institute at Gurugram
entries.purpose: The main objective of this scheme is setting up of “Swarna Jayanti Environment Training Institute at Gurugram” to promote environmental sensitivity and knowledge in all sections of the society including industrial units as air, water, hazardous & solid waste pollution being created by industrial units and the persons handling these works are totally ignorant regarding scientific waste from these units. To impart training to these workers of industrial units who are handling ETP, hazardous/solid waste disposal for proper functioning. The institute will also undertake the research studies on environmental protection and monitoring of air and water quality. The proposed amount will be utilized for the salary of the staff and maintenance of the office, once the construction of the said institute is completed. *****

entries.name: State Environment Impact Assessment Authority- Establishment Expenses
entries.name_in_the_narrative: State Environment Impact Assessment Authority- Establishment Expenses
entries.purpose: The State Environment Impact Assessment Authority (SEIAA) Haryana has been setup by Ministry of Environment, Forest & Climate Change, Government of India, on the recommendation of the State Government as required under EIA Notification for according environmental clearance to Category “B” Projects covered under EIA Notification dated 14.09.2006 in the State of Haryana. EIA Notification is applicable since its inception for different projects like Mining Projects (sand mining, stone mining, etc.), Bio-medical Waste, Common Effluent Treatment Plant, Manufacturing/Storage Units of Hazardous Chemicals and all Construction Projects (more than 20,000 sq.mt. etc.). The State Level Environment Impact Assessment Authority has been reconstituted on 24.12.2025 for three years as per Gazette Notification Govt. of India. The funds are required for salary, sitting fees, travel allowances, purchase of vehicle for Chairman, SEIAA, various site visits, procurement of office items etc.

entries.name: Establishment of Eco Clubs
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Establishment of Eco Clubs
entries.purpose: Under this scheme, this Department has established 5250 Eco-Club schools and 100 Eco Club Colleges in all districts of the Haryana State. These Eco-Clubs are meant for organizing various activities on environmental issues throughout the State like plantation, creating awareness among the students and public etc. This scheme is meant for inculcating the spirit of environmental protection and conservation at grass root level i.e. in schools and colleges of Haryana. The allocated funds will be disbursed to Eco Club Schools for organizing programmes on environmental issues.

entries.name: Climate Change Division
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Climate Change Division
entries.purpose: National Action Plan on Climate Change (NAPCC) was released in the year 2008 with strategy to meet the challenge of Climate Change. The NAPCC is guided by the principles of sustainable development and aligns the environmental and economic objectives. It outlines a national strategy that aims to enable the country adapt to Climate Change and enhances the ecological sustainability of nation’s developmental path. As per guidelines of National Action Plan on Climate Change (NAPCC), State action plan on Climate Change (SAPCC) has been prepared after consultation with various Government Departments by Environment & Climate Change Department being Nodal Agency. The SAPCC has already been approved by the State Steering Committee. It stresses to maintain high growth rate which is essential for increasing living standards of the vast majority of people of the State of Haryana and reducing their vulnerability of the impacts of Climate Change. The focus will be the implementation of the State Action Plan on Climate Change (SAPCC) with the aid of other Departments and stakeholders.

entries.name_in_the_narrative: Establish a Command & Control Centre (CCC) under for Data Backed Decision-making (DSS), under Clean Air Project for sustainable Development-SPV ARJUN
entries.purpose: This scheme was conceived owing to increasing air pollution and deteriorating air quality index in the country, The Haryana Clean Air Project for Sustainable Development (HCAPSD)is an initiative of the Government of Haryana in collaboration with the World Bank. The project intends to improve air quality and reduce emissions in a common geographic area (the Indo-Genetic Plain), across state boundaries. For the implementation of the project, the World Bank is extending financial and technical assistance to Haryana for 5 years,from2025 till 2030. Sector-wise interventions proposed under the project includes:- • Procurement of 10 continuous ambient air quality monitoring stations with real- time source apportionment capabilities (CAAQMS) and Deployment of 2 mobile vans for real-time source apportionment • Establishment of a command control centre (CCC) and integration of data sources. • Driving citizen engagement in all matters related to air quality through awareness initiatives and grievance resolution mechanisms • Collaboration with IGP (Indo-Gangetic Plain) states will to enhance knowledge sharing and capacity building in monitoring air quality. The project will be financed through the World Bank's Program for Results (P for R) mechanism. Under the P for R mechanism, the phase-wise indicated payment from the World Bank will be received only after the targets in the disbursement-linked indicators(DLIs) are met.

entries.name_in_the_narrative: Loan to Horticultural University
entries.purpose: Maharana Pratap Horticultural University (MHU) is the first Horticultural University in Haryana and fifth University in the country. The university became functional on 6th January, 2017. The State Government has provided land at Anjanthali, Karnal for setting up MHU and also at Ambala, Jind and Jhajjar for establishing Regional Research Centres, in addition to Mushroom Regional Research Station, Murthal (Sonepat) running under HAIC which has been merged with MHU, Karnal with the approval of State Government. These four Regional Research Centres have become functional as per mandate of the University. Some emergent and essential regular staff along with contractual employees engaged through HKRNL has been provided at the Centres to make them effective and smooth functional. In additional to above, one Regional Research Centre at Kharkhari, District Bhiwani has been started. The mandate of University is to be a centre of excellence in teaching, research, and extension activities in the field of Horticulture and allied sectors for food and extension security improved livelihood opportunities and economic prosperity of farming communities. The University aims to develop diversified sustainable farming systems for improving productivity and profitability in horticulture and also to train the farmers and extension functionaries for the effective dissemination of advanced horticultural technologies in Haryana with the following objectives. a) To impart education in different branches of horticulture and allied sciences as it may determine, from time to time. b) To further advancement in learning and research in horticulture and allied sciences and to undertake extension of such specialized knowledge to the needy people. c) To undertake study in post-harvest management and marketing strategies of horticulture produce and products.

entries.name: Interest Subvention for refurbishment of Milk Plants under Dairy Processing and Infrastructure Develoment Fund (DIDF) Scheme
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Interest Subvention for Refurbishment of Milk Plants under Dairy Processing and Infrastructure Development Fund (DIDF) Scheme.
entries.purpose: In the Union Budget 2017-18, a proposal for setting up of Dairy Processing and Infrastructure Development Fund (DIDF) with loan assistance from NABARD @6% p.a. under DIDF was announced by the Central Government with an outlay of Rs.10881 crore. Rs.8000 crore shall be loan from NABARD to NDDB and NCDC. Allocation of Rs. 864 crore for meeting interest subvention will be released to NABARD over a period of 12 years covering. The entire loan repayment period from 2018-19 to 2027-28.The Standing Finance Committee (SFC) has also approved the project proposal and subvention scheme to provide interest subvention @2.5% on the loan to be disbursed by NABARD through NDDB under DIDF scheme for refurbishment of Milk Plants in Haryana. The tenure of loan will be maximum 10 years including 2 years moratorium on repayment of principal from the date of first disbursement of loan with last installment allowed up to 1st March 2031. The objective of the project is to strengthen existing system, auto atomization, testing facility to enhance chilling capacity, etc. to improve brand image and to deliver quality milk and milk products to the consumers. After implementation of the project, there would be increase in sales realization, which would be passed on to the milk producers in form of increased milk procurement price. The existing milk plants will become semi-automated for maintaining hygiene and quality of milk & milk products. It will also reduce the running cost of the plant.

entries.purpose: The Hon’ble Chief Minister, Haryana has announced setting up of new Milk Chilling Centre (MCC) at Dabwali, Sirsa (Vide Announcement No. 17921). The Central Government has set a target of doubling the income of the farmers and dairy sector is being considered to have potential to contribute significantly. Milk Union at present does not have its own Milk Chilling Plant. This Chilling Plant will improve the quality of milk & coverage of milk producers. The Milk Plant, Sirsa is required a Milk Chilling Centre of Capacity 20 thousand litres per day at Dabwali to procure milk by giving remunerative price by providing the chilling of raw milk at the area of Dabwali to improve quality of milk and benefit & upliftment of marginal farmers. Hon’ble Chief Minister, Haryana made an announcement during the Budget Speech 2020-21 that first Tetra Pack Plant of Haryana will be set up for packing of liquid milk, fruit juices and fermented milk products. HDDCF will explore possibility for implementing this project in PPP mode as an alternative option, evaluate both the option, give their pros & cons and resubmit with their recommendation. The expression of interest (EOI) has been prepared and is to be floated earliest. After the selection of an agency the work will be start. The major benefit of the scheme is given below:- ● More farmers will be benefited by adding approx. 35 number of villages. ● Quality of milk will be improved due to establishment of MCC. ● Transportation charges will be saved. ● Marginal income of farmers will increase. ● Tetra Pack Plant is a necessity to compete in the market. The quality and shelf life of milk products will improve.

entries.name: Milk Cooperative Societies- Primary Milk Cooperative Societies

entries.purpose: As per mandate of the Central Government to double the income of the farmers, the focus is on strengthening of the village level procurement systems i.e. Bulk Milk Coolers (BMC) by providing of BMC Management System. The BMC Management System will help in reduction in the operational cost of the BMC through monitoring the various aspects of BMC and taking necessary corrective actions. This system will ensure quality, transparency and check adulteration. The aim is to provide BMC Management System to village level Bulk Milk Coolers so that real time information is available and remote monitoring is also possible thereby ensuring quality and stop malpractices. Awareness campaigns will be undertaken by all the Milk Unions for all the societies district wise/area wise in order to spread awareness among the milk producers of the cooperative societies with special emphasis on Women Dairy Cooperative Societies for empowerment of women. The Bulk Milk Coolers (BMC) of various capacities will be installed at village level which will ensure maintaining required temperature for raw milk. The raw milk will be procured through BMCs, which help to maintain the required temperature and its quality. The Bulk Milk Cooler Management System will ensure easy monitoring of milk stored at BMC facility, which will help in increasing efficiency and reduction in malpractices & cost. The awareness campaigns will benefit milk producers who will be made aware of the various welfare schemes run by Haryana Dairy/State Govt., rearing of animals & their diet i.e. Ration Balancing Programme, new varieties of fodder, silage making and schemes related to women.

The State Government will provide financial assistance in the shape of share capital Rs. 80,000/- working capital loan Rs. 80,000/- and managerial subsidy of Rs.40,000/- as per recommendations of Assistant Registrar Cooperative Societies concerned. The assistance shall be given to those L/C Societies that has been registered for more than three years and executed work to the tune of Rs. 10.00 lakh or more. This scheme will help the primary Labour & Construction Societies and district Labour & Construction federation to enhance their business activities as well as SC L/C Societies.

entries.name_in_the_narrative: Organizing the National/State/District level School Games Competitions for under -11 and under-14 age group
entries.purpose: The scheme has been introduced to develop a sports culture at Elementary School Level in the State of Haryana through the games Under-11 (Boys & Girls) and Under-14 (Boys & Girls) age groups and to organize competition for National/State/District School Games of Elementary Schools (Govt. and recognized Private) in different disciplines of Sports competitions every year on the regular basis in accordance with guidelines of School Games Federation of India (SGFI). Under this scheme, the expenditure on Diet Allowance, Sports Kit (Track Suit, Playing Kit, Bag and Stockings), actual fare and other miscellaneous expenditure is incurred for State level and National Level Championships.

entries.name: Expansion of Facilities Classes VI-VIII (Full time)
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Expansion of Facilities Classes VI to VIII (Full Time)
entries.purpose: The objective of the scheme is to provide play way material/infrastructure to improve the quality of education as per provisions of the RTE Act, 2009. Butterfly Tables & Primary Chairs would be required to provide proper environment for students. Hon’ble CM has approved to provide digital boards for the upliftment of education standards for the students of Government Model Sanskriti Schools(GMSS),GPD/GMS/GHS/GSSS in the state to develop the basic aptitude of Mathematics and Sciences and to make teaching learning processes more appealing. The Interactive Whiteboards, Smart Projection Systems, High definition document Cameras and E-books etc. will be provided under this scheme. The amount will be utilized for the procurement of equipment for science labs, establishment of Science/Vigyan, Ganit Gyan clubs in the schools, holding Science seminars/quizzes in the schools.

To cover up the language /communication gap of the students, the Language Labs will be established in phased manner. To impart the education with the play way methods various equipments and teaching aids will also be provided upliftment the educational standards for the students. Under this scheme, two schools (one primary and one middle school) are honoured with cash prizes at Block, District and State level on 26th January every year. The goal of the department is to provide clean, healthy & learning environment to the students in govt. schools by beautifying their building infrastructure as well as clean environment. About 284 schools will be covered in this scheme. The prizes under this scheme are distributed as under: i) At Block Level ₹50,000/- (for one primary and middle school each) ii) At District Level ₹1,00,000/- (for one primary and middle school each)

Beside this, scheme has objective to motivate more and more students to become high achievers in the state short listing of students in Class 6th. The scholarship will take place over two stages:- Stage-I: On the basis of the results of SAT exam in Class 5th, students will be eligible to sit for a special competitive exam which will be conducted by the SCERT Gurugram, Haryana. entries.name: Pratibha Khoj Scheme
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Pratibha Khoj Scheme
entries.purpose: Under the scheme “PRATIBHA KHOJ”, the Haryana State being a welfare state decided to run various programs to enable the talented and meritorious students to prepare for the competitive exams and rightfully earn their places among the white- collar jobs category. It is imperative that a separate scheme has to be created with all necessary financial heads required to run all such coaching programs effectively. Therefore, the Department initiated a new state scheme ”Pratibha Khoj Scheme” for effectively executing the programs already running (i.e. Super-100, Buniyaad, NDA and few others like CLAT etc.).About 6,000 students will be covered under this scheme.

entries.name: Continuous and Comprehensive Evaluation
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Continuous and Comprehensive Evaluation
entries.purpose: Teaching and evaluation have been taken together since long time in our education system. In traditional approaches, the area of assessment has been limited to the cognitive domain only and the objective of assessment has been just to declare how much the student has learnt. This approach encouraged rote learning to pass the examination. Therefore, it doesn’t serve the needs of the present time and there is a need to equip schools with appropriate mechanism of evaluation for regular assessment of all aspects of pupil growth and development i.e. continuous and comprehensive evaluation. In the light of NCF-2005, Department of School Education, Haryana has decided to adopt continuous and comprehensive evaluation in its schools at Senior & Secondary level. In this process, department has started monthly, half yearly and annual assessment test from class 9th to 12th. These help in judging the level of the students regularly and take remedial action timely.

entries.purpose: The State has 36 Educationally Backward Blocks. State Government has decided to run 36 Aarohi Model Schools in society mode in these blocks. A State Society has been registered for these schools namely “Haryana AAROHI Educationally Backward Blocks (EBB) Model School Society” on the pattern of Kendariya Vidyalayas. The aim of this scheme is to develop students and make them aware, socially responsible, creative and capable of contributing to the society. It may also help children of such blocks connect better with the world. The medium of instructions in these schools is English. With this, the talented but poor rural students get opportunity for quality education. About 36 schools will be covered under this scheme.

It helps in increasing enrolment and decrease

entries.name: Swaran Jayanti Programme- Cultural Programme for Students
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Swaran Jayanti Programme-Cultural Programme For Students
entries.purpose: The Scheme has been introduced for strengthening of cultural values, Folk Art, Heritage and Customs of society and to maintain the cultural transformation mechanism for coming generation of Haryana. The School Education Department would like to develop a system for students with the way of school level competitions in Dance, Drama, Music and Music Instruments, Haryanavi Orchestra, Haryanvi songs on various occasions like Bhat, Banra which are commonly sung by the community. At the end of every academic year, it is expected that all the students are not only evaluated on the basis of their academic performance but due weightage must also be given to their co-curricular activities. If student is achieving low grades in academics it is expected that he or she must be very talented or sharp in co-curricular activities. So, objective of this programme is to give equal opportunity to all the students to show their inherent talent. The new pedagogy and education policy elaborate that students are not dump of information but they are expected to be a skilled resource for the nation.

entries.name: Swaran Jayanti Programme- Su-Sanskar-Beti Bachao Beti Padhao (BBBP)
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Swaran Jayanti Programme Su-Sanskar: Beti Bachao Beti Padhao (BBBP)
entries.purpose: The objective of the scheme is to ensure education and welfare of girls. The Department wants to ensure that all girls are able to study up to class-XII and integrating the ‘Beti Bachao Beti Padhao’ Abhiyan (BBBP) initiative of the Government of India by taking various initiatives in this direction. The initiatives include organization of various awareness activities (by way of Rallies, Print Media, Electronic Media, Jingles, Competitions at School, Block, District and State Levels etc.), Celebration of events (like ‘Betion Ka Salam: Rashtra Ke Naam’, ‘Mera Pehla Gantantra Divas’ etc.) Cultural Study Camps at Hilly & Coastal areas etc. By providing necessary infrastructure for girls in the schools like ensuring separate girls toilet, the Department is committed to cleanliness facility in the toilets especially for girls. It provides sanitary napkins vending machines and incinerators in all the Girls High Schools, Senior Secondary Schools and Co-Education High Schools and Senior Secondary Schools with girls student strength of 50 or above as these machines play an important role towards hygiene/sanitation and cleanliness practices.

entries.name: Swaran Jayanti Programme- Swachh Prangan
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Swaran Jayanti Programme Swachh Prangan
entries.purpose: The objective of the scheme is to educate the students about the significance of environment for humans and for animals alike. Linking the concept with Swachhta Kosh at a larger scale, the State will witness the coming around of Swachh Bharat Abhiyan through school education, as cleanliness coupled with eco-sensitivity will be a value imbibed in every student studying in Secondary and Senior Secondary Schools. Further, strengthening of the 3,300 Eco Clubs and setting up of new Eco Clubs in all the Government Middle / High / Senior Secondary Schools of the State with the convergence of Department of Environment, Haryana State Pollution Control Board, and Forest Department etc.

entries.purpose: Haryana State Higher Education Council is statutory Body established by the State Govt. for promotion of academic excellence etc. The Council has been designated as an nodal agency to ponder over, monitor, handholding, mentor the progress regarding implementation of NEP 2020 as a whole encompassing Departments/stakeholders interalia including School, Higher, Technical, Women and Child Departments and the institutions there under.

entries.name: Educational and Excursion Tour for boy Students

entries.purpose: Students generally learn in the confines of their study routine now, it is aimed that the students shall also take excursion event as a purposeful exercise to know the State/Nation. It will help them to become better human being. Short trips of 1-2 days duration and long trips of 4-5 days duration shall be organized by colleges. 100% expenditure on short trips and 75% expenditure on long trips shall be borne from this fund on activities like transportation, refreshment, entry ticket and boarding & lodging. Approximately 40,000 students will be benefitted under this scheme during the year 2026-27.

entries.name_in_the_narrative: Setting up an Education City/EDUSAT in the State of Haryana
entries.purpose: Imparting of education through EDUSAT has been started in 2006 and this is ongoing scheme. This project is meant for imparting education through Satellite. The aims of EDUSAT are: a) EDUSAT will transmit lectures and seminar free of cost to all institutions connected through EDUSAT. b) Every college can have immediate access to technological advancement and scientific up-gradation on any subject. The project has been implemented in 63 Government Colleges and 3 Private Aided Colleges of the State in the first phase and 3 Government Colleges and39 Private Aided Colleges. In the second phase. Approximately 1,30,078 students will be benefitted under this scheme during the year 2026-27.

For the first time in the history of State, four Government sponsored placement fairs were organized at four division level Government Colleges of the state for final year students. About 7,00 students were offered placements and about 22 companies of repute participated in the fairs. Approximately, 64,000 students will be benefitted under this scheme during the year 2026-27.

entries.name: Scholarships(Colleges)
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Scholarships (Colleges)
entries.purpose: The main objective of the scheme is to enable meritorious girl students of Haryana to pursue higher education. The top 10 girl students who after passing 10+2 class with at least 60% marks are studying in any Government Institution pursuing general degree courses are awarded under the scheme. The amount of the scholarship awarded has been ₹3,000/- per college per student annually. There is no income limit for this scheme. There is no need to file an application for the Stipend. The benefit is to be released on the basis of online admission. Approximately, 2,736 students will be benefitted under this scheme during the year 2026-27.

At present students from about 18 States of India are studying in this Institute. State Government has also started the similar institutes in DIET Gurugram and DIET Kurukshetra form 2021-22. For the construction of building of SIASTE Jhajjar, SIASTE Kurukshetra and 4 acre at DIET Gurugram has been approved by the Government. Building construction plan of SIASTE at PG Nehru College, Jhajjar has been approved. entries.name: Haryana State Creche Scheme
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Haryana State Creche Scheme
entries.purpose: Hon’ble Chief Minister has announced to open 500 creches in the State for the benefit of working women, both in organized and unorganized sectors. Accordingly, Haryana State Creche Policy–2022 was formulated and got notified on 21.07.2023 notifying the remuneration of creche workers and helpers, their eligibility for recruitment along with a detailed work out to run the creches in the state. All 500 creches are operational and out of them, 197 creches are stand alone creches. These creches will be upgraded under the Haryana State Creche Policy – 2022. The Department of Women and Child Development has also signed an MoU with Mobile Creche Organization to set up Creche with modern facilities. The following are the objectives of the scheme :- 1. To expand access to Creche and Day Care facilities by promoting diverse models of provisions especially targeting children from disadvantaged and vulnerable backgrounds and children in remote or in accessible areas. 2. To ensure holistic development of all children (aged upto 6 years) by improving their health and nutritional status and promoting their physical, social, emotional and, cognitive development. 3. To improve the learning outcomes of children in the primary classes by ensuring smooth transition from pre-school to formal school. 4. To provide safety and protection from physical and mental abuse by ensuring responsive care in institutional set up and by supporting parents and families in choosing better childcare practices and subsequently reducing the crime rate against children. 5. To engage qualified workforce and to build their capacities for ensuring quality childcare services.

entries.name_in_the_narrative: Financial Assistance to Scheduled Castes families by Haryana Women Development Corporation
entries.purpose: Haryana Women Development Corporation was incepted with a view to promote activities for women’s development, awareness generation, vocational training and to arrange institutional finance for self-employment of women. To make women economically independent, more and more women are required to be channelized into income generating activities. But the women, without any resources are incapable of starting their ventures. Since group activities through community mobilization is over emphasized as an empowerment strategy, more and more SHGs are emerging at the village level. Unless these women groups are linked with economic institutions, the vital issue of economic empowerment of women cannot be adequately addressed. Within this context, to make economic resources more easily accessible to women, Haryana women development corporation (HWDC) plays a vital role through its loaning schemes. It is envisaged to cover at least 5,000 prospective women entrepreneurs every year, not only to give direction and strength to the existing SHGs but also to motivate more and more women to take up income generating activities to become productive members of the society.

Senior Secondary Schools, Exposure visit for meritorious students, Organisation of Science Conclaves, Training of Mathematics/Science School Teachers, Various Science promotion related activities in collaboration with other institutes/ NGOs etc. (ii) Awards & Honours: Haryana Vigyan Ratan & Haryana Yuva Vigyan Ratan Awards and Honouring of meritorious students who have participated/winners in Science/Mathematics Olympiad. (v) Patent Information Centre (vi) Organisation of Conference/workshops/seminars on different fields of Science and Technology in collaboration with different institutes/ NGO etc. (vii) Kalpana Chawala Memorial Planetarium at Kurukshetra: The objective of this planetarium is to create awareness about astronomy among general public and students of the State and imparting non-formal education through films on astronomy/astrophysics.

entries.name_in_the_narrative: Home-cum-Vocational Training Production Centres for Young Girls/Women and Destitute Women and Widows
entries.purpose: In Haryana, there is only one State After Care Home (Nari Niketan) which is being functional in Karnal with a capacity of 65 women for providing institutional care, protection, social security, maintenance, education and training to such girls/women who have no means of subsistence or have been rescued from moral or, are exposed to moral danger with a view to make them self-reliant and become ultimately useful member of the society. The Establishment of “Swarn Jayanti Nari Aashraya Avam Kaushal Kunj” (Multi Skill Training Centre) is required as per the guidelines issued by Haryana Government. The proposal for construction of three Mahila Ashram at Sirsa, Rewari and Narnaul, is in process. PART–II CENTRALLY SPONSORED SCHEMES (SHARING BASIS)

entries.name: Construction of Anganwari Centre
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Construction of Anganwari Centres
entries.purpose: These are State Schemes under which funds are provided to fill the gap of resources for construction of AWCs (Anganwadi Centres) over and above the funds provided by the Government. Under these schemes, it is proposed that Anganwadi Centres will be constructed in each district every year as per applications received from District Programme Officer and the priority will be given to those AWCs which are running in rented accommodations. Under this scheme, the construction work of 140 AWCs and repair work of 319 AWCs have been done and the construction work of 189 New Anganwadi Centres and repair of 812 AWCs is targeted, during the Financial Year 2026-27.

entries.name: Setting up of Science Centre at Ambala Cantt. Renamed as Setting up of Aryabhatta Vigyan Kendra at Ambala
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Setting up of Science Centre at Ambala Cantt. renamed as setting up of Aryabhatta Vigyan Kendra at Ambala
entries.purpose: The Ministry of Culture, Govt. of India has sanctioned the project of Science Centre named as Aryabhatta Vigyan Kendra and is being setup on 5 acres of land on National Highway at Ambala Cantt. Later on, the State Govt. has decided to expand this Centre with two more floors besides creation of three additional facilities viz 270 degree Immersive projection system, Science on a Sphere and Augmented Reality/Virtual Reality Theatre. The entire additional cost would be borne by the State Govt. The construction work of the Science Centre has been started by the PWD (B&R) department.

entries.name: Setting up of Science City at Sonipat Renamed as Setting up of National Science City at Haryana
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Setting up of Science City at Sonipat renamed as setting up of National Science City at Haryana.
entries.purpose: The department has planned to set up a Science City in Sonipat and approaching the Ministry of Culture, Govt. of India for funding the project as per their guidelines. The department is in the process to identify the site for the project. *****

entries.name_in_the_narrative: Loans for Development of Aided Polytechnic
entries.purpose: The aim of the scheme is to develop and establish the three aided institutions under the Technical Education Department namely Chhotu Ram Polytechnic Rohtak, Vaish Technical Institute Rohtak and Seth Jai Prakash Polytechnic Damla Yamunanagar. This scheme is non recoverable financial assistance in the form of interest free Perpetual loan.

entries.name: Loans to Pandit Lakhmi Chand State University of Performing and Visual Arts, Rohtak
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Loans to Pandit Lakhmi Chand State University of Performing and Visual Arts, Rohtak
entries.purpose: The university has four faculties namely Film and Television, Design, Fine Arts, Urban Planning and Architecture. It was felt that in the country in general and North India in particular, the educational opportunities in the area of visual and performing arts are lacking. A unique autonomous Pandit Lakhmi Chand State University of Performing and Visual Arts, Rohtak has been set up for offering degree level academic programmes in design, film & TV, fine arts and urban planning & architecture by the Department of Technical Education, Government of Haryana. This scheme is non recoverable financial assistance in the form of interest free Perpetual loan.

entries.name: Loans to J.C. Bose University of Science and Technology, YMCA Faridabad
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Loan to JC Bose University of Science and Technology, YMCA Faridabad
entries.purpose: J.C. Bose University of Science & Technology, YMCA, Faridabad was established by an Act of the legislature of the State of Haryana (Act 21 of 2009) by upgrading YMCA Institute of Engineering Faridabad, to facilitate and promote studies & research in emerging areas of Higher Education with focus on new frontiers of Science, Engineering, Technology, Management Studies, Non conventional Energy Sources and Environmental Studies and also to achieve excellence in these connected fields. This University is still in developing stage, therefore, development works such as construction of second campus, auditorium, construction of research center, hostels and introduction of new courses in the emerging areas need to be completed. This scheme is non recoverable financial assistance in the form of interest free Perpetual loan.

entries.name_in_the_narrative: Loan to Guru Jambheshwar University of Science and Technology, Hissar
entries.purpose: Guru Jambheshwar University of Science & Technology, Hissar is a Technical University in the State. It is in developing stage, therefore, development works such as already exist construction of auditorium, construction of research center, teacher hostel and introduction of new courses in the emerging areas need to be completed. This scheme is non recoverable financial assistance in the form of interest free Perpetual loan. PART-III CENTRAL SECTOR SCHEMES (100%)

entries.name: State Sports Councils Scheme
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Sports and Games
entries.purpose: The Scheme shall provide fund for activities of setting up of various sports councils and their activities as envisaged in the Sports Policy in the State. The sports are promoted by the various sports associations and councils as well as the Department of Sports and Youth Affairs by extending different type of amenities. In order to patronage these councils, the Department of Sports and Youth Affairs extend them financial aid to motivate and recoup their efforts.

entries.name: Sports Awards and Incentive Scheme-Normal Plan
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Sports Awards & Incentive Scheme–Normal Plan
entries.purpose: Bhim Awards is the highest award of the State Government for the outstanding players of Haryana. The award is given to 11 sportspersons of the State; 5 in individual events, 3 in team events and 2 to Paralympics sportspersons and one for mentally challenged sportsperson. The award will be given once in life to sportspersons of the State based on achievements. Honorarium and pension shall be given to Arjun Awardees, Dhayan Chand Awardees and Dronacharya Awardees from the State in addition to the incentives given by Government of India. In addition to the above, the details of honorarium are furnished below:- Name of Award Revised honorarium Dronacharya ₹20,000/-p.m Arjuna ₹20,000/-p.m Dhayan Chand ₹20,000/-p.m Major DhayanchandKhelRatan ₹20,000/-p.m Tenzing Norgay ₹20,000/-p.m Bhim ₹5,000/-p.m Incentive to coaches will also be awarded to sports coaches under Cash Award scheme who have trained medal winners in following tournaments in accordance with the recommendation of eligible medal winner :- Tournament Gold (₹) Silver (₹) Bronze (₹) Olympics/Para Olympics 20 Lakhs 15 Lakhs 12 Lakhs Asian Games/Para Asian Games 15 Lakhs 10 Lakhs 7 Lakhs CommonwealthGames/Commonwealth 10 Lakhs 5 Lakhs 2 Lakhs Para Games In order to empower the sports persons, the Government of Haryana grant the scholarship to the student sports person of other than SC on following rates :- Level Gold Silver Bronze Participation International 84,000 72,000 60,000 --- National 60,000 48,000 36,000 --- State 42,000 36,000 30,000 18000 (For SC students only) *Female sportspersons shall be given additional amount of ₹1,000/- per month. Approximately 302 State Awardees will be given honorarium & awards and 2500 sportspersons will be benefited under this scheme during the year 2026-2027.

entries.name: Modernization of Information System Scheme
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Modernization of Information System Scheme
entries.purpose: The Sports Department will harness its human resources and infrastructure imaginatively to deliver to the people increased participation, greater inclusion and higher level of excellence in sports. It will employ information technology and current management practices to monitor the Performance of its coaches, administrators and sports quota inductees. The Sports Department shall make extensive use of information technology tools for dissemination of relevant information on matters relating to sports to the various stakeholders, media and public at large. Electronic Sports Equipment for monitoring and enhancing the player’s performance is also proposed. This integrated with provide a state of the Art Infrastructure in the State.

entries.name: Human Resource Development Scheme
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Human Resource Development Scheme
entries.purpose: The Department organizes seminars, workshops and conferences for coaches, sports officials and athletes to keep them abreast with latest development in their field. The scheme covers seminars, workshops and conferences on game specific themes. With a view to promote ‘akhadas’ which are in large number in the State, akhada competitions will be organized regularly. The award money for winners at the district level i.e. District Kesari and District Kumar and at the State Level i.e. State Kesari and State Kumar is intended to be brought at honorable level. Supplementary diet is provided made on the line of SAI. Approximately 24 Sports competitions and 03 Khelo India Youth Games will be organized under this scheme during the year 2026-2027.

entries.name: Infrastructure Scheme
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Infrastructure Scheme
entries.purpose: The Government of Haryana will plan development of sports in a phased manner so that necessary infrastructure is built up over a period of time. ‘State Sports Grid’ would be developed so that maximum people have access to use sports infrastructure. Good quality consumable and non-consumable sports equipments will be purchased for players in coaching centres, Rajiv Gandhi KhelParisars, mini stadiums, sub- divisional level stadiums, district level stadiums and State level stadiums Khelo India & Rehab Centers.

entries.name: Sports and Physical Fitness Authority of Haryana
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Sports and Physical Fitness Authority of Haryana
entries.purpose: The aim of the scheme is to accelerate project preparation and improve the monitoring of projects under execution by ensuring that the Authority is adequately staffed. Department will hire technical people from the Haryana Skill Employment Corporation to meet the need of technical input. The project cell will focus on contemporary, innovative and cost-efficient designs of playgrounds and work for expeditious completion of on-going project. Expenditure is to be incurred towards diet of players, sports kits, education, manpower, residential expenditure & miscellaneous etc.

entries.name: Sports University of Haryana, Rai Sonipat
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Sports University of Haryana, Rai, Sonipat
entries.purpose: The Government of Haryana has established “Sports University of Haryana” in Rai (Sonepat). The objective is to promote sports education in the area of sports science, sports technology, sports management and sports coaching etc. besides functioning as the training center for elite players in selected sports disciplines by adopting best international practices.

entries.name: Infrasturcture Scheme for Scheduled Castes
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Infrastructure Scheme for Scheduled Castes
entries.purpose: The scheme is specifically meant for villages with more than 40% of SC population. The initiative aimed at accelerated delivery of augmented benefits of Department’s infrastructure and youth development schemes to the target villages. The scheme will provide 100% fund for construction of village and block level stadiums and multipurpose halls at Panchayat land of required dimension. These stadiums and halls will be adequately equipped. Medal winners of International, National and State level sporting events shall be given FAIR play sports scholarships for a year at the rates decided by the Government. Level Gold Silver Bronze Participation International ₹84,000 ₹72,000 ₹60,000 --- National ₹60,000 ₹48,000 ₹36,000 ---- State ₹42,000 ₹36,000 ₹30,000 ₹18,000/- Female sportsperson shall be given the additional amount of ₹1,000/- per month Approximately 3,000 players will be given the scholarships under this scheme during the year 2026-2027.

entries.name: Provision of Sports & Equipments & development of playgrounds in Schools
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Provision of Sports Equipment & Development of Playgrounds in Schools
entries.purpose: The objective of the scheme is to strengthen the sports facility in the various Government Schools and to promote sports activities for students at the school level. The goals of the scheme is to improve the standard of sports in the State and to develop the playgrounds, to provide sport equipments in the schools and further to enhance the performance of Haryana State School teams in National School Games Championship. About 336 Schools will be covered under this scheme.

entries.name: Scouting & Guiding Assistance
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Scouting and Guiding Assistance
entries.purpose: The objective of the scheme is to promote Scout, Guide, Cub, Bulbul, Rover, Ranger activities in all the Government schools in the State for the vital benefit of all round development of school children. To improve the training facilities in the various schools of the State and to encourage the students to take part in these activities to take the full advantage of Scout and Guide Programme. The aim is also to open new units and to organize District level and State Level Standard Judging Camps for Scouts, Guides, Cubs and Bulbuls to provide them a competitive platform to expose their hidden talents through various competitions. The

entries.name: Development of Archives- Establishment Expenses
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Development of Archives- Establishment Expenses
entries.purpose: Archives is the only source for keeping an account of daily activities of the Government for posterity. Government Plans can be chalked out on the basis of records. IT Plan of the Department has been prepared and the Websites of the head office have been developed. In the present scenario of computer age, the Department also intends to develop the infrastructure for IT Unit. A post of Junior Programmer and one post of Data Entry Operator will be continued in the year of 2026-27. Besides this, equipment like Computers and its related accessories, scanners, Xerox machines will be purchased for digitalization of record.

entries.name: Publicity programme of Archives
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Publicity Programme of Archives
entries.purpose: The main objective of this scheme is to inculcate the archival consciousness among public in general and students in particular to preserve valuable records for posterity. To achieve the objective, archival exhibitions, seminars and debates are organized in every district of Haryana State. For the purpose of organizing exhibitions, the Department has been purchasing/preparing displaying material for modernization of record room. The Department will organize Archival Exhibitions Preservation of old records are done on scientific lines for posterity so that valuable records may not be destroyed with the passage of time. *****

entries.name: Setting up of Zonal Museum
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Setting up of Zonal Museum
entries.purpose: Under this scheme, the upgradation of different museums such as Bhima Devi museum, Pinjore & Jayanti Devi Museum, Jind along with construction work for the site museum at Kunal, Fatehabad shall be taken, during the year.

entries.name: Setting up of State Archaeological Museum
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Setting up of State Archaeological Museum
entries.purpose: The department is going to set up a State Archaeological Museum at Sector-5, Panchkula where the office of the Department of Archaeology & Museum will also be located. The rare antiquities and priceless artefacts will be displayed in the museum. Also, the museum collection will comprise of archaeological finds such as sculptures, architectural pieces, metal objects, inscriptions, coins, seals-sealings, ceramics, decorative arts and arms & armours etc. Under this scheme, the provision of funds is required for procurement of furniture along with compactors of the State Archaeological Museum, Panchkula.

entries.name: Preparation of Plaster Casts of Ancient Sculptures and Antiquities
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Preparation of Plaster Casts of Ancient Sculptures and Antiquities
entries.purpose: This scheme is framed to popularize the cultural, historical and archaeological wealth of the State. The department prepares the plaster cast replicas of ancient sculpture and sells them on nominal rates. Due to their high artistic quality, these replicas always remain in great demand among the visitors who visit the different exhibitions conducted by the department. The scheme will be helpful to awaken the general public regarding rich cultural heritage and to stop illegal trading of Art objects. The department is also initiating the project for preparation of fibre replicas under this scheme.

entries.name: Protection/Preservation Development of Ancient Monuments Sites
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Protection/ Preservation Development of Ancient Monuments Sites.
entries.purpose: The objective of this scheme is to protect the Sites/Monuments professionally from further damage and restore to the previous state. Accordingly, the department is initiating a project for conservation work at all State Protected Monuments through PWD (B&R) Haryana. Under the scheme, the provision of funds is required for both the direct conservation/ restoration and essential civil works comprising construction of boundary wall, chowkidar Rooms, vegetation clearance, preliminary surveys, essential landscaping and Public Amenities etc. for various sites viz. Buddhist Stupa at Chaneti, Yamunanagar, the Tomb of Sheikh Taiyyab, Kaithal, the Tomb of Char Qutub, Hansi, Nahan Kothi, Panchkula, the Victoria memorial, Karnal and the Ancient Gumbad, Palwal among others.

entries.name: Archaeological Excavation Exploration programme
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Archaeological Excavation Exploration Programme
entries.purpose: The objective of this scheme is to excavate & explore the sites and remains so as to bring into light the archaeological wealth of the State and to provide material to reconstruct history. Under this scheme, the department conducts exploration on different archaeological sites followed by excavations. The sporadic explorations throughout the State will also be carried out to discover ancient sites and monuments. Excavations are done with the approval of Central Advisory Board of Archaeology (CABA). The benefit of the scheme is to promote hidden heritage.

entries.name: Haryana Tourism Corporation Limited
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Haryana Tourism Corporation Limited
entries.purpose: The Haryana Tourism Corporation is not only a commercial organization rather it has social obligations, being a Govt. Public Undertaking. Due to Covid-19 Pandemic, the Tourism industry was badly affected and Haryana Tourism Corporation was also not remained untouched as the financial health of the corporation got deteriorated and it requires a long time to come over it. Hence, the Government has decided to provide grant to Haryana Tourism Corporation Limited for the payment of salaries/ statutory payments/retiral dues etc. to their employees with an ultimate goal of boosting up the tourism industry in Haryana.

entries.name: Buildings(Youth Hostels)
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Buildings (Youth Hostels)
entries.purpose: Ongoing construction work and other new projects of Motilal Nehru Sports School, Rai are to be undertaken in this scheme & other works likely to be projected in the year 2026-2027 i.e. Annual RepairEstimate for Residential and non residential Building in MNSS, Raiand Rough Cost Estimates(RCE) for construction of Senior Boys Hostel “A” Block bathroom, R.C.E. for laying of sewer line in the campus of MNSS Rai, S/R by project design group 30 mm thick B.C. on various internal and external road in MNSS, RAI etc.

entries.name: Sports Infrastructure Scheme
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Sports Infrastructure Scheme
entries.purpose: The selected and identified construction work of Sports & Youth Affairs Department to build up Facilitation Centres, game specific centre of Excellence and Multipurpose indoor stadiums in each district with playing facilities in Basketball, Volleyball, Gymnastic, Boxing, Weight–lifting, Badminton, Wrestling, Kabbadi etc. & Youth Development Centre will be covered under this scheme for which estimated cost would be provided by the PWD (B&R) Department.

entries.name: Buildings (Archaeology)
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Buildings (Archaeology)
entries.purpose: Under the scheme, two major projects i.e. State Archaeological Museum at Panchkula, and Site Museum & Interpretation Center at Rakhigarhi, Hisar have been initiated. The construction work of State Archaeological Museum at Panchkula has nearly been completed and the internal development work including the area for display cases, electrical drawing, networking, facade lighting and other illumination of the building shall be taken during the year 2026-27. The vision for Site Museum & Interpretation Center at Rakhigarhi, Hisar is to share India’s heritage i.e. Ancient Civilization of Saraswati-Drasadvati valley through its unique site and collection with everyone. The construction work has nearly been completed and the external and internal development work is expected to be executed during the year 2026-27. Further, the construction work of Sant Ravi Dass museum at Kurukshetra and Sikh museum at Kurukshetra shall be taken during the year. *****

entries.name: Development of tourist facilities at District/Sub- Divisional & other important towns/places
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Development of Tourist Facilities at District/Sub Divisional and other important towns/places
entries.purpose: Under this scheme, funds are provided for the development of tourism infrastructure at the District Headquarter of State. The provision of funds have been made for the development work of Jyotisar Anubhav Kendra at Kurukshetra and construction/repair/renovation/upgradation of Rooms, VIP suites, Camper huts, Bar, Restaurant, Kitchen, General Toilets, Passage, Entrance Gate, Conference Hall etc. along with other allied works in various Tourist complexes of the state, during the year 2026-27.

entries.name: Air Conditioning and furnishing of new tourist complex
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Air Conditioning and Furnishing of new Tourist Complex
entries.purpose: Under this scheme, the provision of funds have been made for furnishing/ renovation of tourist complexes which includes the work of air-conditioning, purchase of equipment such as air-conditioners and D.G. sets etc. The machinery/ equipment/ furnishing of various complexes will also be upgraded/ modernized so as to keep in tune with the new trends of tourist and hotel trade.

entries.name: Development of Tourist Facilities along with main highways in Haryana.
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Development of Tourist Facilities along with main Highways in Haryana
entries.purpose: Under this scheme, the funds are provided for development of tourism infrastructure on the highways passing through the state. The provision of funds under this scheme have been made for the repair/renovation/upgradation of Rooms, VIP suites, Bar, Restaurant, Toilets, Passage, Minivet Huts, Conference Hall, Water Tank, Meeting Hall, Parking, Boundary Wall etc. and other allied works in various Tourist complexes along with main highways of the state, during the year 2026-27.

entries.name: Tourist facilities at Pinjore.
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Tourist Facilities at Pinjore
entries.purpose: The historic 17th Century Mughal Garden (now Yadavindra Gardens) at Pinjore with numerous facilities is a very popular tourist spot situated on Chandigarh-Shimla highway. The Gardens are also famous for its seven terraces and water fountains. A comprehensive programme has been taken up to develop this spot as a major tourist attraction. Under this scheme, the provisions of funds have been made for the installation of Tube well for water supply and Renovation/Upgradation of Yadavindra Gardens, Pinjore.

entries.name: Facilities at SurajKund
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Facilities at Surajkund
entries.purpose: The Surajkund Tourist Complex is situated just 8 Kms. away from Delhi (South), having facilities of Hotel, Hermitage, Restaurant, Bar, Conference Hall, Health Club and along with availability of Sprawling lawns at site. The Surajkund derives its name from an amphi-theatre (Sunpool) dating back to the 10th Century A.D. The Sunpool is an ancient Kund which was a part of Sun temple constructed there. Though there are now remnants of the Sun temple but the Sunpool (Kund) is existing in its original concept and shape. The Surajkund Tourist Complex is also famous for “International Surajkund Craft Mela” which is held every year in the month of February. This mela promotes Indian heritage and culture. The provision of funds under this scheme have been made for the Renovation of rooms, Construction of new rooms and for Land acquisition compensation court cases, during the year.

entries.name: Holiday & Recreation Resort at Badkhal Lake
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Holiday & Recreation Resort at Badkhal Lake
entries.purpose: The Tourist Complex at Badkhal, Faridabad (32 Kms. from Delhi) is a very popular resort for the residents of Delhi and Faridabad with its numerous attractions/facilities. The Tourist Complex was set up in the year 1973 around the beautiful natural lake. The provision of funds under this scheme have been made for upgradation of the campus with beautiful landscaping and construction of Hotel, Restaurant, Bar and Conventional Hall, during the year.

entries.name: Modernisation/Upgradation of training Institute under Swaran Jayanti Programme
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Modernization/upgradation of training institute under Swarna Jayanti Programme
entries.purpose: Haryana is the only State in the country where five Institutes of Hotel Management (IMH) at Kurukshetra, Rohtak, Faridabad, Panipat and Yamunanagar affiliated with the apex body of Hospitality Education i.e. National Council for Hotel Management & Catering Technology, Noida (set up by Ministry of Tourism, Government of India) is functioning. The provisions of funds have been made for the renovation and upgradation of 05 numbers Institute of Hotel Management (IHMs).

entries.name: Development of sites for Promotion of Sports/adventure Tourism and related activities
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Development of sites for Promotion of Sports/ adventure Tourism and related activities
entries.purpose: Under this scheme, the provision of funds have been made for the promotion of Adventure tourism and sports related activities at Tourist complexes situated at Morni, Sohna, Sultanpur, Hisar, Rohtak and Karnal. Besides this, wellness centres are proposed to be established at various Tourist complexes of the state, during the year.

entries.name: Development of sites for Promotion of tourism activities like festivals/fairs/shows and other related activities
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Development of sites for Promotion of tourism activities like festivals/ fairs/ shows and other related activities
entries.purpose: Under this scheme, the provision of funds have been made for the creation of temporary and permanent structures for organising International Crafts Mela at Surajkund, Mango Mela at Pinjore along with other fairs and festivals, during the year.

entries.name: Development of Wild Life Tourism in Haryana Under Swaran Jayanti Programme
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Development of Wild Life Tourism in Haryana under Swarna Jayanti Programme
entries.purpose: Haryana State is endowed with a rich and varied bio-diversity ranging from the Shivalik Hills in the northeast to the Aravali Hills in the south and over Yamuna-Ghaggar plain in the east to semi-desert sandy plain in the south-west. The Haryana Tourism plans to upgrade wildlife and nature tourism with modern facilities for tourists, by this, natural beauty of Haryana will be conserved & enjoyed by the public at large. Under this scheme, token provisions of funds have been made during the year 2026-27. *****

entries.name: Loans to Sports University of Haryana Rai, Haryana Sonipat
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Loans to Sports University of Haryana Rai, Sonipat
entries.purpose: The Government of Haryana has established “Sports University of Haryana” in Rai (Sonepat). The objective is to promote sports education in the areas of sports science, sports technology, sports management and sports coaching etc. besides functioning as the training center for elite players in selected sports disciplines by adopting best international practices. This scheme is non recoverable financial assistance in the form of interest free Perpetual loan. *****

entries.name: Mukhyamantri Muft Ilaaj Yojna
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Mukhya Mantri Muft Ilaj Yojana (MMIY)
entries.purpose: Under Mukyamantri Muft Ilaj Yojana, the following 3 components:- a). Mukhya Mantri Muft Ilaj Yojana was launched on 01-01-2014. Under this scheme there are 7 types of services being provided completely free to the general patients coming to the various health institutions of the State. 1. Surgeries– Nearly 231 various types of surgeries to Haryana residents. 2. Basic Laboratory Investigations – 69 investigations to the residents of Haryana. 3. X-Ray, ECG and Ultra Sonogram- free for all patients (wherever available in the Government Health Institutions). 4. Indoor Services are free for all patients (residents as well as non residents of Haryana). 5. Free OPD services to all the patients coming to health institutions. 6. Dental treatment – 23 dental procedures are being provided free for all. 7. Free Referral / Ambulance Services are provided to the eligible patients. After the pandemic of COVID is almost over the demand on the public health institutions has increased. Purchase of Lab reagents is being done through MMIY funds under NIROGI scheme as well. b). NIROGI Haryana is one of the flagship schemes of Government of Haryana, launched on November 29, 2022, which endeavors to provide comprehensive health checkup along-with mandatory laboratory investigations to Antyodaya population, once in two years. A web-portal was developed for coverage of peripheral health facilities; presently running in about 1609 health facilities & 1983 users are registered in the web-portal. Till September, 2025, total no. of beneficiaries screened are 95,88,985 & total no. of lab investigations conducted are 5,53,70,079. Total no. of Anganwadis covered are 25,907 in which 4,76,659 Antyodaya children have been screened. Also 14,136 Govt. Schools have been covered in which 7,25,350Antyodaya children have been screened. Laboratory investigations of Antyodaya beneficiaries is an integral component of comprehensive health checkups in NIROGI and up-gradation of laboratory services is in process. c). Mukhya Mantri Muft Ilaj Yojana for the PPP services is under: 1. To upgrade and strengthen the existing Govt. Health facilities for poor and needy population of Haryana, various diagnostic and therapeutic services like CathLab,CT/MRI, Dialysis are running under PPP mode. 2. Way ahead-to establish a. CT Scan facility at all District Hospitals. b. MRI facility at all District Hospitals. c. Cath Lab facility at all District Hospitals. d. Dialysis facility in all Sub-District Hospital. e. Tele ECG services upto PHC level. f. Ultrasound at all District Hospitals, Sub Divisional Hospitals and Community Health Centres is under process. 3. Free Categories- The following categories are free for CT/MRI & Dialysis services and the payment of these categories is done by district authorities. a. BPL+ Urban Slum Patients of Haryana b. Patients receiving Handicap Allowance from Haryana Govt. c. Poor patients who do not belong to any free categories. d. Patients belonging to SC Categories of Haryana. e. Patients belonging to economically weaker section of Haryana as per Haryana Government Reservation Policy. f. Unattended victims of Road Side Accident. g. Haryana Government employees, pensioners & dependents. h. People living with HIV(PLHIV)S.

entries.name: Out Sourcing of Support Services
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Outsourcing of Support Services
entries.purpose: The Government has spent large funds on the construction and up- gradation of various health facilities in all the districts and State of art medical equipment has been installed in these facilities. With the advancement in the medical technologies/ availability of modern medical gadgets, the medical facility is growing fast and in order to come up to the aspirations of Public, customer friendly atmosphere needs to be created. The State Government is committed to provide basic health facility at the minimum cost and reduce the out of pocket expenses of patients and attract public at large to the Government Health Institutions for treatment. It is essential to lay special emphasis on the upkeep/ maintenance of Government Hospitals, so that the cleanliness and sanitation is maintained, hygienic conditions prevail, good ambiance of landscapes, adequate maintenance services, uninterrupted supply of quality sterile articles through Central Sterile Supply Department (CSSD), uninterrupted supply of medical gases through Gas Manifold Services, Fire Safety Services etc. are ensured; the services of Cleaning & Sanitation, Housekeeping, Security, Electrician, Carpenter, Plumber, Landscaping etc. are outsourced under CS Policy. The total 13 Services have been covered under this scheme till date. This scheme has been successfully implemented in all the health institutions up to the level of CHC and it has been recently extended to all PHCs of the State.

entries.name: Grant-in-aid to Haryana Blood Transfusing Council Renamed as Grant-in-aid to various Health Institutions- N.A
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Grant-in-aid to Haryana Blood Transfusing Council Renamed as Grant-in-Aid to Various Health Institutions
entries.purpose: The Haryana State Blood Transfusion Council was registered on 12.7.1996 under Societies Registration Act. It is funded by the Government of India and State Government. With the launch of National Aids Control Programme-III w.e.f. July, 2007. Grant-in-Aid from State started from the year 2003-04. The following components are included under these schemes:- (a) Haryana State Blood Transfusion Council (HSBTC): is a society registered under Societies Registration Act. HSBTC has representation from all the stake holders i.e. Directorate of Health Services in the state , State Drug Controller, Department of Finance of the State/UT, Indian Red Cross Society, private blood Centers, NGO active in the field of securing voluntary blood donations. The HSBTC is responsible for overall implementation of all policy decisions for the Blood Transfusion Services (BTS) taken by the National Blood Transfusion Council, GOI. (b) Grant -in-Aid to New Saket Hospital, Panchkula:-The Mother Teresa Haryana Saket Council is provided grant-in-aid for running of Saket Hospital, Panchkula for pay, allowances, arrears, cost of medicines, equipments, operation theatre expenses, X-ray films and other services like maintenance of ambulance, electricity, water bills etc. Saket was established on 26th January,1957 with the objective to provide a package of integrated services to persons having Orthopedic disease & disabilities. (c) Grant-in-Aid for Keratoplasty: The scheme aims for providing to tackle corneal blindness, presently Rs. 7500/- per case for Keratoplasty from NHM funds (approved by Govt. of India) and Rs. 7500/- from State budget is given to NGOs and Private Practitioners registered under NPCB & VI. This scheme is available for all the residents of Haryana only and has been approved from Hon’ble CM Haryana w.e.f. 23.11.2017.

entries.name: Devi Rupak Rashtriya Utthan Evam Parivar Kalyan Yojna-N.A
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Devi Rupak Rashtriya Utthan Evam Parivar Kalyan Yojana.
entries.purpose: The sex ratio (females against 1000 males) of Haryana has declined from 870 in the year 1981 to 865 in the year 1991, to 861 in the year 2001 which is a point of major concern. Presently the sex ratio is 905 upto October 2024. In order to stabilize population of the State and to check the declining trend in the sex ratio, apart from already existing spacing and permanent methods, some innovative scheme is felt to be introduced in the State which can sensitize the community towards the need of adopting one child norm and spacing of children. It is important to promote these ideas especially among the newly wedded. A monthly incentive at the rates given below up to 20 years from the date of adoption of terminal method of Family Planning by either of the partner is given under the scheme:- Sr.No. Stage of adoption Incentive amount per month 1 At the birth of first girl child Rs. 500/- 2 At the birth of first male child Rs. 200/- 3 At the birth of second girl child Rs. 200/-
