entries.name: CHIRAYU-Families having income less than or equal to Ayushman Bharat Haryana Health Protection Authority
entries.name_in_the_narrative: CHIRAYU -Families having income less than or equal to 1.80 Lakh through Ayushman Bharat Haryana Health Protection Authority
entries.purpose: Ayushman Bharat Scheme was implemented in the State of Haryana on 15th August, 2018 for deprived categories as mentioned in SECC-2011 census database. Every Family figuring in defined Socio Economic Caste Census 2011 database will be entitled to claim benefits under the scheme. The Government of India guidelines provide a treatment cover of Rs. 5 lakh per family per annum on family floater basis and operational cost of Rs. 15.00 Crore covering 15.51 Lakh beneficiary families (identified through SECC 2011 database) of Haryana with no restriction on family size. The cost is being shared in 60:40 ratio by the Government of India and the Government of Haryana. The Hon'ble Chief Minister, Haryana has launched the Comprehensive Health Insurance of Antyodaya Units (CHIRAYU) Scheme on 21/11/2022 for the extension of AB- PMJAY benefits to the families having annual income less than or equal to Rs. 1.80 Lakh.

entries.name: Strengthening of District Ayurveda Offices- Establishment Expenses
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Strengthening of District Ayurveda Offices- Establishment Expenses
entries.purpose: Under this scheme the following sub-schemes are being implemented:- Establishment of District Ayurvedic Offices:- Most of the institutions of ISM&H are located in the remote rural areas. Govt. has posted District Ayurvedic Officers at each District to promote the ISM&H and to supervise and guide the existing dispensaries technically. At present all District Ayurvedic Offices are functioning in the State. The sanctioned posts for the offices of District Ayurvedic Officers are to be continued during the next financial year. Further, there are only four vehicles available at District Head Quarters (Rohtak, Hisar, Karnal and Gurugram). Most of the Government Ayurvedic dispensaries are situated in rural and remote areas. Therefore, there is an urgent need of vehicles for monitoring/supervision and checking purpose to District Ayurvedic Officers (DAOs). The vehicles for the District Ayurvedic Offices has already been hired as per terms and conditions of Supplies and Disposals Department. Establishment of Specialized Therapy Centre of AYUSH in PGIMS, Rohtak . The Government of India is laying a lot of emphasis on AYUSH with Indian Systems of medicines. Under NHM, Government of India has started a component for mainstreaming the AYUSH, where AYUSH services are being provided to people under one roof in all District Hospitals, CHCs and PHCs. In lines with this, in 2013, Government of India sanctioned establishment of specialized therapy centre of AYUSH in PGIMS, Rohtak. The posts created under this scheme are to be continued during the year 2026-27. Establishment of Specialised Therapy Centre of Ayush in Sector-9, Panchkula. As Panchkarma Therapies is Ayurveda’s one of the ancient and important purification and detoxification treatments. AYUSH Department has embarked upon a journey to treat life style diseases by setting up State-of-the Art Panchkarma Centres in all the districts. The Panchkarma Centre at Panchkula is one such centre. The Panchkarma facilities have been set up in Government Ayurvedic Dispensary, Sector-9, Panchkula to provide better Health facilities to the people of Panchkula town and surrounding areas. In this centre, Panchkarma therapies are being used to treat patients suffering from chronic diseases. As per decision a proposal to take over the Panchkarma Centres under the State Govt. scheme was sent to Government. At present 6 Panchkarma Centres are functioning at Panchkula, Thapli, Bahadurgarh, Karnal (Padha), Ambala Cantt. and Ambala City on Pilot Basis.

The Indian System of Medicine (AYUSH) has very important role to play in providing health care to the masses. This Department has planned to provide AYUSH Health Care facilities to the masses by drawing big plans/schemes through expansion of the Department. This scheme, the expenditure for salaries of staff posted at Head Quarter are incurred. Non-development schemes have also been merged in this scheme. At present, the directorate has 29 posts of different categories. Now, 4 more posts of Assistant Directors along with 2 Senior scale Stenographer and other ministerial staff have been

entries.name: Opening/Continuation of Homeopathic Dispensaries
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Opening/Continuation of Homeopathic Dispensaries
entries.purpose: The highest ideal of Homeopathy is to restore health rapidly, gently, permanently and to remove and destroy the whole disease in the shortest, surest, least harmful way according to clearly comprehensible principles. The Departments long term objective is to provide Health Care to the people of the State through increased number of Homeopathic Clinics by adding new ones every year. AYUSH dispensaries are very popular amongst masses due to adverse effect of Allopathic medicines and are, therefore, much accepted amongst the people of the State. The staff posted in these dispensaries are also fully involved in all the National and State Health Programmes. Now it is the policy of the Government of India to utilize the infrastructure of AYUSH at large for the Primary Health Care, RCH and other National Health Programmes. The Government is receiving more and more demands to open Homeopathic dispensaries in the Haryana State. The increased number of Homeopathic dispensaries will provide the better health facilities to rural population. At present 28 Homeopathic Dispensaries are running under this scheme.

entries.name: Purchase of Medicines for Scheduled Castes Patients in Hospitals
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Purchase of Medicines for Scheduled Castes Patients in Hospitals
entries.purpose: To provide basic health facilities to the SC patients of the State, it is the primary duty of the State Health Department to ensure adequate supply of essential life saving medicines to all the outdoor/indoor patients free of cost. Although population of the State has increased substantially over the years and the prices of medicines & consumables, linen, X-Ray films, Bandages, Anti-sera, Gloves, Dentals material, Suture material etc. have also increased many folds. Therefore, sufficient funds are required to provide various health facilities to the SC Patients of the State.

entries.name: Jananee Suraksha Yojna for Scheduled Castes
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Jananee Suraksha Yojana for Scheduled Castes
entries.purpose: Janani Suraksha Yojana (JSY) is a scheme of providing additional cash incentive to SC/ST beneficiaries per institutional delivery for promoting ante-natal care, institutional care during delivery and immediate post-partum period. The total expected population of Haryana in 2026 is 3.14crore. The projected population of SC for 2026 is 60,61,937. Additional cash incentive @ `1500/- per SC/ST beneficiary of JSY scheme is to be given in addition to the Centrally Sponsored JSY to around 33,334 beneficiaries.

entries.name: Strengthening of Ayruvedic/Unani/Homeopath ic Dispensaries/Prathmic Swasthya Kendra and Special Medicine for Women, Children and aged person
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Strengthening of Ayruvedic/ Unani /Homeopathic Dispensaries /Prathmic Swasthya Kendra and Special Medicine for Women, Children and aged person
entries.purpose: Under this scheme, the following components are being implemented. Opening/Continuation of Ayurvedic Dispensaries AYUSH Medicines are getting importance amongst masses due to adverse effect of Allopathic medicines. The staff posted in these institutions are also fully involved in all the National and State Health Programmes. Ayurvedic/Unani/ Homeopathic Dispensaries are so much acceptable to the people of the State that the Government is receiving more and more demands to open AYUSH Dispensaries in the State. 560 dispensaries already functioning under this component will continue its operations. The Government of Haryana has launched an ambitious flagship programme of Yog and Vyayamshalas in the State. In the first phase, 1121 Yog and Vyayamshalas are to make functional. This plan programme was being dealt by Sports and Youth Affairs Department, Haryana. Now the Government has decided Civil/non-civil furnishing of Vyayamshala and engagement of Yoga Volunteers to be dealt by the AYUSH Department Haryana in future. To make functional Yog and Vyayamshalas, 1000 posts of AYUSH Sahayak (on contractual basis) and 22 AYUSH Yog Coach (on regular basis) have been sanctioned. The demand of 1000 AYUSH Sahayak has been sent to Haryana Kaushal Rozgar Nigam out of which 852 are currently working. Recruitment of AYUSH Yog Coach is under process. To provide the AYUSH facilities at PHCs and Sub Centres of Health Department, new 1085 posts of AYUSH Doctors have already been sanctioned by the State govt. The appointment of 805 number of Ayurvedic Doctors is under process. Improvement of existing Ayurvedic/Unani/Homeopathic dispensaries - Special Medicine for Women, Children and Aged. At present, approximately 579 Government institutions of AYUSH are working in the Haryana. Most of these institutions are functioning in remote rural areas, where patients can get medicines of general ailments free of cost. Most of the deliveries in rural areas are non institutional in nature. In some cases, mother and infants require immediate medical care. To provide proper and timely medical care to women, new born children/ aged and others such as accidental and incidental cases, medicines are procured under this scheme for Government Ayurvedic Homeo and Unani dispensaries.

entries.name: Health Awareness through ISM & H through fairs with Medical Camps-N.A
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Health Awareness through ISM & H through fairs with Medical Camps
entries.purpose: ISM&H has important role in the Health Care Delivery System due to its positive preventive and curative aspects for the healthy life of the masses. Accordingly, there is a need to distribute IEC material of AYUSH to the masses through Fairs and Medical Camps in the rural areas besides special medical relief to the aged and needy persons. Govt. of India and State Govt. have also decided to celebrate International Yoga Day on 21st June, Ayurveda Day on Dhanwantri Day, Homeopathic Day on 10th April, Unani Day on 11th Feburary, Ambedkar Jayanti on 14th April, Poshan Maah in September and Naturopathy Day on 18th November every year to promote AYUSH system. 22 Health Fairs with Medical camps are to be held during 2026-27. National Health Programmes like Family Welfare, AIDS, Blindness, Malaria, RCH, MCH etc. will also be propagated in these proposed Fairs. Therefore, medicine, IEC material and office contingencies will be required for this purpose.

entries.name: Grant-in-aid to various Institutions/ Gram Panchayats
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Grant-in-aid to various Institutions/ Gram Panchayats
entries.purpose: The Council of Homeopathic System of Medicine, Haryana at Panchkula & the Council of Indian System of Medicine, Haryana at Panchkula have already been functioning in the State. The function of both the Councils is to register & to maintain the register of the practitioners as per their act and inspection of registered or un-registered practitioners under Haryana Homeopathic Practitioners (General) Rules, 1975 and the Punjab Ayurvedic and Unani Practitioners (General) Rules, 1965 respectively. State Govt. has established the Karamkar Board during the year 2018-19 and Haryana Yog Council during the year 2019-20. Now, Haryana Yog Ayog has been constituted in place of Haryana Yog Council during the year 2021-22. Above said Councils and Yog Ayog have no regular source of income and have to depend upon the Government to pay salary of the staff and other day to day expenditure. Following autonomous organizations are functioning under this scheme:- a. The Council of Homeopathic Systems of Medicine, Haryana, Panchkula. b. The Council of Indian Systems of Medicine, Haryana, Panchkula. c. Board of Haryana Health Care Workers, Panchkula. d. Haryana Yog Aayog, Panchkula.

entries.name: Shri Krishna Ayush University Kurukshertra
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Shri Krishna Ayush University Kurukshetra
entries.purpose: Shri Krishna Govt. Ayurvedic College, Kurukshetra has been upgraded as Shri Krishna AYUSH University, Kurukshetra. The University started its operations w.e.f. 1st March, 2018 in the existing campus of the Shri Krishna Govt. Ayurvedic College & Hospital, Kurukshetra. To establish the said University, 94 acre 5 kanal 1 marla land was identified in village Fattuhpur, District Kurukshetra which has been transferred in the name of Registrar, Shri Krishna AYUSH University, Kuruskehtra and the lease deed for the said land has been executed for 33 years.

entries.name_in_the_narrative: Continuation/improvement of Government Ayurvedic College/Government Ayurvedic Pharmacy/Drug Testing Laboratory, Kurukshetra and ISM&R Institute Panchkula
entries.purpose: Under this scheme, the following sub-schemes are being implemented:- 1. Baba Kheta Nath Govt. Ayurvedic College and Hospital, Pattikara Narnaul:- Ayurvedic Education is the important component of AYUSH System of Medicines. Education is a priority area and good education alone can produce good practitioners. At present only one Govt. Ayurvedic College namely Shri Krishna Ayurvedic College, Kurukshetra now merged in Shri Krishna AYUSH University Kurukshetra is providing the ayurvedic education in the State. To provide the better ayurveda education and health facilities in the State, Govt. of Haryana has decided to establish a Govt. Ayurvedic College at Village Pattikara (Narnaul) in the name of Late Sh. Baba Kheta Nath. For this purpose, Gram Panchayat Pattikara has provided the land. The construction of this college has been completed. The college will be started in a phased manner. In first phase Govt. has sanctioned 109 posts of hospital staff as per CCIM Norms in year 2017- 18.The OPD/IPD facility has been started in Baba Kheta Nath Hospital. The hospital of the said college and BAMS classes is already functional. 2. Government Homeopathic College & Hospital, Chandpura, Ambala Govt. Homeopathic College is being established in village Chandpura, District Ambala. The approval has been issued by Government dated 05.10.2020. The payment of Rs. 3.39 Crore in the favour of Municipal Corporation, Ambala for the land measuring 61 Kanal 13 Marla has been made. The land has been transferred in the name of AYUSH Department. The Administrative approval issued by the Government for the construction of College/ Hospital to PWD(B&R). 54 posts of Medical Superintendent, Senior Medical Officer(Homeopathic), Homeopathic Medical Officer and others staff have been sanctioned. 3. Government Unani College & Hospital, Akera, District Nuh The first Govt. Unani College & Hospital is being established in village Akera @ cost of Rs. 45.43 crore. The foundation stone has been laid down by the Hon’ble Chief Minister on 14.07.2018 and construction work is under progress and 48% work has been completed. 4. 50 Bedded AYUSH Hospital, Mayyar, Hisar The Government has sanctioned 50 bedded Hospital on 15 acre land in Village Mayyar Hisar. The administrative approval has been issued for the construction of buiding of this Hospital. The construction work is being executed by the PWD (B&R) Haryana and 85% work has been completed. The OPD in said college is already started. 5. Establishment of Government Ayurvedic Pharmacy To supply the pure and genuine medicines to patients, a State Ayurvedic Pharmacy is essential in the Government Sector. The purity of the medicine can be assured only by using tested raw materials in Government owned pharmacy. The building of the pharmacy has been completed with the financial assistance from the Central Government. 6. Setting up of State Drug Testing Laboratory Strict quality control over drugs is very essential for their efficacy and for consumer protection. To verify the claims of private pharmacies and to give public a fair evaluation of contents and potency of the drugs in question, a well equipped drug testing laboratory is essential. The Government of India has directed to setup drug testing laboratory in each State. The building of the Laboratory has been completed with the financial assistance from Central Government.

The main objective of the scheme is to provide education to the MBBS students and to provide medical facilities in the rural area surrounding the Institute. The hospital of Shaheed Hasan Khan Mewati Government Medical College was made operational in August, 2012 with 500 bedded facilities. At present, the college is running MBBS course with intake of 120 students per year, MD/MS course with intake of 46 Students and DNB course with intake of 43 and 27 PG students. Now, the hospital is fully operational with 645 bedded facilities. There is an OPD of approximate 1200-1500 patients per day, which is increasing day by day. entries.name_in_the_narrative: Buildings Renamed as Infrastructure/ Administrative Expenses
entries.purpose: Under this Scheme, It is a known fact that Public Infrastructure Development boots the productivity and leads to higher output. Construction of Public Health Infrastructure also does the same; it aids in overall improvement in the patient care. Every year the Health Department propose for building of new health infrastructure and construction is a continual process. Any major project viz a 200 bedded hospital takes at least 2 to 3 years for completion. Health Department Haryana has drawn up a gigantic scheme for the construction of building of health institutions both for the rural and urban areas. State Budget is required for construction of health facilities under Hon’ble CM announcements, Budget speech announcements, reconstruction of condemned buildings and newly approved health facilities. There are various infrastructure schemes of Govt of India such as Pradhan Mantri Ayushman Bharat Health Infrastructure Mission (PM-ABHIM), 15TH Finance Commission where additional support under State Budget is required. As per the cost estimates received from PWD(B&R) Development & Panchayats Deptt. and CPWD, for carrying out the construction of Health buildings. It is also expected that some new announcements will also be made. Major Projects which are proposed to be taken up in the FY 2026-27 are construction of new building of 300 Bedded Civil Hospital Hisar,100 Bedded Civil Hospital, Mandikhera; 400 Bedded Civil Hospital at Gurugram; 250 Bedded Additional Block Civil Hospital at Rewari ; 100 Bedded Additional Block Civil Hospital at Charkhi Dadri. Budget Speech Announcement shelter home facilities will also be provided for their companions. In this regards 5 district Hospitals (Sonepat, Charkhi Dadri, Ambala, Jind and Sirsa) to be taken up in 1st phase. PART-II- CENTRALLY SPONSORED SCHEMES (SHARING BASIS)

entries.purpose: Under this scheme, the youth affairs activities of the Department comprise sporadic adventure sports activities and intermittent activities of various voluntary organizations/ clubs like NSS, Scouts and Guides, NCC without any common thread running through these programmes and activities. Each year, a cash award of ₹ 20,000/- to Best District Youth, cash award of ₹30,000/- to Best District Youth Club, cash award of ₹40,000/- to Best State Youth and, similarly, cash award of ₹ 75,000/- is given to Best State Youth Club for their outstanding social works performed during the last three years. Apart from this, every year Ministry of Youth Affairs & Sports, Government of India provide National Youth Award to young men and women for their outstanding work in the field of national development and social service. The Department organizes camps for youth and offer them opportunities to participate in adventure sports like trekking, mountaineering, rock-climbing, skiing, rafting, water sports and paragliding under ‘Milkha Singh Adventure Sports Club’ which has been formulated vide notification dated 26.11.2021.

entries.name: Providing of mobile vans for facilitating the health care of the workers working in factories-N.A
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Providing of Mobile Vans for Facilitating the Health Care of the Workers Working in Factories
entries.purpose: The objective of the scheme is focused on providing Mobile vans for Facilitating of health care of workers working in the factories. Haryana is one of the most industrialized state in the country; with the pace of time, the industries are increasing and so are dangers in the form of occupational diseases. In order to diagnose occupational disease such as pneumoconiosis (silicosis, Baggiosis, NIHL, Skin, Eczema) etc., the medical examinations of the workers working in the factories and at the Construction sites is mandatory as per the provisions of the Factories Act, 1948 and the, Building and Other Construction workers Welfare Act, 1996 and Rules framed there under. As most of the occupational diseases are incurable at later stage, therefore, there is a great requirement for fully equipped Mobile vans equipped with X-ray machine, snellen chart, Ishihara Chart, Stethoscope, B.P. Apparatus, audiometer etc. in 5 districts of the State . 648 workers have been confirmed as suffering from occupational diseases and their treatment/rehabilitation assistance as per the Haryana Silicosis Rehabilitation Policy has been started. Drivers and technical staff required to operate the vans are available and tests are being done regularly.

entries.name: Strengthening of safety and Health Inspection system in the factories.
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Strengthening of Safety and Health Inspection System in the Factories
entries.purpose: The purpose of this scheme is to ensure the safety, health and welfare of workers working in the factories and construction sites by conducting the inspections under the Factories Act, 1948 and Building & Other Construction Workers Act, 1996 and Rules framed there under the field functionaries of Industrial Safety & Health Wing. Now, the inspection system is digitized and all the violations captured during the inspections have to be uploaded to the departmental portal within 24 hours of the inspection being conducted. Further, in order to enhance the quality and authenticity of the observations to be mentioned in the inspection report, the officers will have to capture each aspect of the observation by taking necessary photographs as evidence of proof. Further, in order to measure the earth resistance, illumination level, noise level etc., some electronic equipment will be required for the inspection.

entries.name: Rehabilitation of Destitute and Migrant Child Labour
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Rehabilitation of Destitute and Migrant Child Labour
entries.purpose: The concept of creation of Rehabilitation Centers is to address the needs of destitute child labour detected during the survey and surprise checks under the National Child Labour Projects. To uplift the livelihood of destitute children who migrated from other states in the vulnerability of being orphan, unaccompanied by any guardian or adult, poor health status, exposed to violence, social inequality, physical, mental and sexual abuse at work like situations. This situation has undoubtedly been grim since Covid-19. It is also understood that due to not being an adult, unawareness and lack of facilities, these children never get a chance of basic schooling, healthcare, social and legal counselling and skill to build and decide the course of their life. One Rehabilitation centre in Panipat is being run by the Department.

entries.name: Setting up Child Labour Cell for implementation of National Programme for Elimination of Child Labour- Establishment Expenses
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Setting up Child Labour Cell for implementation of National Programme for Elimination of Child Labour- Establishment Expenses
entries.purpose: The objective of the scheme is to eliminate the child labour to attain these goals, the Action Plan on Child Labour is being implemented by Labour Department. In the Child Labour Cell, an officer of the rank of Deputy Labour Commissioner along with the supporting staff, looks after this work of data collection, tabulation, monitoring and co-ordinate the work at Headquarter along with over-all health development of children in the State.

entries.name: Grant -in-aid for Social Security Board for Unorganized Workers
Computerization of Labour Department-Estbalishment Expenses
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Computerization of Labour Department– Establishment Expenses
entries.purpose: In this scheme IT mandate of the department is going to increase manifold in view of the roll out of the following Labour Codes and consequent operationization of the provisions from April, 2026 onwards:- 1. The Code on wages, 2019. 2. The Code on Social Security, 2020. 3. The Industrial Relations Code, 2020. 4. The Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, 2020. The major new aspects and areas where the IT footprint will be introduced is as followings:- i. Engagement of Project Management Unit for development of departmental portal for effective implementation of all online work under the Codes. ii. Maintaining the database or record for inter-state migrant workers electronically through portal under the Occupational safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, 2020. iii. Development of common application forms & software for availing different services as per the codes. iv. Computerization of complaint redressal system with tracking and monitoring from Headquarter, etc.

entries.name: Private Placement Consultancy and Recruitment Services (PPC&RSCs)-N.A
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Private Placement Consultancy and Recruitment Services (PPC&RSCs)
entries.purpose: The objective of the scheme is to facilitate placement activities in the Private Sector to provide employment opportunities to the unemployed youth of the State. All District Employment Exchanges organize Job Fairs on quarterly basis. These Job Fairs have been very effective in bringing unemployed persons and employers at one platform. The Employment Department acts as a facilitator between the employers and the applicants. Funds under the scheme shall be utilized for organizing 200 Job Fairs/Placement drives to provide job opportunities.

entries.name: Computerisation of Employment Exchange Operations
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Computerization of Employment Exchange Operations
entries.purpose: The objective of the scheme is computerization of employment exchange operations. In order to create a database and its proper utilization for various purposes, it is of utmost importance that comprehensive computerization is achieved in the Department. For that the services of the Department have been computerized and made available online through the portal www.hrex.gov.inand another website www.hreyahs.gov.in. All the Employment Exchanges have been finally computerized with all online services like Shaksham Portal, HRMS, SARAL, Grievance Portal and E-Office have been computerized in Employment Department. A 35 seater call center is running to outreach the candidates for data enrichment and information about job opportunities. *****

entries.name: Establishment of Haryana Skill Development Mission
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Establishment of Haryana Skill Development Mission
entries.purpose: Haryana Skill Development Mission has been constituted as per directions of Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship, Government of India. The Mission is imparting Short term Trainings, Recognition of Prior Learning(RPL) and Special Projects under various Job Roles. Under this scheme, setting up of 15 skill Centers will be initiated and skill training will be provided to 50,000 trainees during the year 2026-27.

entries.name: Drone Didi Scheme
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Drone Didi Scheme
entries.purpose: The aim of the Scheme is to provide drone pilot training through Drone Imaging and Information Services of Haryana at Karnal to train 4,000 sisters (approx.) of 400 women SHGs in order to upgrade their skills for drone operation & maintenance so that they can unlock new career avenues for their own professional development and can thus become self-reliant job creating entrepreneurs by working as Drone Entrepreneurs.

entries.name: Contractor Saksham Yuva Scheme
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Contractor Saksham Yuva Scheme
entries.purpose: The aim of the Scheme is to train and upskill 8,000 youths having Diploma or Degree qualification in Engineering so that they can unlock new carrier opportunities in the field of Engineering for their professional development leading to better entrepreneur avenues and enable them to perform as Work Contractor.

entries.name: Guru Shishya Kaushal Samman Yojana
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Guru Shishya Kaushal Samman Yojana
entries.purpose: Shri Vishwakarma Skill University, Haryana (SVSU) proposes to implement the State Scheme “Guru Shishya Kaushal Samman Yojana” for recognizing and certifying the Skill set of the Craftsmen, artisans and workers (such as plumbers, carpenters, masons etc.) in the informal sector, to formalize and acknowledge their skill through recognition of prior learning (RPL) and conducting (Train the Trainer) to recognize them as Trade Gurus and subsequent alignment of youth for skill-based apprenticeship training. There is a target to conduct RPL and Training of Trainer of 25000 craftsmen, artisian and workers to recognize them as Trade Gurus and alignment of 75000 youth as apprentices with Trade Gurus for skilled-based apprenticeship training. A minimum of 3 and maximum of 10 Apprentices are aligned with each Trade Guru. This Apprenticeship Certificate of three month will help them in self-employment or it can be linked to Government soft loans/micro finance schemes.

entries.name: Skill Training for Sheduled Castes students
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Skill Training for Scheduled Castes Students
entries.purpose: Under this scheme, skill training is provided to the youth of State making them able to get better job opportunities or for self-employment. Initially, skill training is provided to the weaker section of the society, 18 wings have been established. Further, 12 wings have been started in 15 Government ITIs (Mahendergarh, Bhiwani, Hisar, Piyau Majra, Barwala, Julana, Jind, Guhla-Cheeka, Sujapur, Palwal, Sirsa and Tankri,Moujabad, Kalayat and Mundlana) under Schedule Castes Sub Plan (SCSP).

entries.name: Entrepreneur Development Programme for Scheduled Caste beneficiaries
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Entrepreneur Development Programme for Scheduled Caste Beneficiaries
entries.purpose: For rapid economic development, it is expected from everyone to be a partner in the development process. It is necessary for the social and economic upliftment of SCs/STs, a booster dose in the form of special incentives to encourage them to become entrepreneurs and to start their own industrial service venture. It is proposed to organize Entrepreneurial Development Programmes with special focus on SC rural youth and women in each district of the State to educate them and make them aware of the requirements for setting up their ventures. Under this scheme, SC category candidates are specifically targeted to impart those EDPs. After obtaining the EDP Training, the SC/ST beneficiaries are provided loan under various schemes of the State as well as Govt. of India like Prime Minister Employment Generation Programme (PMEGP), under which the criteria is to provide loan to 22.50% SC/ST beneficiaries. The duration of the programme will be of four weeks. Thus, 1540 SC/ST beneficiaries will be trained under the Scheme in a year.

entries.name: Purchase of Plot for Office Building and Construction of Shram Shakti Bhawan at Panchkula
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Purchase of Plot for Office Building and Construction of Shram Shakti Bhawan at Panchkula
entries.purpose: This scheme is purposed to purchase plot and construction of “Sharam Shakti Bhawan” at Panchkula to consolidate Head Office and Haryana Building and Other Construction Worker's Welfare Board (HBOCWW). The cost will be borne by both the Departments, in the ratio of area occupied i.e. 7:5, respectively. For the purpose, the possession of plot has already been taken from Haryana Shehri Vikas Pradhi Karan, Panchkula in Sector 20 Panchkula.

entries.name_in_the_narrative: Construction of Rozgar Bhawan

ITI’s(Indri, Khewra, Shahbad, Sandhala-Sandhali, Jamba, Badopatti, PhuliaKalan, Barwala, Nalvi, Sisai, Pegan and Chuklana) and 1 existing Govt. Machinery, equipment and furniture is provided in the institutes as per norms prescribed by National Council of Vocational Training (NCVT) NCVT. In this regard, machinery, furniture, tools &equipments, computers & laptops, Digital Podium /smart board, Video conferencing system etc. will be purchased for 188 existing Govt. ITIs.

entries.name_in_the_narrative: Construction of Labour Court Complex
entries.purpose: The objective of the scheme is to construct court’s and office complexes for providing justice to the workers, management and trade unions of the factories in the State. As per CM announcement five Labour Court’s at Bawal, Sonipat, Jhajjar, Palwal and Rewari are to be established. PART-III CENTRAL SECTOR SCHEMES (100%)

There is a reservation for SC students in all the institutes being run under this Department, but there is a need to provide training to more youth of weaker section of society to make them economically self-sufficient.

entries.purpose: The Shri Vishwakarma Skill University, Haryana at village Dudhola, Palwal has been started in order to rollout National Skill Qualification Framework for providing the practical training in real world to evolve system for recognition of Prior Learning competency based on modular courses. The work of first phase of SVSU has been completed. This scheme is non recoverable financial assistance in the form of interest free perpetual loan. PART-III CENTRAL SECTOR SCHEMES (100%)

entries.purpose: Haryana Scheduled Castes Finance and Development Corporation (HSFDC) presently provides subsidy @50% of the project cost subject to maximum of ₹ 10,000/- to the BPL families under Bank tie-up and National Scheduled Castes Finance and Development Corporation (NSFDC) through funds received out of Special Central Assistance (SCA), whereas subsidy under National Safai Karamcharis Finance & Development Corporation (NSKFDC) assisted schemes is released out of funds received from State Government.

entries.name: Establishment of Haryana Scheduled Caste Commission
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Establishment of Haryana Scheduled Castes Commission
entries.purpose: The National Commission had directed the State Govt. to constitute a commission namely ‘Haryana State Commission for Scheduled Castes’, to safeguard the interest of Scheduled Castes and also to check and curb the atrocities being committed on Scheduled Castes. This Commission will investigate and examine the working of various safeguards provided in the Constitution of India or under any other law for the time being in force or under any order of the Government for the welfare and protection of the Scheduled Castes and to inquire into specific complaints with respect to the deprivation of rights and safeguards of the Scheduled Castes along with to take up such matter with the appropriate authorities.

entries.name: Administrative Subsidy to Haryana Scheduled Castes Finance and Development Corporation
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Administrative Subsidy to Haryana Scheduled Castes Finance and Development Corporation.

entries.name: Establishment of Haryana State Commission for Safai Karamcharis
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Establishment of Haryana State Commission for Safai Karamchari
entries.purpose: Haryana State Commission for Safai Karamchari has been constituted to investigate, examine and monitor all matters relating to the safeguards provided for the Safai Karamchari under the Constitution of India or under any other law for the time being in force or under any order of the Government and to evaluate the working of such safeguards. The Commission also advises on the planning process of socio-economic and educational development alongwith enquiring into specific complaints with respect to the deprivation of rights and safeguard of the Safai Karamcharis. Also, it holds seminars, debates and discussion on their problems, for creating public awareness.

entries.name: Establishment of Haryana Kesh Kala and Kaushal Vikas Board
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Establishment of Haryana Kesh Kala and Kaushal Vikas Board
entries.purpose: Haryana Kesh Kala and Kaushal Vikas Board has been constituted to revive and promote the Heritage, Continuity and Upgradation of art of hair grooming and to co-ordinate and assist in bringing new technologies in the profession of the traditional community. The objectives of the board are :- 1. To work for improvement of the traditional art of hair grooming and salon. 2. To suggest/advice the State Government for overall development of castes engaged in this traditional occupation. 3. To set up skill development facilities/co-ordinate the setting up of the skill development facilities in hair grooming, salon and other related activities which are being performed in the profession. 4. To suggest means and measures for the welfare of the professionals engaged in Kesh Kala. 5. To advice the State Government on the policies affecting the community directly.

entries.name: Establishment of Haryana Vimukt Ghumantu Jati Vikas Board
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Establishment of Haryana Vimukt Ghumantu Jati Vikas Board
entries.purpose: Haryana Vimukat Ghumantu Jati Vikas Board has been constituted to suggest proper categorization of various castes and to look into the developmental, economical and social issues regarding the Nomadic, Vimukt (De-notified Tribes) and Tapriwas Castes. The objective of the scheme is to suggest prospects of permanent settlement of shelterless Nomadic people of Haryana and to clarify/ suggest the proper categorization of various castes and to look into the developmental, economical and social issues regarding these castes.

entries.name: Research and Studies
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Research & Studies
entries.purpose: Research and Studies are conducted to know the actual impact of the departmental schemes and to study the inclusion/exclusion of various castes from the list. The Research and Studies are being conducted through private Agencies/Universities. As per terms and conditions of MoU, the payment is done directly to the concerned Agency/University.

The scope of this scheme has been enhanced from the year 2009-10 and the scholarship is being given in the following pattern in different classes under this amended scheme:-

entries.name_in_the_narrative: Subsidy for Administrative Expenditure to Haryana Backward Classes Kalyan Nigam
entries.purpose: To enable the Haryana Backward Classes & Economically Weaker Sections and to meet the administrative expenditure, a subsidy is provided to the Haryana Backward Classes & Economically Weaker Sections Kalyan Nigam under this scheme.

entries.name: Control of Drug Trafficking and setting up de-addiction centre in Haryana.
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Control of Drug Trafficking and setting up of De-addiction Centre in Haryana
entries.purpose: The prevalence and use of drugs, alcohol and narcotic substances has been increasing worldwide as well as in the country. The State of Haryana has also been affected by these unhealthy trends. It is commonly felt that consumption of drugs has increased in both urban and rural areas. As far as the State of Haryana is concerned, the use of type of drugs varies in different parts of the State. The victims of this abuse are the middle class and the poor, who just use various drugs for the sake of enjoyment for a short time and do not hesitate to spend their hard-earned money which has resulted in destroying families, and dissolution of marriages. Accordingly, in order to get rid of this severe problem, a scheme has been framed for treatment of the drug-addicts, their rehabilitation and taking preventive measures. The Government of India has formulated a scheme known as Central Sector Scheme of Assistance for Prevention of Alcoholism and Substance (Drugs) Abuse and for Social Defence Services. Accordingly, the State has also decided to make minimum criteria/benchmarks for various institutions like a Drug De-addiction Centres. It will supplement the Government of India Scheme wherever it falls short of the standards. This Scheme will aim at (i) setting up new model De-addiction Centres, (ii) Upgradation of the existing institutions by supplementing the funds received from Government of India. The aims and objectives of the scheme for prevention of alcoholism and substance abuse will be same as laid down by the Government of India.

entries.name: Financial assistance to non- school going differently abled children
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Financial assistance to non-school going differently abled children.
entries.purpose: Presently, Haryana Government is providing financial assistance in the form of scholarship to such disabled children of State who are below 18 years of age and are getting formal education in different schools, colleges, technical institutions, universities etc. Those disabled persons who are above 18 years of age are being provided financial assistance in the form of Disabled Pension. But there are some mentally retarded children in the age group of 0 to 18 years, who are in the category of profound & severe retardation and who are not able to attend formal education, training etc. due to their disability. They are totally dependent on their parents or relatives and need constant supervision and care of their families. Some of them require nursery care also. These children because of their severity of retardation are looked down upon in society and are also forced to live in deplorable and humiliating environment. Their parents find it difficult to look after them properly either due to financial difficulties or otherwise. Therefore, it is felt that in order to boost the morale of these children as well as provide support to their parents some financial assistance should be given to them for their welfare and respectful upbringing. Keeping this in view, a scheme named “Financial Assistance to the Non-School going Disabled Children” is implemented aiming at providing financial assistance, to such parents who cannot send them for formal schooling and boarding of their disabled wards in the age group of below 18 years because of financial constraints or because of their mental disability. The Government is giving assistance of ` 2400/- from 01.01.2024. The eligibility criteria is as under:-

entries.name: State Level Project/Home for Mentally Handicapped
entries.name_in_the_narrative: State Level Project/Home for Mentally Handicapped
entries.purpose: In Haryana, approximately 4.50 lakh children are Intellectually disabled and out of this, more than 50% fall in the category of educable and remaining 50% in the category of trainable group. Though a few special schools are being run by some voluntary organizations, yet it seems that these are not able to provide full facilities to the mentally challenged due to financial crunch or due to lack of Grant-in-Aid from funding agencies. These schools are providing educational facilities and elementary or vocational training to benefit the challenged of the limited area where these centres are situated. It is also observed that in these centres only Intellectually disabled are getting benefited and the children having cerebral palsy (complex, multi-challenged condition) are not getting benefited. These children also have number of other major impairment and locomotive disabilities. Therefore, to provide full rehabilitation facilities under one roof to the Intellectually Disabled children with cerebral palsy, a State Institute for Rehabilitation Training & Research (SIRTAR) has been established by the State Government at Rohtak. A total of 63 employees (25 Teaching+38 Non-teaching) have been engaged at the Institute and during the current academic year, a total of 145 students (110 Day scholars + 35 Hostellers) have been accommodated at the institute. Accordingly, it is essential to operate SIRTAR for their overall development of Mentally Retarded children. Under this scheme, the funds are required to provide full rehabilitation facilities under one roof to the Intellectually Disabled children with cerebral palsy and other major impairment and locomotive disabilities.

entries.name: Social and overall development of Rohnat Village
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Social and overall Development of Rohnat Village
entries.purpose: On 23.03.2018, Hon’ble Chief Minister, Haryana announced the formation of Rohnat Freedom Trust in village Rohnat, District Bhiwani. Village Rohnat had played a pivotal role in the freedom struggle of the country. During India’s First War of Independence in 1857, severe oppression was inflicted upon the villagers of Rohnat. The rebel sepoys from Rohnat village had broken the jail and released convicts and inmates due to which the British colonizers were furious and they invaded Rohnat, not sparing anyone, not even women and children. As a mark of completion of 160 years of such oppression, when on 20th July 1858, the land of the villagers of Rohnat was auctioned; the need to create a Trust has arisen. The Trust would strive to undertake various activities in the field of education, vocational and skill training, creation of assets and physical development of the village, healthcare, focused development of youth, women, elderly etc. so that the inhabitants of the village can enjoy the benefits of independence under full concentration and focus of the district administration.

entries.name: Operation of Maintenance and Appellate Tribunals for Senior Citizens under Haryana Maintenance of Parents and Senior Citizens Rules 2009
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Operation of Maintenance and Appellate Tribunals for Senior Citizens under Haryana Maintenance of Parents and Senior Citizens Rules 2009.
entries.purpose: In Indian culture, high importance is given to provide care and protection for parents and elderly but the virtual disappearance of traditional joint family system has contributed to the challenges faced by elderly. Now a days they are forced to live alone and are facing various kinds of the problems such as lack of physical, social, emotional and financial support. To overcome such difficulties and to face new challenges, the Government of India has enacted Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act, 2007 so as to provide maintenance and protection to parents and senior citizens. The basic objectives of the Act are to provide in-expensive and speedy procedure to claim monthly maintenance for parents and senior citizens. This Act casts obligations on children to maintain their parents/grandparents and also the relative of the senior citizen to maintain senior citizens. Under this scheme, the funds are provided for the payment of Honorarium/ Meeting Allowances/ Travelling Expenses of the non-official members of Maintenance and Appellate Tribunals and 22 Appellate Tribunals, having 03 members each (total 66 members) and 74 Maintenance Tribunals, having 03 members each (total 222 members).

entries.name: State awards for older persons
entries.name_in_the_narrative: State awards for older persons
entries.purpose: The Government of Haryana is making all efforts in providing social security to the senior citizens in the State. The percentage of persons above the age of 60 years among the total population is increasing. The joint family system has weakened and there is a marked trend in withdrawal of family support. It is the need of the hour to create such favorable conditions so that the senior citizens could spend rest of their lives with dignity and recognize their long services in various fields to the society in general.

entries.name: Establishment of Senior Citizen clubs in all Districts Urban Estates of Haryana
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Establishment of senior citizens clubs in all Districts Urban Estates of Haryana.
entries.purpose: Under this scheme, Day Care Centers/ Senior Citizen clubs and Senior Citizen Network Association are being established throughout the state wherein all old persons are coming for recreational, sports, counseling facilities etc. At present, there are 10 such centers and 3 Network Association in the state.

entries.name: Mukhyamantri Antyodaya Parivar Utthan Mission
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Mukha Mantri Antyodaya Parivar Utthan Mission.
entries.purpose: Each Government agency/department implements its own scheme independent of each other. Most schemes focus only on grants and assistance and are mostly output oriented and not outcome oriented. Therefore, in 2021 it was envisioned by the Hon’ble Chief Minister to have a program in ‘mission’ mode by organizing block/MC level Melas (Fairs) for convergence of all the income generation and employment generation schemes/programs that are being run by different government departments/agencies under an umbrella scheme called Mukhya Mantri Antyodaya Parivar Utthan Yojana (MMAPUY). It is a poverty alleviation program, initiated by the Haryana Government, with the objective of increasing the annual family income. For achieving the objective of the scheme, the information about different schemes of concerned Departments is given to the families by the Zonal Committees in the Antyodaya Gram Utthan Melas so that identified families can get registered with the concerned scheme and in turn increase their income. The data of these families then pushed and linked to one of the schemes from 51 schemes and services of 19 Departments.

entries.name: Financial assistance to Scheduled Castes families under Destitute Children Scheme
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Financial assistance to Scheduled Castes families under Destitute Children Scheme
entries.purpose: Under this scheme, a child under 21 years of age who has been deprived of parental support due to death, continued absence from the house for the last two years or father/mother has been imprisoned for a period not less than one year or physical or mentally incapacity of parents and whose parents/guardians income does not exceed `2.00 lakh per annum, is granted financial assistance but not more than two children

entries.name: Financial assistance to Kashmiri Migrants settled in Haryana
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Financial Assistance to Kashmiri migrants settled in Haryana
entries.purpose: This scheme is implemented w.e.f. 01.04.2006. Under this scheme, those Kashmiri families who have migrated from Jammu & Kashmir to Haryana and are living in various cities of Haryana are given financial assistance @ `1500/- per month per member of the family, subject to the maximum of ` 7500 per family w.e.f. 01.01.2024 where, each family is counted as one unit. The following are eligible:- (i) Kashmiri migrant family should be resident of Haryana. (ii) All the family members should stay together and will be treated as one unit. (iii) The maximum annual income from all sources should not exceed `2.00 lakh. Further, the total time period during which the financial assistance is given, for re-settlement is 5 (Five) years.

entries.name: Deen Dayal Lado Lakshmi Yojana
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Deen Dayal Lado Lakshmi Yojana
entries.purpose: The Lado Lakshmi Yojana aims to promote empowerment of women by fostering financial independence, ensuring social security, enhancing their overall well-being and participation in society. It focuses on empowering the most marginalized sections of society strengthen their financial autonomy. This scheme came into operation w.e.f. 25th September, 2025 and applicable throughout the state of Haryana. Under this scheme, a financial assistance amount to ` 2100/- per month (unless the beneficiary voluntarily chooses to take a lesser amount), or as revised and notified by the Government from time to time, will be given to the eligible beneficiaries as Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) through the Public Finance Management System (PFMS).

entries.name: Financial Assistance for stage III & IV Cancer Patients
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Financial Assistance for stage III & IV Cancer Patients
entries.purpose: This scheme is formulated to provide monthly Financial Assistance/ Pension to Stage III & IV Cancer patients (all age groups) of Haryana state. The Financial Assistance provided under this scheme will be in addition to the benefit being provided under any other Social Security Pension scheme, to the beneficiary. The Government is providing Financial Assistance amounting to ` 3000/- per month to the beneficiary and this scheme is implemented w.e.f. 08.12.2023.

entries.name: Financial Assistance to Acid Victims
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Financial Assistance to Acid Victims
entries.purpose: Acid attack victims means a person disfigured due to violent assault by throwing acid or similar corrosive substance as defined under Section 2(zc) “The Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016”. Under this scheme, the Women, Girls, Male and Transgender Acid Victims would be given monthly financial assistance where an application is filed either by the victim or by heir claiming on her behalf in cases, where the victim herself/himself is disabled to make an application, subject to the following conditions:- • The scheme will cover all acid attack victim’s (girls/women/Transgender) who are domicile / resident of Haryana • Submission of Medical Certificate/ copy of FIR, in support of the application.

entries.name: Pension to Eunucns
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Pension to Eunucns
entries.purpose: Keeping in view the pitiable economic condition of Eunuchs and being socially and economically deprived section of the society, it has been decided to give Financial help @ `3000/-per month per Eunuch, subject to the following conditions: 1. The applicant should be permanent resident/domicile of Haryana State and has been residing in Haryana State for the last 5 years at the time of submission of application. 2. The age of the applicant should not be less than 18 years. 3. The applicant must give a certificate from the Civil Surgeon in support of his application. 4. The applicant should not be involved in any unlawful activity.

entries.name_in_the_narrative: Rajiv Gandhi Pariwar Bima Yojana
entries.purpose: Rajiv Gandhi Pariwar Bima Yojana has been launched w.e.f. 1.4.2006 to give compensation of `1.00 lakh on account of death/permanent disability of a person of Haryana domicile. In other cases, `0.25 lakh to `0.50 lakh on the basis of disability percentage is also given. Coverage is given to all the persons of Haryana domicile between the age group of 18-60 years. As per provision in the Scheme, the claims are to be lodged with Sub-Divisional Officers (Civil) concerned, who are the Nodal Officers under the scheme. This scheme is discontinued w.e.f. 31-03-2017. The funds are required to clear the pending cases.

entries.name: Dr.Shyama Prasad Mukherjee Durghatna Sahayta Yojana
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Dr. Shyama Prasad Mukherjee Durghatna Sahayta Yojana.
entries.purpose: “Dr. Shyama Prasad Mukherjee Durghtana Sahayata Yojana” was launched w.e.f. 01.04.2017. The scope of coverage under the new scheme was limited to those Haryana domiciles and residents of Haryana who were not able to avail the benefit under Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana whether due to non enrolment or otherwise. The benefit admissible under the “Dr. Shyama Prasad Mukerjee Durghtana Sahayata Yojana” was `1.00 lakh. Any person in the age group of 18 to 70 years domicile and resident of Haryana was eligible under the Scheme, provided the person was not enrolled at the time of accident under the Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana (PMSBY). This scheme is discontinued w.e.f. 31-03-2020. The funds are required to clear the pending cases.

entries.name: Ladli (Social Security Pension Scheme) for scheduled castes
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Ladli (Social Security Pension Scheme) for Scheduled Castes
entries.purpose: To remove the sense of economic insecurity from the mind of parents who have only daughters, a Scheme on the pattern of Old Age Allowance scheme, has been started w.e.f. 1-1-2006. Under this scheme, a sum of `3,000/-per month per family is paid from the 45th birthday of father/mother. Under this scheme, any family where biological single parent/ parents are domicile of Haryana or working for Government of Haryana and have no son, biological or adopted, but only daughter/daughters are eligible to get financial assistance.

entries.name: Pension to Differently abled Persons for (Scheduled Castes)
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Pension to Differently Abled Persons for Scheduled Castes
entries.purpose: To provide social security to Disabled persons, the scheme namely ‘Haryana Disabled Pension scheme’ was introduced in the year 1981-82. The aim of the scheme is to provide social security to disabled persons who are unable to sustain themselves from their own resources and are in need of financial assistance. The rate of pension, which was `50/- per month at the beginning of the scheme has now been enhanced to `3000/- per month w.e.f. 01.01.2024. Eligibility Criteria : 1. Age group of 18 years and above. 2. Must be domicile of Haryana and has been residing in Haryana state for the last 3 years at the time of submission of application.

entries.name: Financial assistance to Destitute Women and Widows (Scheduled Castes)
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Financial assistance to Destitute Women and Widows (Scheduled Castes)
entries.purpose: The Haryana Pension to Widows and Destitute Women scheme was introduced in the year 1980-81. The aim of the scheme is to provide social security to women who are unable to sustain themselves from their own resources and are in need of Financial Assistance. Under this scheme, a widow woman in the age group of 18 years and above is eligible for grant of widow pension if she is a domicile of Haryana for 15 years and has been residing in Haryana state for the last one year at the time of submission of application and her own income from all source is not more than `3.00 lakh per annum and if she fulfills any of the three conditions :- 1. If she is a widow; 2. If she is destitute without husband, parents and son(s); 3. If she is destitute due to desertion or physical/ mental incapacity of, i) Husband in case of married women, or ii) Parents in case of non-married women. Further, notwithstanding the above, a women employed by any Government or by Local/ Statutory Body or organization substantially financed by any Government or Local/ Statutory Body or who is drawing pension or Family Pension are not eligible under this scheme.“Pension “wherever occurring in any Government Notification concerning Social Security Benefits means and includes, income received or accrued from accumulated earnings, including schemes. The Government is giving financial assistance of `3000/- per month from 01-01-2024. Further, under this scheme (General component), a financial assistance amounting to `3000/- per month w.e.f. 01.01.2024 is being given to Widower and Unmarried persons of the state, who have attained the age of 40 years, subject to other eligibility conditions.

entries.name: Old age Samman Allowance for Scheduled Caste
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Old Age Samman Allowance for Scheduled Castes
entries.purpose: To provide Social Security to Old Persons who are unable to sustain themselves from their own sources and are in need of Financial assistance, Old Age Pension Scheme was initially started w.e.f. 01.04.1964 during Joint Punjab. The rate of pension, which was ` 15/- per month at the beginning of the scheme was enhanced from time to time. Any person is eligible for grant of Old Age Samman Allowance if, 1. The person is of age 60 years or above, 2. The person is domicile and resident of Haryana state for last 15 years and his/her income from all source together with that of his/ her spouse does not exceed `3.00 lakh per annum. 3. To have Parivar Pehchan Patra (PPP) Further, notwithstanding the above, any person receiving pension from any Government or Local/ Statutory Body or organization substantially financed by any Government or Local/ Statutory Body are not eligible under this scheme. The Government is giving financial assistance of `3000/- per month from 01-01-2024. Further, under this scheme (General component), a financial assistance amounting to `3000/- per month w.e.f. 01.01.2024 is being given to persons suffering from Rare Diseases and recipients of Padma Awards, subject to other eligibility conditions.

entries.name_in_the_narrative: Purchase of Land/Construction of Office Building/ Sainik Sadan/Museum Hall
entries.purpose: A plot of land measuring 938 sq. meter has been allotted by Haryana Shehri Vikas Pradhikaran (HSVP) for the establishment of office building of Sainik and Ardh Sainik Welfare Department, Haryana. This Department is in the process of constructing office building of District Sainik and Ardh Sainik Welfare Office, Museum and Hall at Sector-12 Panchkula and Sainik Sadans at various Districts.

entries.name_in_the_narrative: Construction of Kalyan Bhawan and Hostel
entries.purpose: Kalyan Bhawan is constructed in Sector-2, Panchkula in which the office of (i) Directorate of Welfare of Scheduled Castes & Backward Classes Department, (ii) Haryana Scheduled Castes & Financial Development Corporation, Haryana will be housed. Under this scheme, the construction work of Hostel at Faridabad and Panipat shall be taken, during the year.

entries.name: Share Capital to Haryana Backward Classes Kalyan Nigam.
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Share Capital to Haryana Backward Classes Kalyan Nigam
entries.purpose: The State Govt. has set up a Backward Classes and Economically Weaker Section Kalyan Nigam (HBCKN) for the socio-economic development of Backward Classes in the year 1980. The main objective of the Nigam is to uplift people belonging to Backward classes, minority communities and persons with disabilities. At present the Nigam, being state channelizing agency is implementing income generating scheme in collaboration with three National Corporations i.e. National Backward Classes Finance and Development Corporation, National Minorities Development and Finance Corporation and National Divyangjan Finance and Development Corporation. Under the scheme, the amount of share capital is used while disbursing loan to the beneficiaries as contribution of the Nigam.

entries.name: Performance Linked Outlay (PLO) for Social Justice and Empowerment ( SJE-PLO- CAP)
Purchase of Institutional plot for construction of building of Directorate (Swaran Jayanti)
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Purchase of Institutional plot for construction of building of Directorate (Swarna Jayanti).
entries.purpose: The Directorate office of the department is being run in a rented building in Sector -17 A, Chandigarh. A plot for the construction of Directorate building had been purchased at Sector-17A, Panchkula in FY 2019-20. In FY 2023-24, Welfare of SCs & BCs department has been merged with Social Justice & Empowerment department which is now called SEWA department and their Head Quarters are located at Panchkula & Chandigarh respectively. After merger, SEWA department wants to shift both departments in a single building and according to the sitting capacity of both departments, the size of purchased plot is not enough. Now, the department is doing correspondence with HSVP for purchasing of a new plot with size of 1.00 acre and if the department gets this new plot, then the already purchased plot will be surrendered and the funds will be required for purchasing of new plot & construction of Directorate building. In addition to above, the process of construction of Life Long Care Home at Ambala has also been started.

entries.name: G.I.B Panipat (Boys/Girls)
entries.name_in_the_narrative: G.I.B. Panipat (Boys/Girls)
entries.purpose: Government Institute-cum-Braille Library for the Blind Boys, Panipat is being run with the aim to provide education and training to such blind children who do not have adequate means for the maintenance, education or training, so as to enable them to become self-sufficient. This institute also has hostel facility for boys which was in bad shape. During the year 2016, PWD was asked to re-build the same building. Building work has been completed and taken by department. Under this scheme, the provision of funds have been made for construction of Government hostel for boys at Panipat as per CM announcement.

entries.name: Home for Aged and Infirms Rewari, (Swaran Jayanti Project) Renamed as Old Age Homes
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Home for Aged and infirms, Rewari, (Swarna Jayanti Project) Renamed as Old Age Homes
entries.purpose: An institution for the destitute, aged and infirm persons of the age of 65 years or above in the case of men and 60 years and above in the case of women having no means of livelihood, is functioning at Rewari. As per ‘Haryana Maintenance of Parents and Senior Citizen Act, 2007’, the Old Age Homes needs to be built up in every district of Haryana by 2024, to accommodate a minimum of 150 senior citizens in each Old Age Home. Several district identification of land/transferring of land cases are in the pipeline. At present, there are 14 inmates in their Home which are likely to be increased up to 100. The inmates are provided free boarding, lodging and other facilities like medical aid etc. free of charge. PART-III CENTRAL SECTOR SCHEMES (100%)

entries.name: Road safety Awareness & Computerization of Regulatory wing
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Road Safety Awareness & Computerization of Regulatory Wing
entries.purpose: The objective of the scheme is to ensure Road Safety of the citizens and Computerization of Regulatory Wing. This can be achieved by organizing Road Safety Programmes, Workshops and other activities from time to time to reduce the number of fatalities and accidents. Beside this, the department is exhaustively dedicated to provide online services to the citizens of the State in transparent manner for which Vahan and Sarathi Softwares have been integrated on Saral Portal. Funds are required for providing various online services like payment of smart card based learner/driving license, new registration certificate and other co-related services.

entries.name: Mukhya Mantri Shehri Awas Yojana
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Mukhya Mantri Shehri Awas Yojana
entries.purpose: In order to meet the housing demand of needy families residing in Urban areas in the State, the Department of Housing For All has prepared a policy namely Mukhya Mantri Shehri Awas Yojana (MMSAY) for providing one Marla (30 Sq. Yard) plot to the needy identified families having verified annual income upto `1.80 lacs as per Parivar Pehchan Patra (PPP). In the first phase the Department has allotted 1 Marla (30 sq.yrds.) plots at the cost of `1.00 lac to 15,256 beneficiaries belonging to the categories of GhumantuJati, widow, SCs and others at 14 locations i.e. Charkhi-Dadri, Fatehabad, Jhajjar, Karnal, Panchkula, Mahendragarh, Sirsa, Sonipat, Palwal, Rohtak, Rewari, Julana, Safidon, Yamunanagar and provisional allotment letters have been allotted to the beneficiaries in a State level function. In the second phase process is ongoing for 15251 plots in 16 towns/cities, where in 7804 applicants booked their plots by depositing a booking amount of Rs. 10000. HSVP is in process of taking necessary administrative approvals and preparing detailed cost estimates for all 14+16 locations for development of physical infrastructure works i.e. roads, water supply, sewerage, street light etc.

entries.name: Mukhya Mantri Gramin Awas Yojana
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Mukhya Mantri Gramin Awas Yojana
entries.purpose: In order to meet the housing demand of needy families residing in Rural areas in the State, the Department of Housing For All has prepared a policy namely Mukhya Mantri Gramin Awas Yojana-Extension (MMGAY-E) for providing 50Sq. Yd. plots in Mahagram Panchayat and 100 Sq. Yd. plots in regular Panchayats to the needy identified families having verified annual income upto `1.80 lac as per Parivar Pehchan Patra (PPP). To register the applicants, a portal has been created by the Department of Housing For All. In year 2024-25, 4002 eligible families from 62 Gram Panchayats have been allotted plots and provisional Allotment letter of 100/50 sq.yds. A provision has also been made to provide financial assistance of ₹ 1.38 lakh to these beneficiaries for construction of their pucca house under PMAY-Gramin. In 2nd phase, 8029 applicants of 143 GPs (141 other GPs + 2 Mahagram Panchayats) of 15 districts have been provided plots through draw of lots on 14.10.2025. This Workshop is meant for the maintenance of trainer/advanced aircraft in order to provide self-sufficiency in the matter and to keep the maximum Aircraft and glider serviceable.

entries.name: Swaran Jayanti Integrated Aviation Hub at Hisar
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Swaran Jayanti Integrated Aviation Hub at Hisar
entries.purpose: Hisar Aerodrome will be elevated as an International Airport. The Haryana Government was having 180 acres of land at Hisar Aerodrome and additional 7000 acres of land adjoining the existing Aerodrome at Hisar has been occupied for the development of Integrated Aviation Hub at Hisar. The development work of the project is being planned in phase wise manner. The construction work under Phase-II of the project is in progress. In the second phase, along with the expenditure on extension of Runway and Taxiway Track Apron at Hisar Airport, various buildings, infrastructures, Drainage Works, specialized equipments and vehicles shall be required to be procured and necessitated for the commissioning of the Airport.

entries.name: Maintenance of Aerodromes

entries.purpose: This Scheme is mainly devised to create modern infrastructural facilities for providing flying training facilities and to establish Regional Air Connectivity services at the Civil Aerodromes/Airstrips located in the State at Bhiwani, Karnal, Narnaul and Pinjore. In addition to this, presently, Department is developing Ambala Airport as well as Heli-hub at Gurugram. For this basic development/construction works is required to be carried out at these Civil Aerodromes/Airport/Heli-hub in a phase-wise manner. In addition to this, Gurugram Heli-Hub is to be established for which at least 18.16 Acres land has been identified and budgetary provision also required for security equipment, Shooting range, restructure of buildings, civil works and AAI works for operations at Ambala Air Enclave. *****

The existing crusts of State Highways require strengthening to bear the onslaught of increased traffic. Some sections of Highways require widening for increasing capacity. This has been necessitated for the construction of road works improvement & Up- gradation of State Highways in Haryana. Out of which, 435 Kms. are under National Capital Region as these kilometer of roads of Haryana in NCR region serve as corridor routes for interstate traffic comprising of 13 Districts namely Gurugram, Faridabad, Nuh, Palwal, Rewari, Rohtak, Karnal, Panipat, Jind, Sonepat, Jhajjar, Bhiwani & Mahendergarh, which is 66% of the area of the State.

entries.name: Creation of Urban Infrastructure under Urban Infrastructure Development Fund (UIDF) of National Housing Bank
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Creation of Urban infrastructure under Urban Infrastructure Development Fund (UIDF) of National Housing Bank.
entries.purpose: Urban Infrastructure Development Fund established through priority sector lending shortfall and to be sued by Public Agencies to create Urban Infrastructure in Tier 2 & Tier 3 cities. The fund will be managed by Nation Housing Bank. The fund will be used by public agencies to create Urban Infrastructure in Tier-2 and Tier-3 cities. UIDF aims to supplement efforts for Urban Infrastructure Development works implemented through Public/State Agencies. Municipal Corporation, Urban Local Bodies in Tier-2 and Tier-3 cities by providing a stable and predictable source of financing. entries.name: Installation of Solar Water Pumping System in the State
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Installation of Solar Water Pumping System in the State
entries.purpose: This is a NABARD aided scheme introduced during Financial Year 2018-19. Under this scheme, Solar Water Pumping Systems are provided to the farmers with 75% subsidy (30% MNRE+45% State) under Pradhan Mantri Kisan Surakshaevam Utthaan Mahabhiyan (PM KUSUM). About 65.2 % population of the State lives in the rural area and agriculture is the mainstay of their livelihood. Renewable Energy sources are available in abundance and these are sufficient to meet energy demand for irrigation. Medium and Small Farmers in the State are using diesel pump sets to irrigate their fields. These pumps create pollution and affect the climate. Solar Pumps are very useful for meeting the irrigation needs of the farmers and are pollution free. Once the system is installed, there are no recurring & running expenditure in their day to day working, thus helping these small farmers in earning sustainable income from their farming. Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE), GOI has empanelled firms for the supply, installation and commissioning of 3 HP to 10HP capacity solar water pumping system. The Govt. has proposed 35,000 solar water pumping systems for providing the same to the farmers with 75% subsidy (State+MNRE) for the year 2026-27. Eligibility Criteria: I. Individual farmers will be supported to install standalone solar agriculture pumps of capacity up to 10 HP for replacement of existing diesel agriculture pumps/irrigation systems in off-grid areas, where grid supply is not available. II. Water User Associations, Gaushalas and community/cluster based irrigation system will also be covered under this component. However, priority would be given to small and marginal farmers. III. These solar water pumping systems will only be provided to the farmers who opt for micro-irrigation (drip/sprinkler) and/or Under Ground Pipe Lines (UGPL) in their field. Type/Mode of Benefit: Upfront subsidy @75% of pump cost is provided to eligible categories only for irrigation purpose. a) Long term objective To reduce the dependence on conventional power and to replace diesel pumps so as to save the environment. b)Medium term From 2020-21 to 2025-26, 1,78,372 solar water pumps objective with capacity ranging from 3-10 HP were installed. (5 years horizon) c) Annual objective Keeping in view the demand for solar pumps, 35,000 solar &impact expected water pumping system are proposed to be installed during the year 2026-27.

entries.purpose: The State Mini Cluster Development Programme scheme under HEEP-2020:- The State Government has adopted the cluster development approach as a key strategy for enhancing the productivity and competitiveness as well as capacity building of Micro & Small Enterprises (MSEs) in the State. A cluster is a group of enterprises located within an identifiable and as far as practicable, contiguous area and producing same/ similar products/ services. The essential characteristics of enterprises in a cluster are (a) Similarity in the methods of production, quality control and testing, energy consumption, pollution control, etc. (b) Similar level of technology and marketing strategies/practices (c) Open channels for communication among the members of the cluster (d) Common challenges and opportunities. The objectives of the scheme are as under : (i) To support the sustainability and growth of MSMEs by addressing common issues such as improvement of technology, skills and quality, market access, access to capital, etc. (ii) To set up common facility centers (for testing, design, R&D, training centre, effluent treatment, complementing production processes, etc.)

But, GoI discontinued the central component of ASIDE scheme w.e.f. 01.04.2015. Accordingly the State Government decided to continue the ASIDE Scheme and a new Scheme namely “State Industrial Infrastructure Development Scheme (SIIDS)” was launched by the State Government vide Notification dated 12.06.2018 with an objective to create/upgrade the Industrial Infrastructure in the State. The Haryana Enterprises & Employment Policy, 2020 has been notified on 29.12.2020 by the Government of Haryana whereby several schemes of Incentive & Infrastructure were formulated. One scheme namely ‘State Industrial & Infrastructure Development Scheme (SIIDS)’ was formulated. It was decided by the Higher Authority that new projects sanctioned under SIIDS will be dealt by MSME and the old ongoing projects sanctioned till date under EPP-2015 will continue to be dealt by the Directorate of Industries.
