entries.name_in_the_narrative: Haryana Aatma Nirbhar Textile Policy
entries.purpose: To enhance the growth of the state’s already robust textile sector and provide a comprehensive support framework for the textile industry in the State to grow, innovate and enhance employment opportunities for the State’s youth, the State Government has notified the new “Haryana Aatma Nirbhar Textile Policy 2022-25 (now extended) which aims to foster an ecosystem of self-reliance and innovation by offering a robust incentive framework for backward integration-enhanced production of manmade fibres, promoting circular economy, attracting investments in weaving, knitting, processing, readymade garments, apparel making, technical textiles, integrated units, textile parks, textile clusters, etc. with special emphasis on value addition, employment generation and productivity enhancement. The “Haryana Aatma Nirbhar Textile Policy is in line with the 5F vision of our Hon’ble Prime Minister of India - Farm to Fiber to Factory to Fashion to Foreign. Objectives:- The policy aims to provide an impetus to diversification of Haryana’s textile industry to the ‘B’, ‘C’ and ‘D’ category blocks and on the promotion of sunrise sector within textile i.e., technical textiles, circular economy, backward integration, etc. Technical textiles are the textile material and products manufactured primarily for their technical and performance properties rather than their aesthetic or decorative properties/ characteristics. Examples of technical textiles are Airbags, helmets, bullet proof jackets, parachute fabrics, sports net, shade nets, fishing nets, floor & wall coverings, umbrella cloth, mattress, conveyor belts, diapers, sanitary pads, etc. The key objectives of the Haryana Aatma Nirbhar Textile Policy 2022-25 include: (i) To attract investment in the textile sector to the tune of ` 4000 crore. (ii) To generate 20,000 new jobs in the textile sector across the value chain

entries.name: VAT Assistance in operating Industries on cleaner fuel
entries.name_in_the_narrative: VAT Assistance in operating Industries on cleaner fuel
entries.purpose: The Government recognizes that industries in the Haryana are being pushed to shift to cleaner fuels including natural gas due to concerns arising from the severity of air pollution. The shift would increase the cost of production for industries affecting their competitiveness. To help them remain competitive, 50% reimbursement on VAT collected on natural gas (piped or compressed) from industries in the MSME, Large, Mega and Ultra-Mega on fuel cleaner for a period of two years. This is in recognition of the need to promote industrial development within the principle of sustainable development. i) To promote a clean environment and support sustainable development in the State using cleaner fuels. ii) To incentivize and encourage Industries to use ecologically friendly PNG/CNG/LPG in industries. iii) To assist Industries in compliance mandated by Commission for Air Quality Management in National Capital Region and Adjoining Areas (CAQM). To provide support to the industries from the MSME sector located in NCR districts of Haryana in conversion of Coat/Diesel boilers to PNG/CNG/cleaner fuel boilers, the Government of Haryana has notified the Scheme of "Assistance in conversion of boiler to run on cleaner fuels”. The conversion cost of industries towards cleaner fuels requires investment in infrastructure. In order to provide support, Hon'ble Chief Minister of Haryana announced in his Budget Speech 2022 that MSME sector located in NCR shall be provided an assistance of 30% of the capital expenditure for conversion of their boilers from coal or diesel to cleaner fuels subject to a limit of ` 15 lakh. This will enable these industries to move towards compliance and fulfill their obligations towards a cleaner environment.

entries.name: Bureau of Industrial Policy and Promotion (B I P P)
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Bureau of Industrial Policy and Promotion (BIPP)
entries.purpose: The Investment Promotion Centre (IPC) constituted under the Haryana Industrial Promotion Act, 2005 was renamed as the Bureau of Industrial Policy & Promotion (BIPP) with its offices at Delhi & Chandigarh. The objective of BIPP is to act as a Single Point Contact Agency to provide information, guidance & hand-holding services for prospective entrepreneurs, continuous engagement with the industry in ongoing basis, tracking investment proposals, investment promotion, converting investment queries into investment commitments, participating in fairs/summit organised by ITPO and other leading organisations at National and International Level to show case the policies & achievements and printing of industrial literature for the guidance of entrepreneurs. The main objective of BIPP is to attract investment in the State and to provide facilitation to the entrepreneurs. The officers not below the rank of Divisional Town Planner, Assistant General Manager Haryana State Industrial & Infrastructure Development Corporation Ltd., Environment Engineer, Assistant Director Industrial safety, Deputy General Manager Uttar Haryana Bijli Vitran Nigam, Deputy General Manager Dakshin Haryana Bijli Vitran Nigam, Joint Director Industries, consultants, professionals from the consultancy firms or such other officers as recommended by the Chief Executive Officer/Director or Director General Industries & Commerce Department with the approval of State Government shall be part of the Bureau of Industrial Policy and Promotion (BIPP). The expenditure on office contingency, advertisement, publicity, printing of literature, stationery etc. is borne from the funds provided by the State Government to BIPP under the scheme. Additionally, the Department is in process of empanelment of new PMU for measuring Cost of Regulation (CoR) and planning extensive outreach & promotional activities to strengthen the startup ecosystem in the State, scheduled for January 2026 and April-May 2026.

entries.name: Grant-in-aid to Haryana Mitti Kala Board
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Grant in Aid to Haryana Mitti Kala Board
entries.purpose: Haryana has been an industrially fast developing State and has good performance to its credit. However, it has been observed that the traditional handicrafts, especially in the hands of kumbhkars, are taking a back-seat in the face of technology driven modern development, recognizing the significance of this invaluable historical art and conscious of the need for its revival. The Mitti Kala Board was constituted by the State Government vide Notification dated 08.12.2010 with a objective to revive and promote the heritage, hand-crafted earthen pottery, other clay based artifacts and lay down general guidelines for augmenting the income of the traditional artisans through various initiatives in the production of conventional items. Budget is required for Honorarium to Chairman, Salary and Office Expenses.

entries.name: Provide financial incentive for purchase of boilers running on PNG under Clean Air Project for sustainable Development- SPV ARJUN-N A
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Provide financial incentive for purchase of boilers running on PNG under Clean Air Project for Sustainable Development -SPV ARJUN
entries.purpose: Air pollution represents a signlficant global challenge. Haryana Clean Air Project for Sustainable Development (HCAPSD) establishes the vision of the Government of Haryana for reducing air pollution through the reformation of air quality management. The State Government has partnered with the World Bank for technical and financial support for its clean air project. The detailed project report (DPR) prepared by the state for improving air quality consists of cross-Sectoral Initiatives for mitigation of air pollution. The generator set subsidy and Assistance in conversion of boiler to run on cleaner fuels will be provided under this scheme. The World Bank has formulated an airshed-based air quality management programme to reduce PM emissions in the region by bringing together the Indo- Gangetic Plain (IGP) states to take targeted action for reducing air pollution, and driving interstate collaboration for improving air quality. The project document sets the vision for multi-sector action to reduce air pollution in line with the state's vision to achieve SDGs by 2030. The program focuses on MSME industrial units that operate with outdated boilers and diesel generator (DG) sets, both of which are major contributors to PM 2.5 emissions. The intervention will support adoption of CPCB-compliant boilers, dual-fuel DG sets (natural gas + diesel), or DGs equipped with emission control devices. The project is financed through the World Bank's Program for Results (PforR) mechanism. Under the PforR mechanism, the phase-wise indicated payment from the World Bank will be received only after the targets in the disbursement-linked indicators (DLIs) are met. To meet the expenditure for providing financial incentives to MSMEs for conversion/replacement of boilers to run on cleaner gaseous fuels (PNG)

entries.name: Grant-in-aid to MEANS Council
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Grant in Aid to MEANS Council
entries.purpose: A dedicated agency, MSMEs Advancement & Nurturing Support (MEANS) Council, has been set up within the Directorate of MSME for undertaking facilitation & developmental activities to promote the growth of State’s MSMEs & traders. The MEANS Council shall undertake various activities for promotion, outreach, facilitation, advancement and development of MSMEs and traders of Haryana. Some of the key activities of the MEANS Council are mentioned below: • Act as an implementing agency/ Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV) for coordination and acceptance of funds against various key schemes of Government of India like Ministry of MSME Micro and Small Enterprises- Cluster Development Programme (MSE-CDP) etc. • Provide advisory services to the Directorate and other State government bodies & departments for initiating programs to support MSMEs & traders become competitive. • Establish a governance mechanism to provide direction to the activities of the Directorate and to extend policy advocacy support, whenever required. • Provide recommendations for enhancing Ease of Doing Business (EoDB) and reducing Cost of Doing Business (CoDB) for MSMEs and traders. • Liaison with industries associations at the national & state levels, trading corporations, Trade Development Authority & Export Promotion Councils etc. • Conduct awareness generation & capacity building programs for MSMEs and traders on key topics like market diversification, credit linkages, export promotion, competitiveness, cluster development, skill enhancement etc. • Enable market diversification of MSMEs by participation in international/domestic trade fairs, exhibitions, conferences etc. • Conduct international and domestic study tours to capture best practices for development of the State’s MSMEs ecosystem • Undertake benchmarking studies to analyze and understand the support offered by other countries/states to their MSMEs and traders. • Serve as think tank and knowledge centre for growth of the MSME footprint . • Act as an information helpdesk for the State MSMEs. • Creation and updating of knowledge management system for Directorate and MSMEs, for effective assimilation and dissemination of information. • Preparation of ready project profiles for MSMEs. • Preparation and updating of compendium of MSMEs schemes (Centre/State). • Guiding MSMEs across various functional areas of the enterprise and linking them to Business Development Service Providers (BDSPs). • Conduct MSMEs surveys and publish reports on key trends in the sector. • Engage experts/knowledge partners as per the Directorate’s requirements. • Provide advisory services to Directorate for enabling MSMEs to meet their workforce requirement (linkages with Saksham portal, etc.) • Develop media advertisements, videos, and documentaries for growth of MSMEs. • Publish literature and newsletters for knowledge sharing among MSMEs. In order to carry out the above-listed activities, and to equip the MEANS Council to provide the advisory services to the Directorate on conceptualizing and initiating programs for supporting MSMEs & traders become competitive by overcoming their challenges pertaining to access to finance, markets, technology, infrastructure, skills etc.

The IDDC can also support this industry by providing skilled manpower through various technical programmes and can also support Industry into selection of manufacturing methods & latest machines availability. entries.name: Reh.of Canal Network- Improvement in rehabilitation of Water courses in Scheduled Castes Population in the State
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Rehabilitation of Canal Network-Improvement in Rehabilitation of Water Courses in Scheduled Castes Population in the State
entries.purpose: Most of the canal system in Haryana is about 45 years old. The rehabilitation and modernization of existing system is being given priority to improve the hydraulic flow conditions and to reduce losses to achieve the designed efficiency of water carrier/feeder distribution network. More stress more efforts are being made to bring back the canal system to its designed/required parameters and efficiency with the minimum possible investment. The major rehabilitation work with estimated cost of ` 776.00 Crore has been taken-up on Jui Feeder, Sheranwali Disty, Fatehabad Disty, Masudpur Disty., Badhwar Disty., Garanpura Minor, Pataudi Disty., Hassanpur Disty., Shahbazpur Disty., Narnaul Disty., Kamania Minor, Meghot Minor, Alipur Minor, Dostpur Minor, Kutiyana Disty., Mallekan Minor, Baruwali Disty., Kasumbi Minor and Banmandori Disty., etc. during FY 2025-2026 & 2026-27. Due to meager land holding of scheduled castes population in the State, no rehabilitation of canal network scheme could benefit directly to scheduled castes population. However, flow of benefit in terms of employment and drinking water to SC population can be ensured. This is for improvement in construction works and rehabilitation of existing canal network for efficient distribution of water.

entries.purpose: The basic concept of the project is to utilize maximum Yamuna water during rainy season particularly for the water-deficit Southern part of Haryana. Further, WJC carrier system is not designed to run all the off-taking channels during rainy season when sufficient water is available in the Yamuna River. The WJC Carrier system has been designed in a manner that all the off-taking canal systems from Khubru, Munak and Indri will be able to run simultaneously, if there is demand in the area and no rotational programme would be enforced when sufficient water is available during rainy season. The major works namely “Construction of PLC from RD 0 to 60000, Remodeling of Augmentation Canal from Km 0.00 to Km 75.250 i.e up to merging point with WJC Branch, Remodeling of PD Branch have been approved under NABARD & in-progress. Due to constant running of these channels since 1954, designed carrying capacity of these channels has been reduced from 10794 Cs. to 9500 Cs. entries.name: Scheme for Small Industries Cluster Development
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Scheme for Small Industries Cluster Development
entries.purpose: Small Industries Development Bank of India (SIDBI) has launched a focused vertical for micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) clusters’ SIDBI Cluster Development Fund along with centric programs to give a thrust to hard infrastructure support to state governments. The expert Committee on MSME headed by Shri U.K Sinha, while recommending a more focused engagement of SIDBI with State Governments for MSME development and promotion, indicated "Use of Priority Sector Shortfall (PSS) funds to create a low cost lending window for State Governments for infrastructure projects in clusters, civil works for rehabilitation of existing industrial estates and setting up of new industrial estates. This would require RBI approval and could be structured on the lines of the Rural Infrastructure Development Fund (RIDF)." Pursuant to the recommendation made by the U.K. Sinha Committee and accepted by Gol, RBI formulated broad terms and conditions for setting up of a Cluster Development Fund (CDF) for the purpose of financing of State Governments, etc., to create infrastructure towards development of MSME clusters. The Reserve Bank of India on the advice of Government of India has made an allocation of funds to be utilized by the State Governments/ Government sponsored organizations for infrastructural and Cluster Development initiatives for the MSMEs in the state (subject to state wise cap). This separate fund is called as cluster development fund (CDF). The purpose of this assistance in the form of term loan is as mentioned below:- • Infrastructure projects in MSME Clusters [both green field (induced clusters) and brown field (existing cluster)] including machinery / equipment financing. • Civil works for rehabilitation of existing industrial estates and setting up of new industrial estates. Further, the financing under the scheme would be done for proposals falling under any of the following categories (indicative): I. Industrial and Agri-allied sectors in the MSME eco-space. II. Social sectors in and around MSME clusters III. Connectivity (Roads/Bridges) to MSME Clusters. The interest shall be payable on quarterly basis. The borrowing by the State Government under SCDF will be in the range of 80%- 95% of the project cost subject to the State wise exposure limit, if any.

entries.name: Mukhyamantri Samagra Shahari Vikas Yojana
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Mukhyamantri Samagra Shahari Vikas Yojana
entries.purpose: Haryana exhibits a trend towards rapid urbanization. Urban Local Bodies are entrusted with responsibilities for addressing not only the existing needs of the ULBs, but also the future needs of the growing urban population. In order to cope with the massive problems that have emerged as a result of rapid urban growth, it has become imperative to draw up a coherent urbanization policy/strategy to implement projects in cities of Haryana on mission mode. Presently, there are 87 Urban Local Bodies in the State of Haryana, consisting of 11 Municipal Corporations, 23 Municipal Councils and 53 Municipal Committees. It is generally difficult for several municipal bodies, particularly representing small and medium sized cities, to formulate and execute need based projects due to lack of adequate capacity and resources. Thus there is a need for concentrated efforts to improve the capacities and to ensure availability of resources to urban local bodies for improving urban infrastructure, service delivery, and ultimately to help them in achieving the goal of self- sustainability. In this view, the Government had decided to launch a new scheme namely “Mukhya Mantri Smagra Vikas Yojana” in all the Urban Local Bodies of the State in FY 2020-21. The major objectives of “Mukhya Mantri Smagra Vikas Yojana” is an integrated development of the city/town in a holistic manner within a time frame, with focus on efficiency in urban infrastructure/services delivery mechanism, community participation and accountability of urban local bodies towards citizens. The scheme seeks to ensure sustainable development of cities in a phased manner.

It was decided in the meeting held under the chairmanship of ACS, Finance, Haryana with PSTCP on 19.01.2017, wherein it was agreed to that metro project shall be funded by State Govt. through State Budget. It was concluded that HMRTC does not have any resources for financing of metro projects and state agency like HUDA, HSIIDC and IDF Board are unable to fulfil their commitment as per their agreed share due to financial constraints. Another project has also been approved for the Millennium City Centre, Gurugram for Metro connectivity. HMRTC has conveyed that some more projects are under consideration under this Scheme. The construction of the 28.5 km long metro line from Millennium City Center to Cyber City in Gurugram, will be carried out by Gurugram Metro Rail Limited (GMRL), a joint venture between the state and central governments (50:50 equity participation). entries.name_in_the_narrative: Scheme for Grant Award to Best Performance Self Help Groups (SHGs) promoted under Deen Dayal Antyodaya Yojana National Rural Livelihoods Mission (DAY NRLM)
entries.purpose: Deen Dayal Antyodaya Yojana (DAY)-NRLM, a flagship program of Government of India aims at promoting poverty reduction among poor households in rural areas. Under this scheme awards of `1,00,000/-, `50,000/- and `25,000/- are granted to each of the best performing SHG ranking 1st, 2nd and 3rd respectively on the basis of their earned income as per the following criteria:- 1. All SHGs promoted by DAY-NRLM and satisfying following criteria laid down by Haryana State Rural Livelihoods Mission will be eligible for consideration for the Annual State Awards:- • SHG should be ‘A’ Graded. • SHG must be following Dasa-sutra strictly. • Atleast 70% members should have taken loan. • SHG having Loan recovery more than 90%. • SHG awarded once shall not be considered for the same category of award for next three years. 2. Self Help Groups (SHGs) awarded once shall not be considered for the same category of award for next three years. However, same SHG may be considered for the higher category award. 3. Amount of each cash award to SHG would be credited into its saving bank account to make part of its corpus funds and shall not be distributed amongst members. 4. These awards provide public recognition to the outstanding performance of the SHGs, also instil competition amongst them to perform better and also act as incentives for other SHGs. 5. Eight broader indicators have been developed with maximum score of 100 (each indicator assigned marks ranging between 5 to 30 inclined more towards income generation activities undertaken by SHGs). 6. Each indicator has further been divided into sub indicators with marks for each, based on the performance of the participating SHG, to make the exercise more transparent and competitive.

entries.name: Scheme for delayed compensation and unemployment allowance under Mahatma Gandhi NREGA
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Scheme for delay compensation and unemployment Allowance under Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme (MGNREGA)
entries.purpose: Delay Compensation:- As per MGNREGA guideline in case the payment of wages is not made within 15 days from the date of closure of the muster roll, the wage seeker shall be entitled to receive payment of compensation for the delay 16th day of closer of Muster Roll. As per MGNREGA Act, the State Govt. has to pay the delay compensation to the worker and subsequently recovers the amount from the responsible functionary/institutions who has caused the delay. Unemployment Allowance: A person who is registered under MGNREGS and issued a job card and who has submitted an application seeking employment and whose application is registered in the demand of work registered, shall be entitled to Unemployment allowance, in case, employment is not provided within 15 days of the receipt of the work demand. The Unemployment allowance will be paid @ equal to the ¼ of the prevailing wage rate for the first 30 days and equal to ½ of the wage rate for the remaining period. Note:-This scheme will be replaced by Viksit Bharat – Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin): VB-G RAM G & this component will also be applicable for implementation of VB-G RAM G.

entries.purpose: “The Haryana Pond and Waste Water Management Authority”(HPWWMA) was established on 23.10.2018, and has been collecting data ,since then ,for all the ponds located on the Govt. land in the State of Haryana, through Pond Data Management System (PDMS) Software, which are in total 20018 ponds (Rural: 19110 & Urban: 908 ), as on 20/01/2026. • 19,474 ponds have already been Geo-Mapped and Geo-Tagged and are live on PDMS through Haryana Space Application Centre (HARSAC). • Authority has set a target of rejuvenating 6538 ponds under the Action Plan up to 2025-26, to cover 3141 villages in 22 Districts 1398 Ponds have been completed. • Up to the F.Y Year 2024-25 ,the water capacity and recharging of ponds has been increased by 2133.55 Crore Liters and 1066.77 Crore Liters respectively leading to a significant improvement in ground water level. • The Grey water/waste water flowing into above ponds is being treated through Constructed Wetland Technology, so as to utilize water of these restored ponds for Pisci-culture, Cattle use as well as for Micro-Irrigation. • Due to shifting of Administrative Department from Irrigation to Development and Panchayat Department in 05/2025, and decision of financial control by FD in 10/2025 no funds could have been drawn and transferred up to 10/2025 to executing departments that has ultimately affected the ongoing works for want of funds. • Haryana Pond Authority has already launched a full-scale Awareness/Publicity Programme to enlighten and make the public aware regarding significance and necessity of Ponds in our echo system so that common public owns and take initiative to keep the ponds clean in neighborhood. • The Haryana Pond & Waste Water Management Authority is committed to incorporate the motto ‘‘vIlq vUr% ve`ra%'' (water contains the essence of immortality) into its work and spreading this message among the masses under the guidance of Hon’ble C.M. entries.purpose: Under this scheme, State has 143 Development blocks covered at present. For the proper and efficient functioning, it is essential that the block offices/Zila Parishad offices housed in rented buildings are provided their own buildings. Further, with the passage of time, the buildings of old blocks become un-safe and need to be replaced with new buildings. Beside above, the other main objective for launching the scheme of Gram Sachivalyas is to bring Gram Panchayat and Village-level Functionaries of all departments under one roof for better functioning & coordination. It aims to ensure efficiency, transparency and accountability in the working of Gram Panchayat and other agencies engaged in the process of rural development. As on date 1856 Gram Sachivalyas have been established in the State. For this purpose, the Rajiv Gandhi Sewa Kendras, Panchayat Ghars or any other suitable community building available in Gram Panchayats will be upgraded and basic IT facilities (infrastructure and hardware) will be provided in order to set up Gram Sachivalyas. New Block office buildings and Zila Parishad Bhawans are also constructed under this scheme.

entries.name: Rural Infrastructure Development under State Finance Commission (SFC)
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Rural Infrastructure Development under State Finance Commission (SFC)
entries.purpose: As per mandate of 73rd Constitutional Amendment, the State Government has been regularly constituting the State Finance Commission under Article 243-I read with Section 213 of the Haryana Panchayati Raj Act, 1994 from time to time to review the financial position of the Panchayats. State Finance Commission also makes recommendations on the principles which should govern the distribution between the State and the Panchayats of the net proceeds of the taxes, duties, tolls and fees liveable by the State, which may be further divided between them and the allocation between the Panchayats at all levels of their respective shares of such proceeds; the determination of the taxes, duties, tolls and fees which may be assigned to, or appropriated by the Panchayats; the grants-in-aid to the Panchayats from the Consolidated Fund of the State and the measures needed to improve the financial position of the Panchayats. As per recommendations (Revised Explanatory memorandum) of the sixth State Finance Commission, 80% Amount would be distributed/released on the basis of PPP (Parivaar Pehchaan Patra) population and 20% amount shall be distributed as per Area under the State Finance Commission Grant. Moreover, the funds shall be released to the Panchayat Samitis and Zila Parishads, only as per PPP (Parivaar Pehchaan Patra) Populations of the concerned Zila Parishads/Panchyat Samitis.

State Finance Commission also makes recommendations on the principles which should govern the distribution between the State and the Panchayats of the net proceeds of the taxes, duties, tolls and fees leviable by the State, including their allocation between the Panchayats at all levels, the determination of the taxes, duties, tolls and fees that may be assigned to, or appropriated by the Panchayats and the grants-in-aid to the Panchayats from the Consolidated Fund of the State and the measures needed to improve the financial position of the Panchayats. As per recommendations (Revised Explanatory memorandum) of the sixth State Finance Commission, 80% amount shall be distributed/released to the GPs on the basis of PPP (Parivaar Pehchaan Patra) population of the Panchayats and 20% amount shall be distributed as per Area under the State Finance Commission Grant. Additionally, the funds shall be released to the Panchayat Samitis, and Zila Parishads only as per PPP (Parivaar Pehchaan Patra) populations of the concerned Zila Parishads, Panchyat Samitis and Gram Panchayats.

entries.name: Mahatma Gandhi Gramin Basti Yojna
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Mahatma Gandhi Gramin Basti Yojana (SCSP)
entries.purpose: Mahatma Gandhi Gramin Basti Yojana was launched in Haryana in the year 2008. The scheme is aimed to allot free residential plots of 100 Square yard each to the eligible Scheduled Castes families, Backward Class (Category- A) families and Below Poverty Line (BPL) families in the villages out of the available suitable shamlat land. In the first phase, the plots are being provided out of the shamlat lands, available with the Panchayats and in the villages where no suitable Panchayat land is available, it is being made available either by way of exchange with that of the private land owners or by acquisition. Basic infrastructural facilities such as streets, drinking water, drainage, power supply etc. are being provided alongwith these residential plots in a phased manner. Further, a sum of `10,000/-per acre per year is being paid as annuity to those Gram Panchayats whose land had already been utilized for the purpose of allotment of plots.

entries.name: Gurugram Water Supply & Mewat Feeder pipeline Project
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Gurugram Water Supply & Mewat Feeder pipeline Project
entries.purpose: 1. Remodeling of Existing Gurugram Water Supply Channel [GWS) from RD 0 to 69.585 KM on Engineering, Procurement and Construction (EPC) Mode. Existing GWS channel was commissioned in the year 1995 with capacity of 175 cusecs to provide drinking water to Gurugram and Bahadurgarh. Due to continuous running, the channel is in dilapidated condition and its carrying capacity has reduced more than 50%. Further, due to rapid urban growth in NCR region, demand of water has increased considerably. To cater the increasing demand, it was decided by the Govt. to augment GWS channel as per future demand required of the year 2030, 2040 & 2050 of all stakeholder Departments i.e. HSIIDC, PHED, GMDA, HSVP, etc. 2. Construction of Mewat Feeder Pipeline Along KMP Expressway Off-Taking from RD 50.48 KM of GWS and RD 56.62 KM of NCR Channels Near Badli (Jhajjar) on Engineering, Procurement and Construction (EPC) Mode. District Nuh (Mewat region) has no fresh surface water source and is having brackish ground water which is totally unfit for drinking. To address this issue, PHED had planned various drinking water projects. Further, HSIIDC and HSVP are also developing Industrial and Residential townships in this area e.g. IMT Sohna, Manesar & Dharuhera and HSVP Sohna etc.; for which fresh raw water is to be provided. To provide water to these drinking and industrial development projects, Mewat Feeder Pipeline projects was announced by the Govt. It was also decided by the Govt. to provide Mewat Feeder Pipeline as per future demand required for the year 2030, 2040 & 2050 of all stakeholder Departments i.e. HSIIDC, PHED, HSVP, etc.

entries.name_in_the_narrative: Compensation for Acquired Land for Rural and Urban Water Supply and Sewerage Works
entries.purpose: As a welfare State, the Government of Haryana recognizes that acquisition of land under the statute and the alienation of landowners from their source of livelihood could be a painful process, notwithstanding the payment of compensation for the same as per law. Therefore, it intends to minimize this pain of the affected persons through a set of policy initiatives that include (a) payment of market value as compensation of land to the landowners with the revision and fine-tuning of minimum floor rates in respect of land situated in different parts of the state; (b) introduction of a special incentive for reducing litigation qua the compensation amount; (c) revision of the rates of Annuity payable for a period of 33 years as a social security benefit for the landowners; and (d) review and introduction of certain additional benefit over and above the one-time compensation paid in accordance with the law so as to provide alternate means of sustenance for the landowners and other landless person/artisans who are dependent on the agriculture land being required for non-agricultural purpose. entries.name: Rural Water Supply (SP)- Mahagram Yojana for updation of Drinking Water Supply in Village
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Rural Water Supply (SP)-Mahagram Yojana for updation of Drinking Water Supply in Village
entries.purpose: Mahagram Yojana is the flagship scheme of the State and envisages the supply of drinking water @ 135 LPCD + 15% UAF so as to facilitate the laying of a robust sewerage system in the project villages. This scheme is aimed at providing the basic amenities to society so as to reduce the rural-urban divide and suppress the proclivity of people migrating from the villages to the towns. Currently, 150 villages have been short-listed and during the course of implementation, it has been found that work cannot be taken up in 18 villages as 7 villages have been urbanized and in 11 villages, the panchayats are not interested in the scheme or the scheme is not feasible. Out of the effective 132 villages, work has been completed in 19 villages. Further, implementation work is in progress in 41 villages, out of which 9 villages are to be commissioned by 31.12.2025. All the remaining villages shall be commissioned by 31.12.2028, with staggered timelines.

entries.purpose: NABARD has been providing financial support for infrastructure development of rural water supply since 2000-2001 under the successive tranches of Rural Infrastructure Development Fund (RIDF). This partnership with NABARD has enabled the State to create a humongous infrastructure in the rural areas. Since the last few years, NABARD has expanded its activities and they are financing big-ticket projects on drinking water supply @ 135 LPCD in big villages and also capital-intensive schemes for laying a robust sewerage ecosystem in these big villages, being covered under the prestigious Mahagram progarmme. At present, 80 projects costing ` 135688.40 lakh are in progress. Out of the above said projects, NABARD has recently sanctioned 17 drinking water supply projects for Bhiwani, Charkhi Dadri and Sonipat Districts at a cost of ` 11565.01 lakh under RIDF XXXI. The work on these projects is already under progress and some new projects are likely to be approved during the next fiscal year.

entries.purpose: The funds under Scheduled Caste Sub Plan (SCSP) are predominantly utilized for improving the drinking water infrastructure in the SC dominated habitations of the State. During the past successive years, the funds under SCSP have been utilized to drill additional tube wells, construction of boosting stations and strengthening the existing distribution system. The major performance attributed to the fact that in the past, a robust infrastructure has been built up for the SC habitations. Moreover, under the Jal Jeevan Mission, water taps have been provided in all the rural households, irrespective of caste discrimination. As a consequence, water saturation has been reached in the SC bastis.

entries.name: National Land Records Modernization Programme- Computerization of Registration

entries.purpose: Centre Share: `16,75,000/- State Share: `50,25,000/- It is a Centrally Sponsored scheme (75% Central funds, 25% State funds). The Government of India implemented the Centrally Sponsored Scheme in the shape of the National Land Records Modernization Programme (NLRMP) by merging two existing centrally sponsored Schemes of Computerization of Land Records and Strengthening of Revenue Administration and Updating of Land Records in the Department of Land Resources, Ministry of Rural Development. The integrated programme would modernize management of land records, minimize scope of land dispute, enhance transparency in the land records maintenance system, and to facilitate moving eventually towards guaranteed conclusive titles to immovable properties in the country. This scheme is being implemented from the year 2010. The main objectives of the scheme are:- a) Data entry of legacy encumbrance data b) Scanning & preservation of old documents c) Data entry of valuation details d) Computerization of registration work e) Computerization of SROs. f) Connectivity of SROs with Revenue Offices The above scheme is based on following basic principles: • A single window to handle land records (including the maintenance and updating of textual records, maps). • Timely issuance of copies of land records in the shortest possible time to those who need it. • Transparency in matters of registration of documents, sanction of mutations and aspects of public dealings. • Creation of land records information system, which automatically updates revenue record by bringing all the revenue entries on-line. • Creation of land information system and database for effective reforms, revenue administration and development at grass root level. • Low cost easy storage medium for revenue records and database and efficient retrieval of information both spiritual and textual. • Land disputes will be minimized.

entries.purpose: Centre Share: ` 2,02,20,000/- State Share: `1,34,80,000/- This is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme being implemented on sharing basis of 60:40 ratio. Paddy is grown on an area of about 31.25 lakh acres in Haryana due to which there is continuous excessive exploitation of ground water and soil fertility is also decreasing. Haryana Government is committed to preserve natural resources, in this direction, the State Government has started Crop Diversification Programme in Original Green Revolution in the State under RKVY during 2013. The scheme is being implemented in the more water exhaustive districts like Ambala, Fatehabad, Hisar, Jind, Karnal, Kaithal, Kurukshetra, Panipat, Rohtak, Sonipat, Sirsa and Yamunanagar where paddy is grown in more than 1.25 lakh acre. In order to encourage the farmers, the State Government has decided to provide an incentive of Rs. 2400/- per acre for Maize and Rs. 3600/ - per acre for pulses like Moong, Urd and Arhar and and Rs. 2000/ - per acre for Agro-Forestry i.e inter-cropping of Poplar-Wheat. The target 602 numbers of Power-Spray Pump-set has been kept and subsidy of Rs. 3000/- per Pump-set will also be given to the eligible farmers. The incentive will be disbursed in the farmers bank accounts through DBT after physical verification. The farmer registration is mandatory on www.agriharyana.gov.in to get the benefit of the scheme. Apart from this, District Level Mela will also be organized to make farmers aware about the scheme.

Sericulture includes mulberry plantation and rearing of silkworms on the leaves of the plants for production of cocoon and thereafter raw silk. It is land-based activity having several advantages such as labor-intensive low capital investment and good returns. Sericulture is gaining popularity over the years as a house-hold industry and a remunerative avenue for income generation in rural areas. The bye products like mulberry wood, fruits, waste leave, silkworm litter, silk waste and pupae etc. also supplement the household income on regular basis throughout the year. In this scheme the provision for subsidy is 75% (CS: 50%+SS: 25%+Ben: 25%) for General Farmers and 90% (CS: 65%+ SS: 25%+ Ben: 10%) for SC Farmers. The objective of the scheme are to promote sericulture in favorable ecology & to create productivity employment opportunities in rural areas by promoting sericulture as a cottage industry. • To bring horizontal and vertical growth in cocoon production in the cluster. • To harness the available natural resources viz. waste/ degraded land for development for viable and sustainable Sericulture. • To bring out entrepreneurial abilities among local people. • To provide need cased infrastructure support to silk industry to ensure regular support of raw material to the reeling industry.

The scheme was revamped during the year 2018 as RKVY-RAFTAAR- Remunerative Approaches for Agriculture and Allied sector Rejuvenation. RKVY-RAFTAAR aims at making farming a remunerative economic activity through strengthening the farmers’ efforts, risk mitigation and promoting agri-business entrepreneurship. The main objectives of the scheme are as detailed below:- • To strengthen the farmers’ efforts through creation of required pre and post- harvest agri-infrastructure that increases access to quality inputs, storage, market facilities etc. and enable farmers to make choices. • To provide autonomy, flexibility to States to plan and execute schemes as per local/farmers’ needs. • To promote value chain addition linked production models that will help farmers increase their income as well as encourage production/productivity. • To mitigate risk of farmers with focus on additional income generation activities like integrated farming, mushroom cultivation, bee keeping, aromatic plant cultivation, floriculture etc. • To achieve national priorities through several sub-schemes. • To empower youth through skill development, innovation and agri- entrepreneurship based agri business models that attract them to agriculture. RKVY-RAFTAAR is a project based scheme. All type of farmers have been covered under the scheme. All the projects have been submitted by Agriculture and Allied Departments and Agencies. The subsidy has been given in cash or kind on inputs like seed, fertilizers, pesticides etc. varies from project to project and duration of subsidy also depends on project duration. The research based projects are also covered in this scheme. The scheme consists of Infrastructure & Assets, Production Growth, Sub- Schemes. Main Focus Areas under RKVY are Agriculture (Soil Health, Water Management, Seed Treatment, Farm Mechanization, and Promotion of DSR). Horticulture (Promotion of Integrated Post-Harvest Management, Promotion of Bio-pesticides in horticulture crops, Assistance on Mushroom Production Units), CCS HAU, LUVAS, Hisar, CSSRI, Karnal & Sugarcane Breeding Institute, Karnal (All Research Projects) FPO Haryana State Agriculture Marketing Infrastructure.

entries.purpose: Scheme Name: National Livestock Mission Breed Development of Livestock & Poultry and Seminar for Scheduled Castes (SCSP) (60:40) Centre Share: `1,20,00,000/- State Share: `80,00,000/- The National Livestock Mission (NLM) envisages focused breed improvement and entrepreneurship development under the Sub-Mission on Breed Development of Livestock, Poultry and Innovation & Extension components. In Haryana, the scheme is implemented through the State Implementing Agency under the Animal Husbandry & Dairying Department with a funding pattern of 60:40 between the Government of India and the State Government. The mission aims at enhancing per animal productivity, genetic upgradation, and organized development of poultry, sheep, goat and piggery sectors. Assistance is provided for establishment of Regional Semen Production Laboratories, strengthening of State Semen Banks, propagation of Artificial Insemination services, and import of high genetic merit germplasm to prevent inbreeding and improve production traits. In addition, entrepreneurship development is promoted through capital subsidy support for breed multiplication units in rural poultry, small ruminants and piggery. The Innovation and Extension component supports seminars, conferences, awareness programmes, and capacity building initiatives to disseminate scientific breeding practices and modern technologies among farmers and field functionaries. Through these interventions, Haryana aims to strengthen forward and backward linkages, improve availability of quality germplasm, enhance meat, egg, milk and wool production, and generate sustainable employment in the livestock sector.

entries.name: Livestock Health and Disease Control
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Livestock Health and Disease Control
entries.purpose: Centre Share: `4,80,00,000/- State Share : `3,20,00,000/- This scheme includes the following ongoing component for which the Government of India releases funds regularly:- (i) Assistance to States for the control of animal Diseases (ASCAD) The Government of India has approved a macro management centrally sponsored scheme namely "Livestock Health & Disease Control". Assistance to States for the control of Animal diseases (ASCAD) is one of its component. The main object of this scheme is to control economically important diseases of livestock and poultry in the country by way of immunization and strengthening/modernization of existing biological products units/State Disease Diagnostic Laboratories. (ii) Foot and Mouth disease Control (FMD) Programme FMD is the most important livestock disease in term of economic impact though the morbidity rate is high and the mortality rate due to FMD is low. The economic losses caused by the disease are mainly due to loss in milk production, reduction in working ability of working animals, reduction in the body weight leading reduced yields of meat etc. To prevent economic losses due to FMD and to develop herd immunity in cloven- footed animals, a location specific programme called Foot and Mouth Disease Control Programme with 60 % central assistance is being implemented in the entire State under which a major thrust is upon the control and virtual eradication of Foot & Mouth Disease from the country as a whole and Haryana in particular. For this, mass vaccination and routine vaccination of all the susceptible animals within a zone will be undertaken. (iii) Control of Brucellosis Brucellosis is also an economically important abortifacient disease of cattle. Infected cows/buffaloes usually abort in the second half of pregnancy with the squeal of retained placenta, delayed involution, predisposal to secondary bacterial infections and acute or chronic endometritis. In several cases, it may cause ovaro-bursal adhesions resulting into permanent sterility. Some of the infected animals, which carry fetus to term, often give birth to either dead or weak and underweight calves leading to heavy neonatal mortality. Infected cows usually abort once but may continue to shed the organism subsequently, sometimes for life. There is high risk of Brucellosis transmission through artificial insemination as the semen is deposited after passing cervix which officers a protective barrier. Provision has also been made under this scheme for the taking steps to control this disease also. In initial phase, the testing against brucellosis will be undertaken at bull mother farms, sperm production centers and in the areas having high density of good quality livestock. (iv) Peste-des-Petits Ruminants Control Programme (PPR-CP) Peste-des-petits Ruminants (PPR) also known as ‘Goat Plague’ is a viral disease that affects goats and sheep, which causes huge financial loss to the livestock farmers and economic loss to the country. The Peste des Petits Ruminants (PPR) is characterized by high fever, inflammation of the gastro-intestinal tract leading to necrosis and ulceration of the mucous membrane and diarrhea. The PPR infection causes huge losses in the rural economy both in terms of morbidity and mortality in sheep and goats. The symptoms of disease are purulent discharge from eyes & nose, sores in mouth, swollen & eroded lips, diarrhea, sudden fever, pneumonia and coughing. Affected animals appear restless, have a dull coat, dry muzzle and depressed appetite and the pregnant animals

entries.name_in_the_narrative: Integrated Forest Protection (Intensification of Forest Management Scheme)
entries.purpose: Centre Share: `3,60,00,000/- State Share : `2,40,00,000/- This is a Centrally Sponsored scheme which is being implemented on sharing basis (60:40). The main objectives of the scheme are as under: • Protection of forests from devastating forest fires. • Protection of forests against illegal encroachment. • Infrastructure development for frontline staff. • Enhancement of e-Governance initiatives. • Procurement of Forest Fire Control Tools and equipments etc. • Construction and maintenance of Fire lines. The targets achieved under the scheme include maintenance of fire lines in the forest areas, demarcation of forest boundaries, infrastructure development for frontline staff and creation of awareness amongst local population. World over, the efforts are being made to protect and conserve the forests for healthy and clean environment. The Government of India launched “Integrated Forest Protection Scheme”, commencing from the year 2002-2003 and has been renamed as “Intensification of Forest Management Scheme”. The scheme makes judicious use of all available methods for better protection and conservation of forest resources of the country. These methods include management of forest fires, maintenance of fire lines, purchase of firefighting equipment, demarcation of forest boundaries, enumeration of trees, improving communication through wireless equipments and creation of awareness among the local masses. These methods also include control of forest fires, creation of fire lines and fire watch towers and fire mapping. After initiation of this scheme, the annual loss of forests and wildlife during the fire season has considerably come down.

entries.name: Conservation and Management of Wetland in Haryana under the National Plan for Conservation of Aquatice Eco-systems
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Conservation and Management of Wetland in Haryana Under the National Plan for Conservation of Aquatic Eco-Systems.
entries.purpose: Centre Share: `3,00,00,000/- State Share: `2,00,00,000/- This scheme is being implemented through cost sharing basis between the Central Government and respective State Government. Under this scheme, financial assistance is provided to the States by the Central Government on sharing basis i.e 60% by the Central Government and 40% to be borne by the State Government. Object and Performance of the Scheme As we are aware that Bhindawas Wetland and Sultanpur Wetland declared as Ramsar Sites and these Lakes and Wetlands are important parts of our ecosystems, which are effective in the flood control, waste water treatment, recharging of aquifers and also serve as natural habitat for migratory birds, therefore, the conservation of lakes and wetlands needs immediate attention. Presently, Ministry of Environment, Forest & Climate Change (MoEF&CC), GOI is implementing a scheme namely National Plan for Conservation of Aquatic Eco-systems (NPCA) for conservation and management of identified lakes and wetland in the country. The objective of providing financial assistance is to restore and conserve the urban and semi-urban lakes degraded due to waste water discharge in the lake and other unique freshwater ecosystems. There are two wetlands in Haryana viz. Sultanpur Wetland and Bhindawas Wetland which are notified as sanctuaries under Wildlife Protection Act, 1972. Both of these wetlands carries out habitat improvement activities like deepening of lake area, weed removal from the lake surrounding area, development of watch tower/birds sighting sites, ecosystem stability by introducing fish fingerling etc. Other activities include improving the research base and scientific management by assessing the water quality and identification of flora and fauna in these wetlands. The financial assistance for carrying out new activities in Sultanpur Wetland and Bhindawas Wetland has been provided under National Wetland Conservation Programme(NWCP), Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change, New Delhi with funding on a cost sharing basis of 60:40 between the Central Govt. and the State Govt. Our Sultanpur Wetland and Bhindawas Wetland habitats will be improved which is very important for wildlife conservation.

entries.purpose: Centre Share : `11,40,00,000/- State Share: `7,60,00,000/- The Government's sustained initiative on education and employment of women has resulted in increased opportunities for their employment, and more and more women are now in gainful employment, working within or outside their homes. Thus, the children of such working women, who were earlier getting support from families while they were at work, are now in need of day care services which provide quality care and protection for the children. Lack of proper day-care services is, often, a deterrent for women to go out and work. Hence, there is an urgent need for improved quality and reach of day care services/creches for working women amongst all socioeconomic groups both in the organized and unorganized sectors. Considering the difficulties faced by the working mothers in giving due child care and protection to their children, it has been decided to provide the day-care creche facilities through the component of Palna. Creche services formalise the child care facilities hitherto considered as part of domestic work. Formalization of care work supports "decent work campaign" to achieve the Sustainable Development Goal 8 (SDG 8) ‘Decent work and Economic growth’. Government of India has decided to establish 17000 Anganwadi cum Creches by 15th Finance Commission. Objectives of the Palna Scheme: 1. Providing a safe & secure environment for nutritional, health and cognitive development of the children, 2. Enabling more mothers to take up gainful employment. 3. Monitoring compliance of the stipulations laid down in Section 11A of the Maternity Benefit Act regarding setting up of creche facilities by the establishments. Monitorable Targets: 1. Creche facility to be provided to all mothers, irrespective of their employment status. The scheme focuses on children of 6 months to 6 years.

entries.name: Supplementary Nutrition Programme for Scheduled Castes
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Supplementary Nutrition Programme for Scheduled Castes (50:50)
entries.purpose: Centre Share:`40,00,00,000/- State Share: `40,00,00,000/- This Scheme was started under Integrated Child Development Scheme (ICDS) in the State during 1975-76. The expenditure of Supplementary Nutrition Programme (SNP) is being shared by Centre & State in the ratio of 50:50. The State Government is providing Supplementary Nutrition programme (SNP) containing an average nutritive value as per norms fixed i.e. in case of Pregnant/Lactating mothers 600 calories and 18- 20 gm. protein, in case of children 500 calories and 12-15 gm. protein and in case of severely malnourished children 800 calories and 20-25 gm. protein @ `9.50/- per mother, ` 8/- per child and `12/- per malnourished child respectively, per day for 300 days in a year. Presently,10.29 lakh children and 2.60 lakh pregnant/ lactating mothers are covered under Supplementary Nutrition Programme. The recipes provided under ICDS are Poshtic Panjiri, Bharwa Parantha, Aloo puri, Meetha Chawal, Meetha Dalia, Pulao. Gulgale and Chana, Murmura & Mungfali Mixture etc. At present, the fortified Panjiri is prepared in two Panjiri Plants, one at Gharaundha (Karnal) and other one at Gurugram, which is supplied in the Anganwadi centres of Karnal, Gurugram and Mewat and for the remaining districts, the fortified Panjiri is being distributed through Haryana Agro. These department’s Panjiri Plants are producing 3.5 MT Panjiri per month. The Panjiri produced by these Panjiri Plants is fortified with micronutrients and is being given to the children as morning snack in age group of 3 to 6 years of Anganwadi Centres. At present, these plants are producing Panjiri which caters only 14% requirements. The Panjiri is to be given as Take Home Ration (THR) to approximately4.45 lakh children.

entries.purpose: Centre Share: `15,84,00,000/- State Share: `10,56,00,000/- The Scheme was launched by Hon’ble Prime Minister on 8th March, 2018 in Jhunjhunu district of Rajasthan. The focus of Abhiya an is to lay emphasis on nutritional status of adolescent girls, pregnant women, lactating mothers and children from 0-6 years age. With a targeted approach, the programme by using technology, convergence and community development strives to reduce the level of stunting, Under-Nutrition, Aneamia and Low Birth Weight in Children thus, holistically addressing malnutrition. Community Based Events (CBE) are being celebrated on 8th& 22nd of every month in all Anganwaris, on various themes such as Annaprasan Diwas, Suposhan Diwas, celebrating readiness for pre-school at AWCs and public health messages for improvement of nutrition and reducing illness etc.

entries.purpose: Centre Share : `3,30,00,000/- State Share : `2,20,00,000/- Location of JJB (Juvenile Justice Board) and Child Welfare Committee (CWC):- As provided by the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015, a JJB/CWC shall hold its sittings in the premises of an Observation Home/ Children’s Home. Infrastructure for JJB/ CWC: The Observation Homes being constructed shall have two rooms of 300 Sq. ft. each for the JJB, where an existing Observation Home has the required space available within the premises, the same shall be provided to the Board. However, in districts where there is no Observation Home or the existing Observation Home has no space for the JJB, funds will be provided under the Mission for constructing or renting suitable premises for the JJB. The Board shall hold its sittings in one room while the other room should be used as the waiting area for Children and their families. The committee room where the Board/ Committee holds its sitting must have a child friendly environment and the necessary furniture, computer & other basic equipments shall also be made available. Further, the waiting area should have provisions for toilet and drinking water facility along with indoor recreation facilities for children.

entries.name: GIA to State Ayush Society, Haryana for National Ayush Mission
entries.name_in_the_narrative: GIA to State Ayush Society, Haryana for National Ayush Mission
entries.purpose: Centre Share :` 60,00,00,000/- State Share: `40,00,00,000/- The National AYUSH Mission, Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, Government of India has launched National Ayush mission (NAM) during 12th Plan for implementing through States/UTs. The basic objective of NAM is to promote AYUSH medical systems through cost effective AYUSH services, strengthening of educational systems, facilitate the enforcement of quality control of Ayurveda, Siddha and Unani & Homeopathy (ASU &H) drugs and sustainable availability of ASU & H raw-materials. The basic objective is to promote Ayush medical systems through cost effective and equitable AYUSH health care throughout the country by improving access to the services, to revitalize and strengthen the AYUSH systems making them as prominent medical streams in addressing the health care of the society, to improve educational institutions capable of imparting quality AYUSH education, to promote the adoption of Quality standards of AYUSH drugs and making available the sustained supply of AYUSH raw-materials. This is a sharing basis scheme which has been opened in the year 2014-15. As per the guidelines issued by the Government of India, the scheme will be operative on sharing basis between Centre and State on 60:40. This scheme is being operated as Grant-in-aid. Grant-in-aid is being transferred through treasury route with effect from financial year 2014-15 onwards to the State Government, which in turn transfers the funds to the State AYUSH Society along with State Share. *****

Drugs and Cosmetics Rule-1945 etc., as per provisions of the Acts and rules enacted for the Department. Government of Haryana has signed a MoU with Government of India to ensure the quality, safety and efficacy of drugs for domestic consumers as well as for the export purpose, to strengthen the existing setup of surveillance system and increase the consumer awareness about current and new safety quality related threats. Futuristic programmes of Food& Drugs Administration:- 1. To establish separate District and Zonal offices of Food and Drugs Administration, Haryana with a food testing laboratory at district level. 2. Department of Food and Drugs Administration, Haryana is an enforcement Department responsible for enforcement of provision of Drug and Cosmetics Act, 1940, Drug Price Control Order, Drugs and Magic Remedies Act, Food Standard and Safety Act. Infant Milk Substitute Act, Poison Act, 1919 and many others therefore, to strengthening and proper enforcement all modern facilities to handle the Drug and Food related problem of general public are required which are being made available to field staff and proposed to made in future including vehicles/cell phones/laptop etc. 3. Up-gradation of Food and Drug Testing Laboratories by procuring modern/sophisticated equipment/instruments as well as manpower to meet present and future challenges for better testing results of Food and Drug items.

entries.name_in_the_narrative: Pradhan Mantri Formalisation of Micro Food Processing Enterprises (PMFME)
entries.purpose: Centre Share: `19,20,00,000/- State Share: `12,80,00,000/- The main objective of the scheme is to enhance the competitiveness of New/existing individual micro-enterprises in the unorganized segment of the food processing industry and promote formalization of the sector as well as to support Farmer Producer Organizations (FPOs), Self- Help Groups (SHGs) and Producer’s Cooperatives. The objectives of scheme are to build capability of microenterprises to enable:- a) Increased access to credit by existing micro food processing entrepreneurs, FPOs, Self Help Groups and Co-operatives. b) Integration with organized supply chain by strengthening branding &marketing. c) Support for transition of existing 2,00,000 enterprises into formal framework. d) Increased access to common services like common processing facility, laboratories, storage, packaging, marketing and incubation services. e) Strengthening of institutions, research and training in the food processing sector. f) Increased access for the enterprises, to professional and technical support. The scheme envisages an outlay of ₹10, 000 crore over a period of five plus one years from 2020-21 to 2025-26, and as per the draft EFC note shared by MoFPI, Gol, it is proposed to extend the scheme for an additional five years beyond 2025-26. The expenditure under the scheme would continue to be shared in a 60:40 ratio between the Central and State Governments, in a 90:10 ratio with North-eastern and Himalayan States, 60:40 ratio with UTs with legislature, and 100% by the Centre for other UTs. Strategies of the Department: Under the scheme, following approaches will be adopted:- a) Capacity building and research; b) Conducting capacity building and training for State and District officials; c) Conducting training for District Resource Persons; d) Provide inputs for Branding and Marketing plans being prepared by SNAs; e) Provide mentoring support to District Resource Persons for handholding micro enterprises, preparations of DPRS, etc. f) The District MSME Centres are already implementing the scheme under which 15% SC/ST beneficiaries of the allocated target are granted loan through banks in rural as well as urban areas,

entries.name: Comprehensive Handlooms Development Scheme
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Comprehensive Handlooms Development Scheme
entries.purpose: Centre Share: `50,00,000/- State Share: `5,00,000/- National Handloom Development Programme has been formulated for its implementation during financial year 2021-22 to 2025-26. The scheme will follow need- based approach for integrated and holistic development of handlooms and welfare of handloom weavers. The scheme will support weavers, both within and outside the cooperative fold including Self Help Groups etc. towards raw material, design inputs, technology up-gradation, marketing support through exhibitions, create permanent infrastructure in the form of Urban Haats, marketing complexes etc. The objectives of the scheme are as under:- i. To give equal marketing opportunities including direct linkages domestically and internationally to handloom workers with special focus on talented and uncovered weavers for enhancement of their incomes. ii. To focus on development of pockets at the intersection of handlooms & handicrafts, untouched by commercialization, pockets requiring revival of languishing crafts and having export potential. iii. To reorient IIHTs as handloom and handicraft hubs by collaborating with NIFT, NID & DC (HC). iv. To ensure capacity building of handloom workers and other stakeholders, especially technical, managerial & entrepreneurship skills, exposure to banking & formal sources of finance, laws & legal terminology, export procedures & foreign market trends, digital literacy and e-commerce, etc. v. To ensure preservation and archiving of traditional designs, tribal weaves, languishing weaves, looms etc. vi. To link handlooms with fashion through interface between weavers, professional designers & the industry and tourism through creation of handloom craft villages for according greater visibility and outreach to the sector. Under the scheme, priority would be given for sanctioning of components/projects inter-alia, to the handloom workers in the following areas/cluster: i. Areas having individual weavers who are outside the fold of any formal organization. ii. Handloom clusters having export potential/market potential. iii. Pockets at the intersection between handloom and handicrafts. iv. Handloom Pockets requiring revival of languishing crafts. v. Areas untouched by commercialization such as North East. Funding pattern:- (i) Interventions like Baseline Survey, Diagnostic Study, Formation of Consortium, Awareness Programmes, Product Development, Exposure visit, participation in exhibitions/BSMs/publicity, Documentation of cluster activities, service charges to designated agency, Project Management Cost, Engagement of Textiles Designer, wage compensation to the trainees for skill up-gradation, incentive to IA etc. will be fully funded by GoI, excluding land cost. (ii) Other Interventions benefitting directly individual weavers like Hathkargha Samvardhan Sahayata and lighting units will be funded in the ratio of 90:10 by the GoI : Beneficiary (iii) Individual Workshed-SC/ST/Women/differently-abled – 100% by GoI share. Others – 75% by the GoI: 25% beneficiary (iv) Common Workshed – 90% by the GoI: 10% beneficiary (v) Solar Lighting System for Common Workshed - 90% by the GoI: 10% beneficiary.

entries.purpose: Centre Share: `168,75,00,000/- State Share : `56,25,00,000/- This is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme on 90:10 sharing basis between Centre and State for material component. Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme (MGNREGS) is being implemented in all the districts of Haryana State since 2008-09. The basic objective of the scheme is to enhance livelihood security in rural areas by providing atleast 100 days of guaranteed wage employment in a financial year to every rural household whose adult members volunteer to do unskilled manual work. The scheme is applicable only to rural areas. 1/3rd of the jobs are reserved for women. Rural household are to apply for registration with concerned Gram Panchayats. After registration, Job Cards are issued to the households by the Gram Panchayats. The payment of wages is being made on weekly or fortnightly basis. The contractors are banned under this programme. Under this scheme, the Ministry has provided a detailed list of 266 kinds of works/activities identified as permissible works, out of which 182 kinds of works relate to Natural Resource Management (NRM) alone, 85 are Water related and 164 of the total works are related to Agri and Agri-Allied works. Type/mode of Benefit- Wages of Rs. 400/- per day (DBT) w.e.f. from 1.04.2025 is given with 150 days employment guarantee in a financial year as fixed by the Centre Government. The outlay has been kept for the year 2026-27and this provision is required for the pending liabilities of MGNREGA. The Parliament has passed the historic Viksit Bharat – Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin): VB-G RAM G Act, 2025. This Act is aligned with the national vision of Viksit Bharat @ 2047 and replaces the existing Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA)

entries.purpose: Centre Share: `60,00,00,000/- State Share : `40,00,00,000/- The Parliament has passed the historic Viksit Bharat - Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin): VB-G RAM G Act, 2025. This Act is aligned with the national vision of Viksit Bharat@2047 and replaces the existing Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA). Need for the VB-G Ram G Act,2025: This new legislation represents a major reform of the Mahatma Gandhi NREGA, aligning rural employment with the long-term vision of Viksit Bharat 2047 by addressing structural deficiencies while enhancing employment, transparency, and accountability. Features: 1. 125 Days of Guaranteed Employment: Through this scheme, every rural household whose adult members are willing to do unskilled manual labour will be provided with 125 days of guaranteed employment in each financial year, so that a prosperous and strong rural India can be built by promoting empowerment, development, convergence, and completeness in rural India. 2. 60-Day Break During the Agricultural Season: According to the scheme, to ensure the availability of laborers during the sowing and harvesting seasons, work under the scheme will be suspended for a total of 60 days, ensuring that laborers have stable employment while also participating in agricultural activities. For this, state governments will have to make an advance announcement of the period of up to 60 days in the financial year. Laborers will continue to receive 125 days of guaranteed employment during the remaining 305 days, benefiting both farmers and laborers. 3. Fund Sharing: This will be operated as a Centrally Sponsored Scheme, under which: a. The fund sharing ratio between the Central Government and State Governments will be 60:40 for all states (this ratio is 90:10 for North-Eastern and Himalayan states). b. The State and Central Governments will share wages, material costs, and administrative costs in the same ratio. c. Provision for unemployment allowance. 4. Framework of Works: Employment generation is linked to infrastructure development through four thematic areas of work: a. Water Security through Water-Related Works: Water conservation structures, irrigation support, groundwater recharge, rejuvenation of water bodies, watershed area development, and afforestation – these water-related works will strengthen water security in rural areas. b. Core Rural Infrastructure Works: Essential civic, social, and service delivery assets such as rural roads, public buildings, school infrastructure, sanitation

entries.purpose: Name of scheme Scheme for Development of Minority under Pradhan Mantri Jan Vikas Karyakaram (PMJVK) Centre Share: `36,00,00,000/- State Share : `24,00,00,000/- This is a Centrally Sponsored scheme on (60:40) sharing basis between Centre and State. The Ministry of Home Affairs, the Government of India has started Multi- Sectoral Development Programme in the year 2008-09 and this scheme was restructured as “Pradhan Mantri Jan Vikas Karyakram (PMJVK)” w.e.f. 01.04.2018 to address the development deficits of the identified Minority Concentration Areas. The areas for implementation of PMJVK has been identified on the basis of substantial population of minority communities i.e. 25% of minority population in the area and backwardness parameters in the area concerned which are below the national average on the basis of the Census-2011. Under this scheme, infrastructure will be created to improve the quality of life of people and to reduce the imbalances in the identified minority concentration areas to be at par with the rest of the country. 80% of the resources would be utilized for projects relating to education, health and skill development, out of which at least range to 33-40% will be earmarked for creation of assets/facilities for women/girls. entries.name: Headquarters staff Land Records Agricultural Census
entries.purpose: Name of Scheme Headquarters Staff Land Records Agricultural Census. The Government of India has been conducting quinquennial Agriculture Census since 1970-71. Ten Census have been conducted in the country. First Agricultural Census was conducted with 1970-71 as the reference year. The subsequent census were conducted with 1976-77, 1980-81, 1985-86, 1990-91, 1995-96, 2000-01 and 2005-06, 2010-2011 &2015-16 as the reference year. 11th Agricultural Census with reference year 2021-2022 is being taken up, under this scheme the work of Phase-I work has been completed. The Training workshop cum phase-II has been provided to all DC’s with guidelines from Government of India Ministry of New Delhi. Aims and Objectives of the Scheme:- Its main objectives are to provide data on number and area of operational holdings, their tenancy particulars, land utilization, irrigation status, and source- wise area irrigated number of wells and tube wells, area under crops according to irrigated and un-irrigated conditions and dispersal of operated area. The data collected under this scheme is very important and useful for administrators, planner and research scholars. The data is collected in respect of land holders’ size class wise, social status wise and sex wise which are widely used for agriculture and development planning purpose.

entries.name: National Land Records Modernization Programme- Computerization of Land Records
entries.name_in_the_narrative: National Land Records Modernization Programme- Computerization of Land Records.
entries.purpose: It is a 100% Centrally Sponsored scheme. The Government of India implemented the Centrally Sponsored Scheme in the shape of the National Land Records Modernization Programme (NLRMP) by merging two existing centrally sponsored Schemes of Computerization of Land Records and Strengthening of Revenue Administration and Updating of Land Records in the Department of Land Resources, Ministry of Rural Development. The integrated programme would modernize management of land records, minimize scope of land dispute, enhance transparency in the land records maintenance system, and to facilitate moving eventually towards guaranteed conclusive titles to immovable properties in the country. This scheme is being implemented from the year 2010. NLRMP Scheme was launched by the Government of India in the State of the Haryana for achieving the targets of Modernisation of Revenue Record Rooms, Computerization of Land Records, Computerization of Registration and Survey/ Resurvey work etc. The work related to Modern Record Rooms, Computerization of Land Records and Computerization of Registration was completed but the work related to Survey / Resurvey could not be completed and is pending due to litigation, and the matter is subjudice in Hon’ble High Court of Punjab and Haryana, Chandigarh. The main objectives of the scheme are:- a) Data entry of legacy encumbrance data b) Scanning & preservation of old documents c) Data entry of valuation details d) Computerization of registration work e) Computerization of SROs. f) Connectivity of SROs with Revenue Offices The above scheme is based on following basic principles: • A single window to handle land records (including the maintenance and updating of textual records, maps). • Timely issuance of copies of land records in the shortest possible time to those who need it. • Transparency in matters of registration of documents, sanction of mutations and aspects of public dealings. • Creation of land records information system, which automatically updates revenue record by bringing all the revenue entries on-line. • Creation of land information system and database for effective reforms, revenue administration and development at grass root level.
