entries.purpose: Census 2027 is going to be first digital Census in the history of the country. The Census 2027 will be conducted in two phases: 1. House listing and Housing Census 2. Population Enumeration. The first phase of Census 2027 i.e. House listing and Housing Census has been notified for conduct in Haryana from 1st May 2026 to 30th May 2026. And the option for Self-Enumeration will also be available from 16th April 2026 to 30th April 2026. This will be the 6 th Census since the formation of the State. The pre-test experience in Haryana where the mobile apps were tested in three districts namely Panchkula, Hisar and Faridabad has been encouraging with cent percent work completed in time through the apps. A Census Management and Monitoring System (CMMS) Portal has been developed for effective monitoring of the field operations. Census 2027 will be India’s first Census conducted using digital tools. Enumerators will collect data through secure digital applications, supported by digital maps and real time monitoring systems. Public will also have the option of Self Enumeration through an online portal. The calibrated adoption of technology is aimed at improving operational efficiency enhancing data quality and enabling faster availability of Census data. The successful conduct of Census 2027 depends on meticulous preparation, a well-trained field workforce and coordinated implementation across all administrative levels. A structured training architecture and phased operational planning are being adopted to ensure uniform understanding of procedures, adherence to timelines and high standards of data quality across States and Union Territories. The Union Cabinet has approved the Scheme for Conduct of Census of India 2027, with a total financial outlay of Rs. 11,718.24 crore. Similarly for Haryana it will be approx. Rs. 200 Crores. The approval covers all preparatory activities, digital infrastructure, training, field operations, data processing and dissemination for both phases of the Census. *****

entries.name: Special Assistance to State for Capital Investment-N A
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Special Assistance to State for Capital Investment
entries.purpose: It is a 100% Centrally Sponsored scheme. The Government of India implemented the Centrally Sponsored Scheme in the shape of Special Assistance to State for Capital Investment. The National Geospatial Knowledge-based Land Survey of Urban Habitations (NAKSHA) Programmeis an initiative launched by the Department of Land Resources (DoLR) under the Ministry of Rural Development, Government of India. It is a part of the Digital India Land Records Modernization Programme (DILRMP) and aims to modernize urban land records using advanced geospatial technologies. The programme focuses on creating accurate, digitized land ownership records for urban areas, particularly in smaller cities and towns, to enhance transparency, reduce disputes, and support urban planning. Benefits of the scheme:- • Improved Urban Planning and Development High-resolution digital maps enable precise land boundary identification and resource optimization. • Enhanced Transparency and Accessibility Public access to land records reduces fraud and disputes, building trust in governance. • Efficient Land Management A centralized digital database streamlines land administration and property transactions. • Support for Policy Making Geospatial data aids policies on land use, urban expansion, and environmental conservation. • Economic Advantages Reliable records boost investor confidence and reduce litigation costs. • Environmental Conservation Tracks urban sprawl and protects natural resources through better land use monitoring. • Citizen Benefits Simplifies access to land records, reducing bureaucratic delays. Implementation of NAKSHA in Haryana:- Haryana is part of the NAKSHA pilot phase, focusing on smaller ULBs in Haryana. It integrates with existing systems like the BhuNaksha portal and HARSAC’s geospatial expertise. The detail of selected ULBs for pilot phase is as under:- • Municipal Corporation, Manesar • Municipal Council, Narnaul • Municipal Corporation, Panchkula Steps to be taken for implementation of the programme are as under:- • Drone-Based Surveys: Captures aerial imagery for accurate mapping. • Web-GIS Platform: Integrates survey data for public access. • Transparency and Dispute Resolution: Enhances Haryana’s BhuNaksha system. *******

entries.purpose: Scheme Name: National Livestock Mission-Training & Assistance for Quality Fodder Seed Production(100%) and Code No. 3-10-2403-51-789-82-51- Scheme Name: National Livestock Mission-Training & Assistance for Quality Fodder for Scheduled Castes (SCSP) (100%) Outlay: ₹2,50,00,000/- The National Livestock Mission (NLM) provides focused support for strengthening fodder resources through “Training & Assistance for Quality Fodder Seed Production (100%)” under the Sub-Mission on Feed and Fodder Development. In Haryana, this scheme component is being implemented to establish an effective fodder seed production chain comprising breeder, foundation and certified seed. The scheme provides 100% central assistance for incentivizing quality fodder seed production by eligible agencies such as ICAR institute. National Seed Corporation, State Agricultural Universities, State Seed Corporations, Dairy Cooperatives and other credible organizations. Financial assistance is provided on a per kilogram basis for different categories of seeds, thereby encouraging multiplication of high-yielding and improved fodder varieties. The first installment is released after approval of a viable proposal, while the second installment is provided after production and self-certification of seed by the concerned agency. Where farmers are engaged in seed production, 75% of the subsidy is passed on to farmers and 25% retained by the producing agency towards operational and certification costs. The programme also emphasizes capacity building of field functionaries and livestock owners through training, awareness and technical guidance in forage production, conservation and utilization. By ensuring timely availability of certified quality fodder seed, the initiative aims to enhance green fodder production, reduce feed deficit, and support sustainable livestock development in Haryana. *****

entries.name: Scheme for care and support to victims under section 4&6 of the protection of children from sexual offences POCSO Act, 2012
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Scheme for care and support to victims under section 4&6 of the protection of children from sexual offences POCSO Act, 2012
entries.purpose: The objective of this scheme is to provide integrated support and assistance to minor pregnant girl child victims under one roof and to facilitate their immediate, emergency and non emergency access to a range of services for long term rehabilitation in terms of access to education, police assistance, medical (also comprising maternity, neo-natal and infant care), psychological, mental health counselling, legal support, Non-Institutional care support, place of stay in Child Care Institutions (CCIs)/Aftercare facilities and health insurance cover for the girl child victim and her new-born to enable access to justice and empowerment of such girl child victims. Eligibility criteria: Any girl below the age of 18 years, who is a victim of :- 1. Penetrative Sexual Assault – Section 4 of the POCSO Act; 2. Aggravated Penetrative Sexual Assault – Section 6 of the POSCO Act; and, 3. Section 376, 376A-E of Indian Penal Code, 1860 (IPC). and, who becomes pregnant due to such assault or rape is covered under the scheme. Under the scheme,a sum of `10.00 lakh per district shall be allocated to the State/UT from the Nirbhaya Fund of Ministry of Women & Child Development, Govt. of India, and the state may utilize the fund flexibly as per actual incidence and need of districts. At district level District Child Protection Unit (DCPU) shall utilize this fund under the overall control of District Magistrate/District Collector.

The Child helpline shall run in coordination with State and District functionaries and it will be integrated with the Emergency Response Support System (ERSS-112) helpline of MHA (Ministry of Home Affairs). The Child Helpline control rooms are set up at Headquarters and also in all districts, to address cases of children in distress.

entries.purpose: Launched by the Hon’ble Prime Minister on January 22, 2015, from Panipat, Haryana, the Beti Bachao Beti Padhao (BBBP) program is the Government of India’s flagship initiative aimed at addressing gender imbalance, empowering girls, and driving societal transformation. The Government of Haryana has played a pivotal role in successfully implementing this program, making remarkable strides in improving the status of girls across the state.

entries.name: Universalization of Women Helpline
entries.name_in_the_narrative: Universalization of Women Helpline
entries.purpose: This scheme intends to provide 24 hours immediate and emergency response to women affected by violence through referral (linking with appropriate authority such as police, One Stop Centre, hospital) and by providing information about women related Government programs across the country through a single uniform number. Women Helpline (WHL) is integrated with One Stop Centre Scheme (OSC) as one OSC shall be established in every State/UT to provide integrated support and assistance to women affected by violence, both in private and public spaces under one roof. Women Helpline is also integrated with ERSS 112 service and Child Helpline 1098. The daily and weekly feedback is taken by the staff of Women Helpline for making further improvement in the service. The objectives of the Scheme are: 1. To provide toll-free 24-hours telecom service to women affected by violence seeking support and information. 2. To facilitate crisis and non-crisis intervention through referral to the appropriate agencies such as Police/Hospitals/Ambulance services/District Legal Service Authority (DLSA)/Protection Officer (PO)/OSC. 3. To provide information about the appropriate support services, Government schemes and programmes available to the women affected by violence, in her particular situation within the local area in which she resides or is employed.

Working women, who may be single, widow, divorced, separated, married or whose husband or immediate family does not reside in the same city as well as women who are under training for more than 1 year are eligible. Out of 20 Working Women Hostels in the State, 7 are functional at Rohtak (2), Hisar, Panchkula, Kurukshetra, Gurugram and Faridabad and 323 women’s are residing in these Working Women Hostels, at present. Under this scheme, Ministry of Finance provides 50 year interest free loan for construction of Working Women Hostel. GOI has sanctioned funds for construction of Working Women Hostel in Gurugram and Faridabad.

entries.name: National Action Plan for Drug de-addiction and Rehabilitation
entries.name_in_the_narrative: National Action Plan for Drug De-addiction and Rehabilitation.
entries.purpose: The Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, Government of India is the Nodal Ministry for drug demand reduction and has formulated a National Action Plan for Drug Demand Reduction (NAPDDR) which aims at reduction of adverse consequences of drug abuse through a multipronged strategy involving education de-addiction and rehabilitation of affected individuals and their families. OBJECTIVE & SCOPE- a) To Focus on preventive education, awareness generation, identification, counseling treatment and rehabilitation of individuals with substance dependence, training and capacity building of the service providers through collaborative efforts of the Central and State Governments and Non-Governments Organizations. b) To create awareness and educate people about the ill-efforts of substance dependence on the individual, family, workplace and the society at large. c) To reduce stigmatization in order to integrate them back into the society. d) To Develop human resource and build capacity to, i. Provide for a whole range of community based services for identification, motivation, counseling, de-addiction treatment, after care and rehabilitation for Whole Person Recovery (WPR) of dependents. ii. Formulate and implement comprehensive guidelines, schemes, and programmes using a multi-agency approach for drug demand reduction. iii. Undertake drug demand reduction efforts to address all forms of illicit use of any substances.

entries.name: National Action Plan for Senior Citizens
entries.name_in_the_narrative: National Action Plan for Senior Citizens
entries.purpose: The National Action Plan for Senior Citizens (NAPSrC) highlights all facts which are required to create an eco-system where all Indians can age gracefully and live a life of dignity. The NAPSrC includes ten components encompassing the needs of senior citizens. These are :- i) Financial Security ii) Health Care and Nutrition iii) Shelter and Welfare iv) Protection of life and property of Senior Citizens v) Active and Productive Ageing with Intergenerational Bonding and Skill development vi) Accessibility, transport and Age friendly environment vii) Awareness Generation and Capacity Building viii) Promoting Silver Economy : senior friendly industrial goods services in the society ix) Research and Study x) Project Management Further, the Government of India has requested that each State/UT may strategize & frame their own State Action Plan for the Welfare of Senior Citizens (SAPSrC)by taking into account their local consideration and that State Action Plan may comprise a long term strategy as well as annual action plan. The Funds are being allocated to each State/UT for enabling implementation of the SAPSrC for the duration of NAPSrC, to ensure sustained implementation of the State Action Plan. As the number of senior citizens increased from 10.3 crore in 2011 to an estimated 17.3 crore in 2026, the need for setting up Senior Citizens Homes for elderly, specially for the elderly women and indigents becomes crucial. This requirement is acute in both rural and urban areas with a large number of elderly population living below the poverty line where vulnerability of elderly people against crimes and alienation from their families is increasing. The MWPSC Act, 2007 provides for setting up of at least one such Senior Citizens Home by the State/UT Governments in each district of the State/UT for at least 150 indigent persons. Also, as people are living longer post their retirement, the challenge is to find ways to remain actively engaged and productive, with dignity and involving all the following stakeholders of elderly sector :- 1. Elderly themselves (Rural/ Urban, all ages Male and Females, Bedridden persons). 2. Their informal caregivers/ Families (unpaid care givers) in the community.

entries.name_in_the_narrative: Social Audit Unit (MGNREGA)-Normal
entries.purpose: As per Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme (MGNREGS) Guidelines, social audit of the works taken up under the Scheme shall be conducted in each year for better transparency and accountability in the Scheme. Therefore, Social Audit Unit has been established. For implementation of the SAU, manpower has been engaged at State, District, Block and Village level to conduct the Social Audit of each work taken under the Scheme. The Ministry of Rural Development, Govt. of India is providing 100% funds for making the payment of Salary, Honorarium of Village Resource Person and other office expenses. Note:- This scheme will be replaced by Viksit Bharat – Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin): VB-G RAM G & this component will also be applicable for implementation of VB-G RAM G.

entries.purpose: The Project UNNATI has been launched by the Ministry of Rural Development, Govt. of India to improve the livelihoods of most needy Mahatma Gandhi NREGA workers by providing a skill either for self-employment or wage employment. This project was meant for providing training for one adult member (of age 18-45 year) of a household who has completed 100 days of work under Mahatma Gandhi NREGA in the previous financial year from the year of commencement of the project. Under this project, stipend (against wage lost compensation) has to be paid to the trainees. Note:- This scheme will be replaced by Viksit Bharat – Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin): VB-G RAM G & this component will also be applicable for implementation of VB-G RAM G.

entries.name: Untied Grants to Gram Panchayats on the recommendations of the Central Finance Commission
entries.purpose: Name o f the Scheme Untied Grants to Gram Panchayats on the recommendation of the Central Finance Commission This is a Central Grant-in-Aid scheme to Gram Panchayats on the recommendations of the Central Finance Commission. The funds provided by Central Finance Commission to Gram Panchayats/Panchayat Samiti/Zila Parishad in the ratio of 75:15:10 on the basis of weightage to population @80% and to the geographical area @20%. Untied grant can be used by the concerned PRI for location-specific needs except for salary or other establishment expenditure. The Tied Grant can be used for the basic services of (a) sanitation and maintenance of open-defecation free (ODF) status and (b) supply of drinking water, rain water harvesting and water recycling.

entries.purpose: This is a Central Grant-in-Aid scheme to Gram Panchayats on the recommendations of the Central Finance Commission. The funds are provided by the Central Finance Commission to the Panchayats/Panchayat Samities/Zila Parishads in the ratio of 75:15:10. Central Finance Commission is providing the grants in the shape of basic grants (Untied Grant) and Tied Grants in ratio of 60:40. In addition to this, the provision Health Sector Grant has also been made under the Central Finance Commission. The aim of Health Sector Grant is to strengthen the health infrastructure/health facilities in the rural areas. In past practice these grants were been disbursed by the Health Department to the PRIs. But now, it has been decided funds under the health sector grant shall also be disbursed by the Panchayat Department. *****

entries.purpose: AMRUT II aims to provide water supply through functional taps to all households in statutory towns and coverage of sewerage/ septage management. Administrative & Other Expenses will be fully funded by the Centre and shall be utilized to cover the cost of preparing CWBPs, Program Management Units (PMUs), Detailed project Reports (DPRs), Project Implementation Units (PIUs), Project Development and Management Consultants (PDMCs), development of Aquifer Management Plans and Independent Review and Monitoring Agencies (IRMAs), Capacity Building etc.. Various activities like AMRUT MITRA, Tree Plantation -Ek Ped Ma Ke Naam, IEC activities are being performed under this Head. MoHUA has sanctioned 41 projects for various activities such as water sample collection household survey, identification of leakage and in sanitary connection and OT testing in 29 towns. 53 Projects for tree Plantation “Ek Ped Ma Ke Naam” under AMRUT MITRA in various towns.

entries.name: National Action for Mechanized Sanitation Ecosystem (NAMASTE) Scheme (100:0)-N A
entries.name_in_the_narrative: National Action for Mechanize Sanitation Ecosystem (NAMASTE) Scheme (100:0)
entries.purpose: A scheme namely "National Action for Mechanised Sanitation Ecosystem" (NAMASTE), a joint effort of the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment (MoSJE) and Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA) for ensuring zero death in hazardous cleaning of sewer and septic tanks has been finalised / launched from 01.04.2023 to 31.03.2026. The intended outcomes as provisioned in the guideline vide Para 3.2 reproduced as under: - a) Zero fatalities in sanitation work in India b) All sanitation work is performed by formalized skilled workers c) No sanitation worker come in direct contact with human faecal matter d) Strengthening and capacitating SRU to ensure safe delivery of mechanized sanitation services e) Sanitation workers are collectivized into SHGs and are empowered to run sanitation enterprises. f) Sewer and Septic tank sanitation workers (SSWs) and their dependents also have access to livelihoods by providing capital subsidy for purchase of sanitation related equipments.

myscheme_join_defects.defect: A SCHEME BRAND SHARED BY MANY myScheme SUB-SCHEMES AND ONE BUDGET LINE. myScheme lists eighteen PMMSY components for Haryana, each named 'PMMSY: <component>'; the Plan Memo states the whole programme once. Every one of the eighteen matches on the written acronym, so one budget row absorbs eighteen records
myscheme_join_defects.example_budget: Development of Fresh Water Aquaculture Renamed as Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana
myscheme_join_defects.example_myscheme: PMMSY: Construction of New Grow Out Ponds - Haryana
myscheme_join_defects.note: not wrong in direction, since every one of them IS funded from that line, and useless for attribution, because the money cannot be split eighteen ways by anything in either document.

myscheme_join_defects.defect: a FUNDING CHANNEL read as a scheme. NSKFDC is the National Safai Karamcharis Finance and Development Corporation, which lends to five different myScheme schemes; the budget names it once

myscheme_join_defects.example_myscheme: Mahila Samridhi Yojana under NSKFDC- Haryana

myscheme_join_defects.defect: A COMMUNITY BUDGET CUT READ AS AN ACRONYM. SCSP is the Scheduled Caste Sub Plan, a cut of a budget and never a scheme. Haryana writes it in capitals at the end of a row name, so it is a WRITTEN acronym; the myScheme side DERIVES an initialism from a long name and that initialism contains it
myscheme_join_defects.example_budget: National Livestock Mission Breed Development of Livestock & Poultry SCSP
myscheme_join_defects.example_myscheme: Consolidated Stipend Scheme for Scheduled Caste Students Pursuing Higher Education
myscheme_join_defects.note: NOT_ACRONYMS already holds sc, st, obc and vjnt because a community is who a scheme is for and never which scheme it is. scsp and tsp are the same axis written as a plan name and are not on the list. Four joins here, two from csscsphe and two from fbscsphe.

myscheme_join_defects.defect: a DERIVED initialism equal to another DERIVED initialism, on two names that differ in one word. Disabled and Destitute are different children
a NATIONAL HONOUR read as a coined acronym. Padma is the award; PADMA is Haryana's Programme to Accelerate Development for MSME Advancement

myscheme_join_defects.example_myscheme: Haryana Gaurav Samman Scheme for Padma Awardees

myscheme_join_defects.reason_string: all 2 content words of the shorter name are present

myscheme_join_defects.defect: containment on a parent brand. Mukhyamantri Vivah Shagun Yojana is the general marriage grant and Mukhyamantri Samajik Samrasta Antarjatiya Vivah Shagun Yojana is the inter-caste one; the budget states both and the shorter absorbed the longer
myscheme_join_defects.example_myscheme: Mukhyamantri Samajik Samrasta Antarjatiya Vivah Shagun Yojana

myscheme_join_defects.reason_string: all 3 content words of the shorter name are present

myscheme_join_summary.how: indexed on match.tokens, match.skeleton and match.acronyms, then match.probably_same on every candidate pair, then every join read by eye
myscheme_join_summary.read_this_carefully: This is the state the whole exercise was picked to test. myScheme claims 249 Haryana schemes against DBT Bharat's 171, one of only three states where the portal claims more than DBT counts, so the question was whether the portal is ahead of the state's own books. It is not. The Plan Memo names 970 schemes with codes and 824 with a paragraph of purpose, and a generous matcher finds only 53 of myScheme's 249 in it. Read the 32 wrong joins before reading anything into that 53: 18 of them are a single budget line for PMMSY matched to eighteen myScheme records that are components of it, which says myScheme's Haryana count is partly made of sub-schemes a budget states once.

part_totals.what: every printed Total Part-I, Total Part-II and Total Part-III against the scheme rows read under it, in all five money columns

row_arithmetic.what: Total = Central Share + State Share on every scheme row

units.what: each department's Summary of Budget Estimate total, printed in full rupees, against the same total from the scheme table in lakh multiplied by 100,000. This is the check that would catch a unit read wrongly anywhere in the book

source: Haryana Budget 2026-27, Explanatory Memorandum on Welfare & Development Schemes (Plan Memo)
unit_note: be_lakh, central_share_lakh, state_share_lakh, establishment_lakh and works_lakh are rupees in LAKH, read from the `(₹ In Lakhs)` header the scheme tables print and never assumed: this book also prints full rupees to eleven digits in its per-department Summary and again on every narrative `Outlay` line, and one page prints the words LIST OF SCHEMES over a table in rupees. outlay_rupees is that narrative figure and is left in RUPEES on purpose, so the two can be compared without a conversion hiding a mistake. The scale is checked, not asserted: each department's Summary total in rupees is compared with its scheme table's total in lakh times 100,000.
variant_note: Haryana publishes one Plan Memo per cycle with no original/revised split, so there is no variant to choose. Two of its 96 scheme-table pages are headed LISTOFSCHEMESBUDGETESTIMATE2025-26, spaces and all missing, for Community Development & Panchayats. Those figures are 2026-27: that department's table totals equal its own 2026-27 rupee Summary to the rupee, which is the units check. The stale heading is recorded in banners_read.
